qs.q: The polynomial \(kx^3 + mx^2 - 11x + 6\) is divisible by \(x - 2\). When it is divided by \(x + 3\), the remainder is \(-60\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Since the polynomial is divisible by \(x - 2\), synthetic division gives \(8k + 4m - 16 = 0\) (\(2k + m = 4\)), while division by \(x + 3\) gives \(-27k + 9m + 39 = -60\) (\(-3k + m = -11\)). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(5k = 15\), so \(k = 3\) and \(m = 4 - 2(3) = -2\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + kx^3 - mx - 18\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 3\) and \(x + 2\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(x - 3\) gives \(9k - m = -21\), and division by \(x + 2\) gives \(-4k + m = 1\). Adding these yields \(5k = -20\) so \(k = -4\), which gives \(m = 9(-4) + 21 = -15\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + ax^3 - bx + 12\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(a\).
qs.s: Setting the remainder from synthetic division by \(x - 1\) to zero gives \(a - b + 13 = 0\), and by \(x + 2\) gives \(-4a + b + 14 = 0\). Adding these two equations yields \(-3a + 27 = 0\), so \(a = 9\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + kx^2 + mx - 12\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Using a \(0\) placeholder for the \(x^3\) term, synthetic division by \(x - 2\) yields \(2k + m = -2\), and division by \(x + 3\) yields \(3k - m = -23\). Adding the equations gives \(5k = -25\), so \(k = -5\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + mx^3 + kx + 8\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 1\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(x - 2\) gives the remainder condition \(4m + k = -12\), and division by \(x + 1\) gives \(m + k = 9\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(3m = -21\), so \(m = -7\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + kx^3 - mx - 10\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(x - 1\) gives \(k - m = 9\), and by \(x + 2\) gives \(-4k + m = -3\). Adding the equations yields \(-3k = 6\) so \(k = -2\), giving \(m = -2 - 9 = -11\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 12\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(16\). When divided by \(x + 3\), the remainder is \(6\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(x - 2\) gives \(2k + m = 2\), and by \(x + 3\) gives \(3k - m = -57\). Adding these two equations gives \(5k = -55\), so \(k = -11\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 - 2x^2 + bx - 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(15\). When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-9\). Find the value of \(a - b\).
qs.s: Synthetic division with remainder \(15\) at \(x = 2\) gives \(4a + b = 6\), and with remainder \(-9\) at \(x = -1\) gives \(a + b = 3\). Solving the system yields \(a = 1\) and \(b = 2\), so \(a - b = -1\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(2x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 - 5x - 3\) has no remainder when divided by both \(2x + 1\) and \(x - 3\). Find the value of \(b\).
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(x + \frac{1}{2}\) gives \(-a + 2b = 3\), and division by \(x - 3\) gives \(3a + b = -16\). Solving the linear system gives \(a = -5\) and \(b = -1\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(2x^4 + kx^3 - 3x^2 + mx - 2\) has no remainder when divided by \(2x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - \frac{1}{2}\) gives the remainder condition \(k + 4m = 21\), and dividing by \(x + 2\) gives \(4k + m = 9\). Solving this system yields \(k = 1\) and \(m = 5\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^5 + ax^3 + bx^2 - 4x + 12\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Use synthetic division to find the value of \(a\).
qs.s: Using a \(0\) placeholder for the \(x^4\) term, synthetic division by \(x - 1\) yields \(a + b = -9\), and division by \(x + 2\) yields \(-2a + b = 3\). Subtracting the equations gives \(3a = -12\), so \(a = -4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 - kx^3 + 2x - 5\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + kx + 5\) is divided by \(x - 3\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division of \(P(x)\) by \(x - 1\) produces remainder \(-k - 2\), and synthetic division of \(Q(x)\) by \(x - 3\) gives remainder \(3k + 14\). Equating the two gives \(-k - 2 = 3k + 14\), which solves to \(k = -4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 4x - 4\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^3 - x^2 + kx + 9\) is divided by \(x + 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division of \(P(x)\) by \(x - 2\) gives remainder \(4k - 4\), and synthetic division of \(Q(x)\) by \(x + 1\) gives remainder \(6 - k\). Equating the remainders gives \(4k - 4 = 6 - k\), which solves to \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - kx^2 + 5\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 + 2kx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Using synthetic division, the remainder of \(P(x)\) divided by \(x - 1\) is \(7 - k\), and the remainder of \(Q(x)\) divided by \(x - 2\) is \(4k + 2\). Setting \(7 - k = 4k + 2\) yields \(5k = 5\), so \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 - 2x^3 + kx + 3\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 1\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By synthetic division, dividing \(P(x)\) by \(x - 2\) gives remainder \(2k + 3\), and dividing \(Q(x)\) by \(x - 1\) gives remainder \(k - 2\). Setting \(2k + 3 = k - 2\) results in \(k = -5\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 3x^3 + kx^2 - 2x + 4\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^4 - 3x^2 + kx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division of \(P(x)\) by \(x + 2\) yields a remainder of \(4k - 16\), while dividing \(Q(x)\) by \(x - 2\) yields \(2k - 2\). Setting \(4k - 16 = 2k - 2\) gives \(2k = 14\), so \(k = 7\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 16x^4 - 8x^2 + kx + 5\) is divided by \(2x + 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 5x - 12\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division of \(P(x)\) using divisor root \(-\frac{1}{2}\) gives remainder \(4 - \frac{1}{2}k\), and division of \(Q(x)\) by \(x - 2\) gives remainder \(4k - 14\). Setting \(4 - \frac{1}{2}k = 4k - 14\) yields \(\frac{9}{2}k = 18\), so \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 4x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 3\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 7x - 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Using synthetic division with \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), the remainder of \(P(x)\) divided by \(2x - 1\) is \(\frac{1}{4}k + \frac{1}{2}\), while the remainder of \(Q(x)\) divided by \(x - 2\) is \(4k - 7\). Equating \(\frac{1}{4}k + \frac{1}{2} = 4k - 7\) gives \(\frac{15}{4}k = \frac{15}{2}\), so \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 2kx^2 + 5x - 8\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 3x^3 - kx^2 + 4kx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division of \(P(x)\) by \(x + 2\) yields a remainder of \(-16k - 2\), and synthetic division of \(Q(x)\) by \(x - 2\) yields \(4k + 18\). Solving \(-16k - 2 = 4k + 18\) gives \(-20k = 20\), so \(k = -1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^5 - kx^4 + 3x^3 - 4x + 7\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^4 + 4x^3 + kx^2 - 15x - 20\) is divided by \(x + 3\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Synthetic division of \(P(x)\) by \(x - 1\) gives remainder \(8 - k\), and synthetic division of \(Q(x)\) by \(x + 3\) gives remainder \(9k - 2\). Equating \(8 - k = 9k - 2\) yields \(10k = 10\), so \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^5 - 2x^4 + kx^2 - 18\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^4 - kx^3 + 5x - 13\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Using synthetic division with zero placeholders for missing powers, dividing \(P(x)\) by \(x - 3\) leaves a remainder of \(9k + 63\), and dividing \(Q(x)\) by \(x - 2\) leaves \(29 - 8k\). Setting \(9k + 63 = 29 - 8k\) yields \(17k = -34\), so \(k = -2\).

exercises.name: Evaluating polynomials using the Remainder Theorem

qs.s: By synthetic division with \(k = \frac{3}{2}\), the quotient coefficients are \(2, -2, -4, 2\) and the remainder is \(-12 + 2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -9\), so \(P\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -9\).
Substituting \(x = 3\), the first two terms cancel since \(4(3^5) - 12(3^4) = 972 - 972 = 0\), leaving \(7(27) - 15(3) + 25 = 189 - 45 + 25 = 169\).
Evaluating at \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\), we have \(P\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{9} - \frac{2}{9} - \frac{8}{9} - 1 + 7 = -1 - 1 + 7 = 5\).

Using synthetic division or direct substitution, \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 6\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) - 7\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) + 8\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) - 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + 3 = -\frac{1}{2} + 3 = \frac{5}{2}\).
Dividing \(P(x)\) by \(x + 2\) using synthetic division yields quotient coefficients \(2, 1, -5, 11, -36\) and a remainder of \(64\), so \(P(-2) = 64\).

Evaluating \((1 + \sqrt{2})^3 = 7 + 5\sqrt{2}\) and \((1 + \sqrt{2})^2 = 3 + 2\sqrt{2}\), direct substitution yields \(P(1 + \sqrt{2}) = (7 + 5\sqrt{2}) - 3(3 + 2\sqrt{2}) - (1 + \sqrt{2}) + 5 = 2 - 2\sqrt{2}\).
Dividing \(P(x)\) by the minimal polynomial \(x^2 - 2x - 1\) gives \(P(x) = (x^2 - 2x + 2)(x^2 - 2x - 1) + 5\); since \((1+\sqrt{2})^2 - 2(1+\sqrt{2}) - 1 = 0\), \(P(1 + \sqrt{2}) = 5\).
Substitute \(x = a\) into \(P(x)\) to obtain \(P(a) = a^4 - 4a^3(a) + 3a^4 = a^4 - 4a^4 + 3a^4 = 0\).
Substitute \(x = a\) into \(P(x)\) to obtain \(P(a) = a^3 - 3a^2(a) + 5a^3 = (1 - 3 + 5)a^3 = 3a^3\).

exercises.name: Finding unknown coefficients using the Remainder or Factor Theorem

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + 4x^2 + kx - 10\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(-3\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 1^3 + 4(1)^2 + k(1) - 10 = k - 5\). Setting \(k - 5 = -3\) gives \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + kx - 7\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-2\). Find the value of \(k\).
When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 4x + 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(5\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2(2)^3 + k(2)^2 - 4(2) + 1 = 4k + 9\). Setting \(4k + 9 = 5\) gives \(4k = -4\), so \(k = -1\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + kx + 5\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(8\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 3^3 - 3(3)^2 + 3k + 5 = 3k + 5\). Setting \(3k + 5 = 8\) gives \(3k = 3\), so \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 3x^3 + kx - 11\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(7\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 3(2)^3 + 2k - 11 = 2k + 13\). Setting \(2k + 13 = 7\) yields \(2k = -6\), so \(k = -3\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(0\), and when it is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-12\). Find the value of \(a\).
qs.s: Applying the Remainder Theorem gives \(P(1) = a + b - 2 = 0\) and \(P(-1) = a - b - 6 = -12\). Adding \(a + b = 2\) and \(a - b = -6\) yields \(2a = -4\), so \(a = -2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - 3x^3 + kx^2 - 8x - 12\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(18\). Find the value of \(k\).
When \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^2 - 5\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 - kx + 4\) is divided by \(x + 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k - 3\) and \(Q(-2) = 2k - 4\). Equating the two remainders gives \(k - 3 = 2k - 4\), which simplifies to \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 2\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(16\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 3\)?
The polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 6\) is divisible by both \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m - 5 = 0\) and \(P(-2) = 4k - 2m - 14 = 0\). Adding \(k + m = 5\) and \(2k - m = 7\) gives \(3k = 12\), so \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 - 3x^2 - kx + 8\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 1^3 - 3(1)^2 - k(1) + 8 = 6 - k\). Setting \(6 - k = 2\) gives \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 + 2x^2 + kx - 12\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(0\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(2) = 2^3 + 2(2)^2 + 2k - 12 = 2k + 4\). Setting \(2k + 4 = 0\) gives \(k = -2\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x + k\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(7\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 3^3 - 2(3)^2 + 3(3) + k = 18 + k\). Setting \(18 + k = 7\) gives \(k = -11\).

qs.q: When \(2x^3 + kx^2 - 7x - 6\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(0\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-2) = 2(-2)^3 + k(-2)^2 - 7(-2) - 6 = 4k - 8\). Setting \(4k - 8 = 0\) yields \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 + kx - 5\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-8\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-1) = (-1)^3 + k(-1) - 5 = -k - 6\). Setting \(-k - 6 = -8\) gives \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^5 - 3x^4 + 2x^3 - kx^2 + 4x - 15\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(6\). Find the value of \(k\).
When \(x^3 + kx^2 - 4x + 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(9\). What is the remainder when this polynomial is divided by \(x + 3\)?
qs.s: First, find \(k\) using \(P(2) = 2^3 + 4k - 8 + 1 = 4k + 1 = 9\), which gives \(k = 2\). Then, the remainder upon division by \(x + 3\) is \(P(-3) = (-3)^3 + 2(-3)^2 - 4(-3) + 1 = 4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^2 + 3\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is equal to the remainder when \(Q(x) = x^3 + kx - 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: The remainders are \(P(1) = 2 + k + 3 = k + 5\) and \(Q(2) = 8 + 2k - 1 = 2k + 7\). Setting \(k + 5 = 2k + 7\) gives \(k = -2\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = kx^3 + mx^2 + 2x - 4\) leaves a remainder of \(3\) when divided by \(x - 1\), and a remainder of \(-24\) when divided by \(x + 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Setting up the system from the remainders gives \(P(1) = k + m - 2 = 3 \implies k + m = 5\) and \(P(-2) = -8k + 4m - 8 = -24 \implies 2k - m = 4\). Adding the two equations yields \(3k = 9\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - 3x^3 + kx^2 + 5x - 2\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is \(1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 2\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) - 3\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) + k\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 5\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) - 2 = \frac{k+1}{4}\). Setting \(\frac{k+1}{4} = 1\) gives \(k = 3\).

qs.q: When \(3x^4 + kx^3 - 2x^2 + 5x - 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(8\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Using the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 3(1)^4 + k(1)^3 - 2(1)^2 + 5(1) - 4 = 8\), so \(k + 2 = 8\). Therefore, \(k = 6\).

qs.q: When \(x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 + 4x - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(10\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2^4 - 2(2)^3 + k(2^2) + 4(2) - 6 = 10\), which simplifies to \(4k + 2 = 10\). Solving for \(k\) gives \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 - 2x^2 + kx + 9\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(3\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-2) = (-2)^3 - 2(-2)^2 + k(-2) + 9 = 3\), which simplifies to \(-2k - 7 = 3\). Solving for \(k\) yields \(k = -5\).

qs.q: When \(2x^3 - kx^2 + 5x - 3\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(7\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2(2)^3 - k(2)^2 + 5(2) - 3 = 7\), which simplifies to \(23 - 4k = 7\). Solving for \(k\) gives \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When \(x^4 + kx^2 - 5x + 2\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(12\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2^4 + k(2^2) - 5(2) + 2 = 12\), which simplifies to \(4k + 8 = 12\). Solving for \(k\) gives \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(32\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(2) = 4k + 20 = 32\) gives \(k = 3\). Then, the remainder when divided by \(x + 1\) is \(P(-1) = 2(-1)^4 - (-1)^3 + 3(-1)^2 - 5(-1) + 6 = 17\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^2 + 3x - 1\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 + kx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + 4\) and \(Q(2) = 2k + 2\). Setting them equal gives \(k + 4 = 2k + 2\), which yields \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 4x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is \(5\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(1/2) = 4(1/2)^3 + k(1/2)^2 - 5(1/2) + 6 = 4 + k/4\). Setting \(4 + k/4 = 5\) gives \(k = 4\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 12\) is divisible by both \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\). Find the value of \(k + m\).
qs.s: Since \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\) are factors, \(P(2) = 4k + 2m - 4 = 0\) (\(2k + m = 2\)) and \(P(-3) = 9k - 3m - 39 = 0\) (\(3k - m = 13\)). Adding the equations gives \(5k = 15\), so \(k = 3\) and \(m = -4\), which gives \(k + m = -1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 + mx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(24\), and when divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-6\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m + 10 = 24\) (so \(4k + m = 7\)) and \(P(-1) = -k - m - 5 = -6\) (so \(k + m = 1\)). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(3k = 6\), so \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + kx - 5\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is 7. Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 3^3 - 3(3)^2 + 3k - 5 = 7\), which simplifies to \(3k - 5 = 7\). Adding 5 and dividing by 3 gives \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 2\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is 12. Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-2) = (-2)^3 + k(-2)^2 - 5(-2) + 2 = 12\), which simplifies to \(4k + 4 = 12\). Solving for \(k\) yields \(4k = 8\), so \(k = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 - 2x^3 + kx - 11\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is 31. Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 3^4 - 2(3^3) + k(3) - 11 = 31\), which simplifies to \(16 + 3k = 31\). Subtracting 16 gives \(3k = 15\), so \(k = 5\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 - 2kx + 7\) is divided by \(x + 3\), the remainder is -2. Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-3) = (-3)^3 - 2k(-3) + 7 = -2\), which simplifies to \(6k - 20 = -2\). Adding 20 gives \(6k = 18\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^3 - x^2 + kx - 9\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is 1. Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2(2)^3 - (2)^2 + k(2) - 9 = 1\), which simplifies to \(2k + 3 = 1\). Subtracting 3 gives \(2k = -2\), so \(k = -1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + kx + 3\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is 5. Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 2\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) - 5\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + \frac{k}{2} + 3 = 2 + \frac{k}{2}\). Setting \(2 + \frac{k}{2} = 5\) gives \(\frac{k}{2} = 3\), so \(k = 6\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 6\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and when divided by \(x + 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m - 5 = 0\) and \(P(-2) = 4k - 2m - 14 = 0\), giving the linear system \(k + m = 5\) and \(2k - m = 7\). Adding the two equations yields \(3k = 12\), so \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 4x + 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 - 3x + k\) is divided by \(x + 3\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 4k + 9\) and \(Q(-3) = k - 18\). Setting \(4k + 9 = k - 18\) leads to \(3k = -27\), so \(k = -9\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^3 + mx^2 - 3x + 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is 10. When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is 2. Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m + 1 = 10\) and \(P(-1) = -k + m + 7 = 2\), yielding \(k + m = 9\) and \(-k + m = -5\). Adding the two equations gives \(2m = 4\), so \(m = 2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is 16. What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(2) = 4k + 4 = 16\) gives \(k = 3\). Then, the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 3\) is \(P(-3) = (-3)^3 + 3(-3)^2 - 5(-3) + 6 = 21\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 - kx^2 + 4x + 6\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-18\). What is the remainder when it is divided by \(x - 3\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-2) = (-2)^3 - k(-2)^2 + 4(-2) + 6 = -4k - 10 = -18\), giving \(k = 2\). Evaluating at \(x = 3\) gives the remainder \(P(3) = 3^3 - 2(3^2) + 4(3) + 6 = 27\).

qs.q: When \(2x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 1\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(8\). What is the remainder when it is divided by \(x - 2\)?
qs.s: Applying the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-1) = 2(-1)^3 + k(-1)^2 - 5(-1) + 1 = k + 4 = 8\), giving \(k = 4\). Dividing by \(x - 2\) gives a remainder of \(P(2) = 2(2^3) + 4(2^2) - 5(2) + 1 = 23\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 + 4x^2 - kx - 10\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(-3\). What is the remainder when it is divided by \(x + 3\)?
qs.s: Using the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 1^3 + 4(1)^2 - k(1) - 10 = -k - 5 = -3\), yielding \(k = -2\). The remainder upon division by \(x + 3\) is \(P(-3) = (-3)^3 + 4(-3)^2 - (-2)(-3) - 10 = -7\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 + kx^2 + 3x - 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(21\). What is the remainder when it is divided by \(x + 1\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2^3 + k(2^2) + 3(2) - 5 = 4k + 9 = 21\), which gives \(k = 3\). The remainder when divided by \(x + 1\) is then \(P(-1) = (-1)^3 + 3(-1)^2 + 3(-1) - 5 = -6\).

qs.q: When \(x^3 - 2x^2 + kx + 4\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(7\). What is the remainder when it is divided by \(x + 2\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 3^3 - 2(3^2) + 3k + 4 = 3k + 13 = 7\), which solves to \(k = -2\). The remainder when divided by \(x + 2\) is \(P(-2) = (-2)^3 - 2(-2)^2 - 2(-2) + 4 = -8\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(0\), and when divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-10\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 3\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m - 3 = 0\) and \(P(-1) = k - m - 5 = -10\), which solve to \(k = -1\) and \(m = 4\). The remainder when divided by \(x - 3\) is \(P(3) = 3^3 - 3^2 + 4(3) - 4 = 26\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^5 - 3x^4 + kx^3 - 4x^2 + 2x - 8\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(-12\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 32 - 48 + 8k - 16 + 4 - 8 = 8k - 36 = -12\), which gives \(k = 3\). Evaluating at \(x = -1\) yields the remainder \(P(-1) = -1 - 3 - 3 - 4 - 2 - 8 = -21\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - 3x^3 + kx^2 + 5x - 1\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is \(3\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\)?

When \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 4x + 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is equal to the remainder when \(Q(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2kx + 9\) is divided by \(x - 1\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\)?
qs.s: We have \(P(2) = 4k + 9\) and \(Q(1) = 2k + 7\), and equating them gives \(4k + 9 = 2k + 7\), so \(k = -1\). Then the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\) is \(P(-2) = 2(-8) - (-2)^2 - 4(-2) + 1 = -11\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 2x^2 + mx - 12\) is divisible by both \(x - 2\) and \(x + 1\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(2) = 0\) and \(P(-1) = 0\) gives the linear system \(4k + m = 2\) and \(k + m = -13\), yielding \(k = 5\) and \(m = -18\). Thus, the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 3\) is \(P(3) = 3^4 + 5(3^3) - 2(3^2) - 18(3) - 12 = 132\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^3 + mx^2 - 3x + 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(4\). When it is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(8\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m + 1 = 4\) and \(P(-1) = -k + m + 7 = 8\). Solving the system \(k + m = 3\) and \(-k + m = 1\) yields \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx + 6\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(0\). When it is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(12\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m + 7 = 0\) and \(P(2) = 4k + 2m + 14 = 12\). Simplifying gives \(k + m = -7\) and \(2k + m = -1\), which subtract to give \(k = 6\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(7\). When it is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-11\). Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 4k + 2m + 11 = 7\) and \(P(-1) = k - m - 7 = -11\), which simplify to \(2k + m = -2\) and \(k - m = -4\). Solving this system gives \(k = -2\) and \(m = 2\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^3 - x^2 + mx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(0\). When it is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-40\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Using the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 27k + 3m - 15 = 0\) and \(P(-2) = -8k - 2m - 10 = -40\), which reduce to \(9k + m = 5\) and \(4k + m = 15\). Subtracting these equations gives \(5k = -10\), so \(k = -2\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 3x^3 + mx^2 + kx - 2\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(10\). When it is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-20\). Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Applying the Remainder Theorem gives \(P(1) = k + m + 1 = 10\) and \(P(-2) = -2k + 4m - 26 = -20\). Adding the simplified equations \(k + m = 9\) and \(-k + 2m = 3\) gives \(3m = 12\), so \(m = 4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2kx^3 + mx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is \(5\). When it is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-40\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1/2) = \frac{k+m}{4} + \frac{7}{2} = 5 \implies k + m = 6\), and \(P(-2) = -16k + 4m + 16 = -40 \implies -4k + m = -14\). Subtracting the equations yields \(5k = 20\), so \(k = 4\).

qs.q: Both \(x - 2\) and \(x + 1\) are factors of the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^4 - 3x^3 + mx^2 + 11x - 6\). Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(2) = 16k + 4m - 8 = 0\) and \(P(-1) = k + m - 14 = 0\), giving \(4k + m = 2\) and \(k + m = 14\). Subtracting the equations yields \(3k = -12\), so \(k = -4\) and \(m = 18\).

qs.q: When the degree-4 polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 2x^2 + mx - 8\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(16\). When it is divided by \(x + 3\), the remainder is also \(16\). Find the value of \(2k + m\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m = 16\) and \(P(-3) = 55 - 27k - 3m = 16\), which simplify to \(4k + m = 8\) and \(9k + m = 13\). Solving gives \(k = 1\) and \(m = 4\), so \(2k + m = 2(1) + 4 = 6\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^3 - 5x^2 + mx - 12\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(0\). When it is divided by \(x + 3\), the remainder is \(45\). Find the value of \(k - m\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m = 0 \implies 4k + m = 0\) and \(P(-3) = 105 - 27k - 3m = 45 \implies 9k + m = 20\). Solving gives \(k = 4\) and \(m = -16\), so \(k - m = 4 - (-16) = 20\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 3x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 4\) is divided by \(3x - 1\), the remainder is \(-2\). When it is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-10\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1/3) = \frac{k + 3m - 35}{9} = -2 \implies k + 3m = 17\), and \(P(-1) = k - m - 7 = -10 \implies k - m = -3\). Subtracting gives \(4m = 20 \implies m = 5\), which leads to \(k = 2\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 18\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 3\) and \(x + 2\). What is the value of \(k\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(3) = 0\) gives \(3k + m = -3\), and setting \(P(-2) = 0\) gives \(2k - m = -7\). Adding both equations yields \(5k = -10\), so \(k = -2\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 - kx^2 + mx - 6\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and \(x - 3\). What is the value of \(m\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(1) = 0\) gives \(-k + m = 5\), and setting \(P(3) = 0\) gives \(-3k + m = -25\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(2k = 30\), so \(k = 15\) and \(m = 20\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + kx^3 + mx - 12\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 1\). What is the value of \(k\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m + 4 = 0\) gives \(4k + m = -2\), and \(P(-1) = -k - m - 11 = 0\) gives \(k + m = -11\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(3k = 9\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + kx^3 + 2x^2 + mx - 8\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). What is the value of \(k\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(1) = 0\) yields \(k + m = 5\), and setting \(P(-2) = 0\) yields \(4k + m = 8\). Subtracting the equations gives \(3k = 3\), so \(k = 1\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(x^4 + kx^3 - 5x^2 + mx + 12\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\). What is the value of \(m\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m + 8 = 0\) simplifies to \(4k + m = -4\), and \(P(-3) = -27k - 3m + 48 = 0\) simplifies to \(9k + m = 16\). Solving this system gives \(k = 4\) and \(m = -20\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 + mx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(45\), and when divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(60\). What is the value of \(m\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 27k + 9m + 72 = 45\) gives \(3k + m = -3\), and \(P(-2) = -8k + 4m + 32 = 60\) gives \(-2k + m = 7\). Subtracting gives \(5k = -10\), so \(k = -2\), which yields \(m = 3\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = 3x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 30\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\). What is the value of \(k + m\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(2) = 0\) simplifies to \(2k + m = -1\), and \(P(-3) = 0\) simplifies to \(3k - m = -89\). Adding the equations gives \(5k = -90\), so \(k = -18\) and \(m = 35\), which results in \(k + m = 17\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 3x^2 + mx + 8\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(14\), and when divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-1\). What is the value of \(km\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m + 12 = 14\) gives \(4k + m = 1\), and \(P(-1) = -k - m + 6 = -1\) gives \(k + m = 7\). Solving the system gives \(k = -2\) and \(m = 9\), so \(km = -18\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^5 + kx^4 + mx^2 - 4x + 12\) has no remainder when divided by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). What is the value of \(m\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m + 9 = 0\) gives \(k + m = -9\), and \(P(-2) = 16k + 4m - 12 = 0\) gives \(4k + m = 3\). Subtracting gives \(3k = 12\), so \(k = 4\) and \(m = -13\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^3 + mx^2 - 7x + 6\) has no remainder when divided by \(2x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). What is the value of \(k - m\)?
qs.s: Evaluating \(P(1/2) = 0\) yields \(k + 2m = -21\), and \(P(-2) = 0\) yields \(2k - m = 13\). Solving this system gives \(k = 1\) and \(m = -11\), so \(k - m = 1 - (-11) = 12\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 - kx + 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 3x^3 + kx^2 - 2\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
When \(P(x) = 2x^3 - kx^2 + 3x - 1\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 + kx - 20\) is divided by \(x - 3\). Find the value of \(k\).
When \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 6\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^4 + kx - 8\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 2(1)^3 + k(1)^2 - 6 = k - 4\) and \(Q(2) = 2^4 + 2k - 8 = 2k + 8\). Equating the remainders gives \(k - 4 = 2k + 8\), which simplifies to \(k = -12\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^4 + 2x^3 - kx + 1\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^3 + 2kx + 5\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-1) = (-1)^4 + 2(-1)^3 - k(-1) + 1 = k\) and \(Q(1) = 2(1)^3 + 2k(1) + 5 = 2k + 7\). Equating the remainders gives \(k = 2k + 7\), so \(k = -7\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 4x^3 + kx^2 + 6\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^4 - 2kx + 3\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-2) = 4(-2)^3 + k(-2)^2 + 6 = 4k - 26\) and \(Q(1) = 1^4 - 2k(1) + 3 = 4 - 2k\). Equating them gives \(4k - 26 = 4 - 2k\), so \(6k = 30\) and \(k = 5\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - 3x^3 + kx^2 - 12x + 8\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(R_1\). When \(Q(x) = x^4 + 2kx^2 - 5x - 14\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(R_2\). If \(R_1 = 3R_2\), find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(R_1 = P(2) = 4k - 8\) and \(R_2 = Q(-1) = 2k - 8\). Substituting into \(R_1 = 3R_2\) gives \(4k - 8 = 3(2k - 8)\), which simplifies to \(-2k = -16\), so \(k = 8\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 + mx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(8\). When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-4\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m + 2 = 8 \implies k + m = 6\), and \(P(-2) = 32 - 8k + 4m = -4 \implies 2k - m = 9\). Adding the two linear equations gives \(3k = 15\), so \(k = 5\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^3 - 7x^2 + mx - 12\) is divisible by both \(x - 2\) and \(x + 1\). Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(2) = 8k + 2m - 8 = 0 \implies 4k + m = 4\), and \(P(-1) = -k - m - 17 = 0 \implies k + m = -17\). Subtracting these equations gives \(3k = 21 \implies k = 7\), which yields \(m = -17 - 7 = -24\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 4x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 3\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + 2x - 4\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{k}{4} + \frac{1}{2}\) and \(Q(2) = 4k + 8\). Setting \(\frac{k}{4} + \frac{1}{2} = 4k + 8\) and multiplying by \(4\) gives \(k + 2 = 16k + 32\), so \(k = -2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^5 - 3x^4 + 2x^3 + kx^2 - 15x + 18\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^4 - kx^3 + 5x^2 - 8x - 26\) is divided by \(x - 2\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 9k + 27\) and \(Q(2) = 10 - 8k\). Setting \(9k + 27 = 10 - 8k\) yields \(17k = -17\), which gives \(k = -1\).

exercises.name: Theoretical properties of the Remainder and Factor Theorems

qs.q: According to the Factor Theorem, the binomial \(x - a\) is a factor of a polynomial \(P(x)\) if and only if which condition is satisfied?
qs.s: The Factor Theorem states that \(x - a\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) if and only if the remainder is zero, meaning \(P(a) = 0\).

qs.q: According to the Factor Theorem, if \(x + 4\) is a factor of the polynomial \(P(x)\), what is the value of \(P(-4)\)?
qs.s: Since \(x + 4\) is a factor of \(P(x)\), division by \(x + 4\) leaves no remainder, which means \(P(-4) = 0\).

qs.q: If a polynomial \(P(x)\) satisfies \(P(c) = 0\), which binomial is guaranteed to be a factor of \(P(x)\) by the Factor Theorem?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, if \(P(c) = 0\), then \(x - c\) must be a factor of \(P(x)\).

qs.q: According to the Remainder Theorem, what is the value of the remainder when a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 5\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, dividing \(P(x)\) by \(x - 5\) leaves a remainder equal to \(P(5)\).

qs.q: According to the Remainder Theorem, if a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + a\), what is the value of its remainder?
qs.s: Setting the divisor \(x + a = 0\) gives \(x = -a\). By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(-a)\).

qs.q: If \(x - 4\) is a factor of the polynomial \(P(x)\), and the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\) is \(-18\), what is the value of \(2P(4) - P(-2)\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(4) = 0\), and by the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-2) = -18\). Thus, \(2P(4) - P(-2) = 2(0) - (-18) = 18\).

qs.q: According to the Remainder Theorem, what is the value of the remainder when a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \(a x - b\), where \(a \neq 0\)?
qs.s: Setting the divisor \(a x - b = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{b}{a}\). Substituting this into the polynomial gives the remainder \(P\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)\).

qs.q: When a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(5\). According to the Remainder Theorem, what is the remainder when the polynomial \(G(x) = (x + 1)P(x) + 4\) is divided by \(x - 2\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 5\), so the remainder when \(G(x)\) is divided by \(x - 2\) is \(G(2) = (2 + 1)P(2) + 4 = 3(5) + 4 = 19\).

qs.q: Let \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) be polynomials. When divided by \(x - c\), \(P(x)\) leaves a remainder of \(5\) and \(Q(x)\) leaves a remainder of \(-2\). According to the Remainder Theorem, what is the remainder when the polynomial \(F(x) = 2P(x) - 3Q(x)\) is divided by \(x - c\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(c) = 5\) and \(Q(c) = -2\), so the remainder is \(F(c) = 2P(c) - 3Q(c) = 2(5) - 3(-2) = 16\).

qs.q: According to the Factor Theorem, the binomial \(3x + 2\) is a factor of a polynomial \(P(x)\) if and only if which equation is satisfied?
qs.s: Setting \(3x + 2 = 0\) gives \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\). By the Factor Theorem, \(3x + 2\) is a factor if and only if the remainder \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = 0\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the positive value of \(k\) such that \(P(1) = 18\), given \(P(x) = 2x^3 - kx^2 + 4x + k^2\).
qs.s: Evaluating gives \(P(1) = 2(1)^3 - k(1)^2 + 4(1) + k^2 = k^2 - k + 6\). Setting \(k^2 - k + 6 = 18\) leads to \(k^2 - k - 12 = 0\), so \((k - 4)(k + 3) = 0\), yielding the positive value \(k = 4\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the positive value of \(k\) such that \(P(2) = 9\), given \(P(x) = x^3 - kx^2 - 2x + k^2\).
qs.s: By the remainder theorem, \(P(2) = 2^3 - k(2^2) - 2(2) + k^2 = k^2 - 4k + 4\). Setting \(k^2 - 4k + 4 = 9\) gives \(k^2 - 4k - 5 = 0\), which factors as \((k - 5)(k + 1) = 0\), yielding the positive value \(k = 5\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the greater value of \(r\) such that \(P(2) = 15\), given \(P(x) = x^3 - rx^2 + 5x + r^2\).
qs.s: Evaluating gives \(P(2) = 2^3 - r(2^2) + 5(2) + r^2 = r^2 - 4r + 18\). Setting \(r^2 - 4r + 18 = 15\) gives \(r^2 - 4r + 3 = 0\), so \((r - 1)(r - 3) = 0\), which gives the greater value \(r = 3\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the smaller value of \(m\) such that \(P(3) = 10\), given \(P(x) = x^3 - mx^2 - x + m^2\).
qs.s: Evaluating gives \(P(3) = 3^3 - m(3^2) - 3 + m^2 = m^2 - 9m + 24\). Setting \(m^2 - 9m + 24 = 10\) gives \(m^2 - 9m + 14 = 0\), so \((m - 2)(m - 7) = 0\), which yields the smaller value \(m = 2\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the positive value of \(k\) such that \(P(2) = 15\), given \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 7x + k^2\).
qs.s: Evaluating gives \(P(2) = 2^3 + k(2^2) - 7(2) + k^2 = k^2 + 4k - 6\). Setting \(k^2 + 4k - 6 = 15\) gives \(k^2 + 4k - 21 = 0\), so \((k + 7)(k - 3) = 0\), giving the positive value \(k = 3\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 8x^3 - 4cx^2 + 6x + c^2\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is 16. Use the remainder theorem to find the positive value of \(c\).
qs.s: Setting \(2x - 1 = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), so the remainder is \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 8\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) - 4c\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 6\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + c^2 = c^2 - c + 4\). Setting \(c^2 - c + 4 = 16\) gives \(c^2 - c - 12 = (c - 4)(c + 3) = 0\), so the positive value is \(c = 4\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 - rx^2 + 2x + r^2\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is the same as when \(Q(x) = 2x^3 + rx^2 + 5x + 11\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Use the remainder theorem to find the positive value of \(r\).
qs.s: The remainders are \(P(2) = r^2 - 4r + 12\) and \(Q(1) = r + 18\). Setting them equal gives \(r^2 - 4r + 12 = r + 18\), so \(r^2 - 5r - 6 = (r - 6)(r + 1) = 0\), giving the positive value \(r = 6\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 + kx^3 - k^2x^2 + 8x + 16\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-28\). Use the remainder theorem to find the sum of all possible values of \(k\).
qs.s: By the remainder theorem, \(P(-2) = 32 - 8k - 4k^2 = -28\), which simplifies to \(k^2 + 2k - 15 = 0\). Factoring gives \((k + 5)(k - 3) = 0\), so the values of \(k\) are \(-5\) and \(3\), giving a sum of \(-5 + 3 = -2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 - kx^2 + 3x + k^2\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is 19. If \(k > 0\), what is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\)?
Given \(P(x) = x^4 - 2kx^3 + 3kx - 14 + 3k^2\), use the remainder theorem to find the positive value of \(k\) such that when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is 10.
qs.s: By the remainder theorem, the remainder is \(P(2) = 2^4 - 2k(2^3) + 3k(2) - 14 + 3k^2 = 3k^2 - 10k + 2\). Setting \(3k^2 - 10k + 2 = 10\) yields \(3k^2 - 10k - 8 = (3k + 2)(k - 4) = 0\), so the positive value is \(k = 4\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^n + 2x - 1\) is divided by \(x - 3\), there is a remainder of 32. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(3) = 3^n + 2(3) - 1 = 3^n + 5\). Setting \(3^n + 5 = 32\) gives \(3^n = 27\), so \(n = 3\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^n + 3x - 7\) is divided by \(x - 4\), there is a remainder of 21. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(4) = 4^n + 3(4) - 7 = 4^n + 5\). Setting \(4^n + 5 = 21\) gives \(4^n = 16\), so \(n = 2\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^n - 2x + 9\) is divided by \(x - 3\), there is a remainder of 84. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(3) = 3^n - 2(3) + 9 = 3^n + 3\). Setting \(3^n + 3 = 84\) gives \(3^n = 81\), so \(n = 4\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^n - 3x + 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), there is a remainder of 31. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(2) = 2^n - 3(2) + 5 = 2^n - 1\). Setting \(2^n - 1 = 31\) gives \(2^n = 32\), so \(n = 5\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^n + 4x - 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), there is a remainder of 67. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(2) = 2^n + 4(2) - 5 = 2^n + 3\). Setting \(2^n + 3 = 67\) gives \(2^n = 64\), so \(n = 6\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^{2n} + x^n - 3x + 2\) is divided by \(x - 2\), there is a remainder of 16. Given that \(n\) is a positive integer, what is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = (2^n)^2 + 2^n - 4 = 16\), which gives \((2^n)^2 + 2^n - 20 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2^n - 4)(2^n + 5) = 0\), and since \(2^n > 0\), we have \(2^n = 4\), so \(n = 2\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(x^n + 3x^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(x + 2\), there is a remainder of \(-4\). What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(-2) = (-2)^n + 3(-2)^2 - 5(-2) + 6 = (-2)^n + 28\). Setting \((-2)^n + 28 = -4\) gives \((-2)^n = -32\), so \(n = 5\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(3x^n - 2x^3 + 5x - 11\) is divided by \(x - 2\), there is a remainder of 31. What is the value of \(n\)?
When \(P(x) = x^n + 2x^2 - 11\) and \(Q(x) = 7x^3 + 2x + 1\) are both divided by \(x - 2\), they produce the same remainder. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: The remainder for \(Q(x)\) is \(Q(2) = 7(8) + 4 + 1 = 61\), and the remainder for \(P(x)\) is \(P(2) = 2^n + 2(4) - 11 = 2^n - 3\). Setting \(2^n - 3 = 61\) yields \(2^n = 64\), so \(n = 6\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(16x^n - 12x^2 + 7\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), there is a remainder of 6. What is the value of \(n\)?
qs.s: Evaluating at \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), the remainder is \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 16\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n - 12\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 7 = 16\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n + 4\). Setting this equal to 6 gives \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n = \frac{1}{8}\), so \(n = 3\).

qs.q: When \(x^2 - 5x - 4\) is divided by \(x - a\), the remainder is \(10\). Find the larger of the two possible values of \(a\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(a) = a^2 - 5a - 4\). Setting \(a^2 - 5a - 4 = 10\) gives \(a^2 - 5a - 14 = 0\), which factors as \((a - 7)(a + 2) = 0\), so the larger value is \(a = 7\).

qs.q: When \(x^2 + 3x + 6\) is divided by \(x + a\), the remainder is \(10\). Find the positive value of \(a\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(-a) = (-a)^2 + 3(-a) + 6 = a^2 - 3a + 6\). Setting \(a^2 - 3a + 6 = 10\) yields \(a^2 - 3a - 4 = 0\), which factors as \((a - 4)(a + 1) = 0\), giving the positive value \(a = 4\).

qs.q: When \(x^2 + 8x + 1\) is divided by \(x + a\), the remainder is \(-14\). Find the smaller of the two possible values of \(a\).
qs.s: The remainder is \(P(-a) = (-a)^2 + 8(-a) + 1 = a^2 - 8a + 1\). Setting \(a^2 - 8a + 1 = -14\) yields \(a^2 - 8a + 15 = 0\), which factors into \((a - 3)(a - 5) = 0\), so the smaller value is \(a = 3\).

qs.q: When \(x^2 - 4x + 3\) is divided by \(x - a\), the remainder is \(8\). Find the positive value of \(a\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(a) = a^2 - 4a + 3\). Setting \(a^2 - 4a + 3 = 8\) gives \(a^2 - 4a - 5 = 0\), which factors as \((a - 5)(a + 1) = 0\), so the positive value is \(a = 5\).

qs.q: When \(x^2 - 6x + 5\) is divided by \(x + a\), the remainder is \(12\). Find the sum of all possible values of \(a\).
qs.s: The remainder is \(P(-a) = (-a)^2 - 6(-a) + 5 = a^2 + 6a + 5\). Setting \(a^2 + 6a + 5 = 12\) gives \(a^2 + 6a - 7 = 0\), whose roots are \(a = 1\) and \(a = -7\), giving a sum of \(1 + (-7) = -6\).

qs.q: When \(x^2 + 4x - 5\) is divided by \(2x - a\), the remainder is \(7\). Find the positive value of \(a\).
qs.s: Setting \(2x - a = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{a}{2}\), so the remainder is \(\left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2 + 4\left(\frac{a}{2}\right) - 5 = 7\). Simplifying yields \(\frac{a^2}{4} + 2a - 12 = 0 \implies a^2 + 8a - 48 = 0\), which factors as \((a + 12)(a - 4) = 0\), giving the positive value \(a = 4\).

qs.q: When \(2x^2 + 7x + 5\) is divided by \(x + a\), the remainder is \(9\). Find the sum of all possible values of \(a\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(-a) = 2(-a)^2 + 7(-a) + 5 = 2a^2 - 7a + 5\). Setting \(2a^2 - 7a + 5 = 9\) gives \(2a^2 - 7a - 4 = 0\), which factors into \((2a + 1)(a - 4) = 0\), giving solutions \(a = 4\) and \(a = -\frac{1}{2}\) with a sum of \(4 + \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 3x + 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is equal to the remainder when \(Q(x) = 2x^3 - x^2 + kx - 3\) is divided by \(x - 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: The remainders are \(P(2) = 2^3 + k(2^2) - 3(2) + 5 = 4k + 7\) and \(Q(1) = 2(1)^3 - 1^2 + k(1) - 3 = k - 2\). Setting them equal gives \(4k + 7 = k - 2\), which solves to \(k = -3\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 4\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(14\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 3\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2^3 + k(2^2) - 5(2) + 4 = 4k + 2 = 14\), which gives \(k = 3\). Evaluating \(P(-3) = (-3)^3 + 3(-3)^2 - 5(-3) + 4\) gives a remainder of \(19\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(0\), and when it is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-12\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 1 + k + m - 6 = 0 \implies k + m = 5\), and \(P(-2) = -8 + 4k - 2m - 6 = -12 \implies 2k - m = 1\). Adding these two linear equations gives \(3k = 6\), so \(k = 2\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to solve the following: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^{60} - kx^{35} + 3x^2 - 11\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is 8. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
Use the remainder theorem to solve the following: When the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^{100} + 5x^{45} - 2x + 9\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is 1. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
Use the remainder theorem to solve the following: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 3x^{75} + kx^{24} - 6x^3 + 8\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is 15. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(-1) = 3(-1)^{75} + k(-1)^{24} - 6(-1)^3 + 8 = -3 + k + 6 + 8 = k + 11\). Setting \(k + 11 = 15\) yields \(k = 4\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to solve the following: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 4x^{80} - x^{51} + kx - 13\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is -2. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
Use the remainder theorem to solve the following: When the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^{40} - 3x^{21} + 5x - 2\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is 12. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).

When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 3\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is equal to the remainder when \(Q(x) = 3x^4 - kx^3 + 4x^2 + 32\) is divided by \(x + 1\). Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 2(8) + 4k - 10 + 3 = 4k + 9\) and \(Q(-1) = 3(1) + k + 4(1) + 32 = k + 39\). Equating them gives \(4k + 9 = k + 39\), which yields \(3k = 30\), so \(k = 10\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 8x^4 - 4x^3 + kx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is 7. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P(1/2) = 8(1/16) - 4(1/8) + k(1/4) - 5(1/2) + 6 = \frac{k}{4} + \frac{7}{2}\). Setting \(\frac{k}{4} + \frac{7}{2} = 7\) gives \(\frac{k}{4} = \frac{7}{2}\), so \(k = 14\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = kx^{101} - 3kx^{50} + 4x^{25} - 2x^2 + 15\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is 37. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
The polynomial \(P(x) = 2kx^{99} + (k - 5)x^{64} - 3kx^3 + 7x - 18\) has \(x + 1\) as a factor. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(x + 1\) is a factor if and only if \(P(-1) = 0\). Evaluating gives \(P(-1) = -2k + (k - 5) + 3k - 25 = 2k - 30 = 0\), which yields \(k = 15\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^4 - kx^3 + (k - 1)x^2 + 5x - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is 12. Determine the value of the constant, \(k\).
The polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 + mx + 6\) has \(x - 2\) as a factor. When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(12\). Find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: By the Factor and Remainder Theorems, \(P(2) = 4k + 2m + 22 = 0 \implies 2k + m = -11\) and \(P(-1) = k - m + 4 = 12 \implies k - m = 8\). Solving this linear system gives \(k = -1\) and \(m = -9\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the value of \(k + m\) if \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + kx + m\), \(P(2) = -6\), and \(P(-1) = -12\).
qs.s: The conditions give \(P(2) = 2k + m - 8 = -6 \implies 2k + m = 2\) and \(P(-1) = -k + m - 5 = -12 \implies -k + m = -7\). Solving yields \(k = 3\) and \(m = -4\), so \(k + m = -1\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(2\). When it is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-4\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m - 3 = 2 \implies k + m = 5\) and \(P(-2) = 4k - 2m - 12 = -4 \implies 2k - m = 4\). Adding these two equations gives \(3k = 9\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: If \(P(x) = 3x^3 - x^2 + kx + m\) satisfies \(P(2) = 23\) and \(P(-1) = 5\), find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: Evaluating gives \(P(2) = 20 + 2k + m = 23 \implies 2k + m = 3\) and \(P(-1) = -4 - k + m = 5 \implies -k + m = 9\). Adding twice the second equation to the first gives \(3m = 21\), which simplifies to \(m = 7\).

qs.q: Use the remainder theorem to find the value of \(k\) if \(P(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 + kx + m\), \(P(1) = 1\), and \(P(-1) = -7\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 3 + k + m = 1 \implies k + m = -2\) and \(P(-1) = 1 - k + m = -7 \implies -k + m = -8\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(2k = 6\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + mx + 4\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(10\). When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(3\) times the remainder obtained when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 1\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: The first condition gives \(P(1) = k + m + 5 = 10 \implies k + m = 5\). The second condition gives \(P(2) = 3P(-1) \implies 4k + 2m + 12 = 3(k - m + 3) \implies k + 5m = -3\), which solves to \(m = -2\) and \(k = 7\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 + kx^3 - 5x^2 + mx + 12\) is divisible by both \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\). Find the value of \(k - m\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m + 8 = 0 \implies k + m = -8\) and \(P(-2) = -8k - 2m + 8 = 0 \implies 4k + m = 4\). Subtracting gives \(3k = 12 \implies k = 4\), which gives \(m = -12\), so \(k - m = 4 - (-12) = 16\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 6\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(0\), and when divided by \(x + 1\), the remainder is \(-12\). What is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 3\)?
qs.s: Using the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = k + m - 4 = 0 \implies k + m = 4\) and \(P(-1) = k - m - 8 = -12 \implies k - m = -4\), which gives \(k = 0\) and \(m = 4\). Then the remainder when \(P(x) = 2x^3 + 4x - 6\) is divided by \(x - 3\) is \(P(3) = 2(27) + 4(3) - 6 = 60\).

qs.q: If the polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 + mx - 18\) is divisible by both \(x - 3\) and \(x + 3\), find the value of \(m\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(3) = 9k + 3m + 9 = 0 \implies 3k + m = -3\) and \(P(-3) = 9k - 3m + 117 = 0 \implies 3k - m = -39\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(2m = 36\), so \(m = 18\).

qs.q: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 4x^3 + kx^2 + mx + 5\) is divided by \(2x - 1\), the remainder is \(7\). When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-23\). Find the value of \(k\).
qs.s: Setting \(P(1/2) = 7\) gives \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{k}{4} + \frac{m}{2} + 5 = 7 \implies k + 2m = 6\), and setting \(P(-2) = -23\) gives \(4k - 2m - 27 = -23 \implies 4k - 2m = 4\). Adding these equations yields \(5k = 10\), so \(k = 2\).

exercises.name: Finding missing factors using synthetic division

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^3 - 5x^2 - x + 6 = (x - 2)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^3 - 5x^2 - x + 6\) by \(x - 2\) using synthetic division yields the quotient \(2x^2 - x - 3\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x - 3)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^3 - x^2 - 11x + 10 = (x - 1)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^3 - x^2 - 11x + 10\) by \(x - 1\) using synthetic division yields the quotient \(2x^2 + x - 10\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x + 5)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(3x^3 + x^2 - 12x - 4 = (x - 2)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^3 + x^2 - 12x - 4\) by \(x - 2\) using synthetic division yields the quotient \(3x^2 + 7x + 2\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((3x + 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^3 + 3x^2 - 8x + 3 = (x + 3)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^3 + 3x^2 - 8x + 3\) by \(x + 3\) using synthetic division yields the quotient \(2x^2 - 3x + 1\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x - 1)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(3x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 4 = (x + 1)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 4\) by \(x + 1\) using synthetic division yields the quotient \(3x^2 - 8x + 4\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((3x - 2)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^4 - 2x^3 - 7x^2 + 8x + 12 = (x - 2)(x + 1)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing successively by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 1\) using synthetic division gives the quotients \(x^3 - 7x - 6\) and \(x^2 - x - 6\). Factoring the quadratic yields \((x - 3)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(4x^3 - 12x^2 - 19x + 12 = (2x - 1)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - \frac{1}{2}\) using synthetic division gives \(4x^2 - 10x - 24\), which divided by \(2\) results in \(2x^2 - 5x - 12\). Factoring this quadratic yields \((2x + 3)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(6x^3 + 19x^2 + x - 6 = (3x + 2)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(x + \frac{2}{3}\) using synthetic division gives \(6x^2 + 15x - 9\), which divided by \(3\) results in \(2x^2 + 5x - 3\). Factoring this quadratic yields \((2x - 1)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(6x^3 + 13x^2 - 4x - 15 = (x - 1)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^3 + 13x^2 - 4x - 15\) by \(x - 1\) using synthetic division yields \(6x^2 + 19x + 15\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x + 3)(3x + 5)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^4 - 3x^3 - 12x^2 + 7x + 6 = (x - 1)(x - 3)(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x - 3\) using synthetic division gives \(2x^3 - x^2 - 13x - 6\) and then \(2x^2 + 5x + 2\). Factoring the resulting quadratic yields \((2x + 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^3 + x^2 - 10x + 8 = (x - 2)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Synthetic division with \(2\) yields the quotient polynomial \(x^2 + 3x - 4\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^3 - 6x^2 + 3x + 10 = (x + 1)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Using synthetic division with root \(-1\), the quotient polynomial is \(x^2 - 7x + 10\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((x - 2)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^3 + 3x^2 - 13x - 15 = (x + 5)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing by \(x + 5\) using synthetic division gives the quotient \(x^2 - 2x - 3\). Factoring the quadratic gives \((x - 3)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^3 - 2x^2 - 11x + 12 = (x + 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing synthetically by \(-3\) gives the quotient \(x^2 - 5x + 4\). Factoring this quadratic yields \((x - 1)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^3 - 5x^2 - 8x + 12 = (x - 6)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Using synthetic division with \(6\) yields the quotient \(x^2 + x - 2\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^4 + 3x^3 - 15x^2 - 19x + 30 = (x - 1)(x - 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing synthetically by \(1\) and then by \(3\) gives the quadratic quotient \(x^2 + 7x + 10\). Factoring this quotient yields \((x + 2)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 6 = (x - 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(3\) gives the quotient \(2x^2 + 3x - 2\). Factoring this quadratic results in \((2x - 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(3x^3 - 7x^2 - 22x + 8 = (x + 2)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing synthetically by \(-2\) gives the quotient \(3x^2 - 13x + 4\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((3x - 1)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^4 - 2x^3 - 13x^2 + 14x + 24 = (x + 1)(x - 2)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing synthetically by \(-1\) gives \(x^3 - 3x^2 - 10x + 24\), and dividing that result by \(2\) gives \(x^2 - x - 12\). Factoring yields \((x - 4)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(4x^3 + 8x^2 - 11x - 15 = (x + 1)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Synthetic division by \(-1\) yields the quotient \(4x^2 + 4x - 15\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x - 3)(2x + 5)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 - 2x^3 - 25x^2 + 50x = x(x - 2)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(x^3 - 2x^2 - 25x + 50\) by \(x - 2\) using synthetic division with \(2\) gives the quotient \(x^2 - 25\). Factoring this difference of squares yields \((x - 5)(x + 5)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 + 2x^3 - 16x^2 - 32x = x(x + 2)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the cubic factor \(x^3 + 2x^2 - 16x - 32\) by \(x + 2\) using synthetic division with \(-2\) yields the quotient \(x^2 - 16\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 - 8x^3 + 19x^2 - 12x = x(x - 1)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(x^3 - 8x^2 + 19x - 12\) by \(x - 1\) using synthetic division with \(1\) gives the quotient \(x^2 - 7x + 12\). Factoring the quadratic gives \((x - 3)(x - 4)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 + 2x^3 - 5x^2 - 6x = x(x + 1)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(x^3 + 2x^2 - 5x - 6\) by \(x + 1\) using synthetic division with \(-1\) gives the quotient \(x^2 + x - 6\). Factoring this quadratic yields \((x - 2)(x + 3)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 - 3x^3 - x^2 + 3x = x(x - 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(x^3 - 3x^2 - x + 3\) by \(x - 3\) using synthetic division with \(3\) results in the quotient \(x^2 - 1\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle 3x^4 - 10x^3 - 9x^2 + 4x = x(x - 4)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^3 - 10x^2 - 9x + 4\) by \(x - 4\) using synthetic division with \(4\) gives \(3x^2 + 2x - 1\). Factoring this non-monic quadratic gives \((3x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 - 6x^3 + 3x^2 + 26x - 24 = (x - 1)(x - 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the polynomial by \(x - 1\) gives \(x^3 - 5x^2 - 2x + 24\), and dividing that result by \(x - 3\) gives \(x^2 - 2x - 8\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((x - 4)(x + 2)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle 2x^4 + 7x^3 - 2x^2 - 13x + 6 = (x - 1)(x + 2)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the polynomial by \(x - 1\) gives \(2x^3 + 9x^2 + 7x - 6\), and dividing that result by \(x + 2\) gives \(2x^2 + 5x - 3\). Factoring this quadratic yields \((2x - 1)(x + 3)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle 2x^4 + 7x^3 - 10x^2 - 24x = x(x + 4)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^3 + 7x^2 - 10x - 24\) by \(x + 4\) using synthetic division with \(-4\) gives the quotient \(2x^2 - x - 6\). Factoring this non-monic quadratic yields \((2x + 3)(x - 2)\).

qs.q:
Find the missing factors by synthetic division:
\(\displaystyle x^4 - 3x^3 - 15x^2 + 19x + 30 = (x - 2)(x + 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing successively by \(x - 2\) and then by \(x + 3\) using synthetic division results in the quotient \(x^2 - 4x - 5\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((x - 5)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(3x^4 - 7x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x - 2 = (x - 1)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^4 - 7x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x - 2\) successively by \(x - 1\) three times using synthetic division with \(x = 1\) gives final quotient coefficients of \(3\) and \(2\). Hence, the missing factor is \(3x + 2\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(x^4 - 5x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x - 8 = (x - 2)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(x^4 - 5x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x - 8\) successively by \(x - 2\) three times using synthetic division with \(x = 2\) yields quotient coefficients of \(1\) and \(1\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 1\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(2x^4 - 17x^3 + 45x^2 - 27x - 27 = (x - 3)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^4 - 17x^3 + 45x^2 - 27x - 27\) successively by \(x - 3\) three times using synthetic division with \(x = 3\) yields quotient coefficients of \(2\) and \(1\). Therefore, the missing factor is \(2x + 1\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(2x^4 + 3x^3 - 3x^2 - 7x - 3 = (x + 1)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^4 + 3x^3 - 3x^2 - 7x - 3\) successively by \(x + 1\) three times using synthetic division with \(x = -1\) yields quotient coefficients of \(2\) and \(-3\). Therefore, the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(x^4 + 3x^3 - 6x^2 - 28x - 24 = (x + 2)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing \(x^4 + 3x^3 - 6x^2 - 28x - 24\) successively by \(x + 2\) three times using synthetic division with \(x = -2\) gives quotient coefficients of \(1\) and \(-3\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x - 3\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(2x^5 - 5x^4 + 10x^2 - 10x + 3 = (x - 1)^4(\) \()\)
qs.s: Using a \(0\) placeholder for the \(x^3\) term, perform synthetic division by \(x = 1\) four consecutive times. The final quotient has coefficients \(2\) and \(3\), which corresponds to \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(x^5 + x^4 + x^3 + 7x^2 + 10x + 4 = (x + 1)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing the degree-5 polynomial successively by \(x + 1\) three times using synthetic division with \(x = -1\) leaves quadratic coefficients \([1, -2, 4]\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x^2 - 2x + 4\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(2x^5 - 9x^4 + 5x^3 + 26x^2 - 36x + 8 = (x - 2)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Dividing the coefficients \([2, -9, 5, 26, -36, 8]\) successively by \(x = 2\) three times yields the remaining quadratic coefficients \([2, 3, -1]\). Hence, the missing factor is \(2x^2 + 3x - 1\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(2x^4 - 11x^3 + 15x^2 + 8x - 20 = (x - 2)^2(x + 1)(\) \()\)
qs.s: Apply synthetic division twice using \(x = 2\), then divide the resulting quotient once using \(x = -1\). The final quotient coefficients are \(2\) and \(-5\), giving the missing factor \(2x - 5\).

qs.q: Find the missing factor by synthetic division: \(x^4 - 6x^2 + 8x - 3 = (x - 1)^3(\) \()\)
qs.s: Using a \(0\) placeholder for the missing \(x^3\) term, divide the coefficients \([1, 0, -6, 8, -3]\) by \(x = 1\) three times sequentially. The resulting linear quotient has coefficients \(1\) and \(3\), giving the missing factor \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^4 + 9x^3 - 4x^2 - 36x - 16 = (x^2 - 4)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^4 + 9x^3 - 4x^2 - 36x - 16\) successively by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 2\) using synthetic division results in the quotient \(2x^2 + 9x + 4\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x + 1)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(3x^4 + x^3 - 14x^2 - 4x + 8 = (x^2 - 4)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^4 + x^3 - 14x^2 - 4x + 8\) successively by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 2\) using synthetic division gives the quotient \(3x^2 + x - 2\). Factoring this quadratic yields \((3x - 2)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^4 - 5x^3 - 14x^2 + 5x + 12 = (x^2 - 1)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^4 - 5x^3 - 14x^2 + 5x + 12\) successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 1\) using synthetic division yields the quotient \(2x^2 - 5x - 12\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x + 3)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^4 - 3x^3 - 23x^2 + 27x + 45 = (x^2 - 9)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^4 - 3x^3 - 23x^2 + 27x + 45\) successively by \(x - 3\) and \(x + 3\) using synthetic division results in the quotient \(2x^2 - 3x - 5\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((2x - 5)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(3x^4 - 7x^3 - 9x^2 + 7x + 6 = (x^2 - 1)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^4 - 7x^3 - 9x^2 + 7x + 6\) successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 1\) using synthetic division gives the quotient \(3x^2 - 7x - 6\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((3x + 2)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(4x^4 - 15x^3 - 15x^2 + 50x - 24 = (x^2 - 5x + 4)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor the divisor as \((x - 1)(x - 4)\), then divide \(4x^4 - 15x^3 - 15x^2 + 50x - 24\) successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x - 4\) using synthetic division to obtain \(4x^2 + 5x - 6\). Factoring this quotient gives \((4x - 3)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(4x^4 - 43x^2 + 9x + 90 = (x^2 + x - 6)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor the divisor as \((x - 2)(x + 3)\), then divide \(4x^4 + 0x^3 - 43x^2 + 9x + 90\) successively by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\) using synthetic division to obtain \(4x^2 - 4x - 15\). Factoring this quotient yields \((2x + 3)(2x - 5)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(5x^4 - 9x^3 - 46x^2 + 32 = (x^2 - 2x - 8)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor the divisor as \((x - 4)(x + 2)\), then divide \(5x^4 - 9x^3 - 46x^2 + 0x + 32\) successively by \(x - 4\) and \(x + 2\) using synthetic division to find the quotient \(5x^2 + x - 4\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((5x - 4)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(6x^4 - 17x^3 - 13x^2 + 33x - 9 = (x^2 - 4x + 3)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor the divisor as \((x - 1)(x - 3)\), then divide \(6x^4 - 17x^3 - 13x^2 + 33x - 9\) successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x - 3\) using synthetic division to get \(6x^2 + 7x - 3\). Factoring this quotient gives \((2x + 3)(3x - 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(6x^4 + 19x^3 - 15x^2 - 46x + 24 = (x^2 + 5x + 6)(\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor the divisor as \((x + 2)(x + 3)\), then divide \(6x^4 + 19x^3 - 15x^2 - 46x + 24\) successively by \(x + 2\) and \(x + 3\) using synthetic division to obtain \(6x^2 - 11x + 4\). Factoring this quotient gives \((2x - 1)(3x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^5 - x^4 - 9x^3 + 13x^2 + 8x - 12 = (x^2 + 2x - 3)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 + 2x - 3\) into \((x - 1)(x + 3)\), then divide successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 3\) using synthetic division to reach \(x^3 - 3x^2 + 4\). Dividing further by \(x + 1\) yields \(x^2 - 4x + 4 = (x - 2)^2\), yielding missing factors \((x + 1)(x - 2)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^5 - 5x^4 - 3x^3 + 29x^2 + 2x - 24 = (x^2 - 2x - 3)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 - 2x - 3\) as \((x - 3)(x + 1)\) and divide the polynomial synthetically by \(x - 3\) and then \(x + 1\) to get \(x^3 - 3x^2 - 6x + 8\). Testing root \(1\) gives quotient \(x^2 - 2x - 8 = (x + 2)(x - 4)\), so the missing factors are \((x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^5 + 3x^4 - 5x^3 - 15x^2 + 4x + 12 = (x^2 + 5x + 6)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 + 5x + 6\) as \((x + 2)(x + 3)\) and use synthetic division to divide by \(x + 3\) and \(x + 2\), giving the quotient \(x^3 - 2x^2 - x + 2\). Factoring by grouping yields \(x^2(x - 2) - 1(x - 2) = (x + 1)(x - 1)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^5 - 3x^4 - 5x^3 + 15x^2 + 4x - 12 = (x^2 + x - 2)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factoring the divisor gives \((x - 1)(x + 2)\); dividing successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 2\) with synthetic division yields the quotient \(x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6\). Dividing this quotient by \(x + 1\) produces \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)\), giving the missing factors \((x + 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^5 - 11x^4 + 45x^3 - 85x^2 + 74x - 24 = (x^2 - 5x + 4)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 - 5x + 4\) as \((x - 1)(x - 4)\) and perform synthetic division with \(1\) and \(4\) to obtain the quotient \(x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6\). Testing root \(1\) gives \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)\), so the missing factors are \((x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^6 - 4x^5 - 2x^4 + 20x^3 - 11x^2 - 16x + 12 = (x^2 - x - 2)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 - x - 2\) as \((x - 2)(x + 1)\) and divide the degree 6 polynomial successively by \(2\) and \(-1\) to get \(x^4 - 3x^3 - 3x^2 + 11x - 6\). Dividing by \(x - 1\) twice leaves \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x + 2)(x - 3)\), giving missing factors \((x - 1)(x - 1)(x + 2)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(x^5 - 8x^3 + 6x^2 + 7x - 6 = (x^2 - 1)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Using a \(0\) placeholder for the missing \(x^4\) term, divide successively by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 1\) to get \(x^3 - 7x + 6\). Synthetic division by \(x - 1\) on \(x^3 + 0x^2 - 7x + 6\) leaves \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x - 2)(x + 3)\), giving the missing factors \((x - 1)(x - 2)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(3x^5 + x^4 - 15x^3 - 5x^2 + 12x + 4 = (x^2 - 4)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Divide successively by \(x - 2\) and \(x + 2\) using synthetic division to reach \(3x^3 + x^2 - 3x - 1\). Factoring by grouping gives \(x^2(3x + 1) - (3x + 1) = (3x + 1)(x^2 - 1) = (3x + 1)(x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^5 - 11x^4 + 15x^3 + 5x^2 - 17x + 6 = (x^2 - 3x + 2)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(x^2 - 3x + 2\) as \((x - 1)(x - 2)\) and divide synthetically to find the quotient \(2x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 3\). By the Rational Root Theorem, test and divide by \(x + 1\) to obtain \(2x^2 - 7x + 3 = (2x - 1)(x - 3)\), giving missing factors \((2x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the missing factors by synthetic division: \(2x^5 - x^4 - 10x^3 + 5x^2 + 8x - 4 = (2x^2 + x - 1)(\) \()(\) \()(\) \()\)
qs.s: Factor \(2x^2 + x - 1\) into \((2x - 1)(x + 1)\) and divide synthetically by \(-1\) and then \(\frac{1}{2}\) (halving the quotient coefficients) to obtain \(x^3 - x^2 - 4x + 4\). Factoring this cubic by grouping gives \(x^2(x - 1) - 4(x - 1) = (x - 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

exercises.name: Finding remaining roots of a polynomial equation

qs.q: If 1 is a root of the equation \(4x^3 + 5x^2 - 18x + 9 = 0\), what is the larger of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(4x^3 + 5x^2 - 18x + 9\) by \(x - 1\) gives \(4x^2 + 9x - 9 = (4x - 3)(x + 3) = 0\). The remaining roots are \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(-3\), of which the larger is \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: If 4 is a root of the equation \(6x^3 - 25x^2 + 2x + 8 = 0\), what is the larger of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^3 - 25x^2 + 2x + 8\) by \(x - 4\) yields \(6x^2 - x - 2 = (2x + 1)(3x - 2) = 0\). The other roots are \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\frac{2}{3}\), so the larger root is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: If \(-1\) is a root of the equation \(3x^3 - 7x^2 - 18x - 8 = 0\), what is the smaller of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^3 - 7x^2 - 18x - 8\) by \(x + 1\) yields the quotient \(3x^2 - 10x - 8 = (3x + 2)(x - 4) = 0\). The other roots are \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(4\), so the smaller root is \(-\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: If \(-2\) is a root of the equation \(3x^3 - 8x^2 - 33x - 10 = 0\), what is the smaller of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^3 - 8x^2 - 33x - 10\) by \(x + 2\) yields \(3x^2 - 14x - 5 = (3x + 1)(x - 5) = 0\). The other roots are \(-\frac{1}{3}\) and \(5\), so the smaller root is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: If 3 is a root of the equation \(2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 6 = 0\), what is the larger of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(2x^3 - 3x^2 - 11x + 6\) by \(x - 3\) gives the quotient \(2x^2 + 3x - 2 = (2x - 1)(x + 2) = 0\). The other roots are \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(-2\), so the larger root is \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: If 1 is a root of the equation \(x^3 - 3x^2 - 2x + 4 = 0\), what is the larger of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(x^3 - 3x^2 - 2x + 4\) by \(x - 1\) gives \(x^2 - 2x - 4 = 0\). Applying the quadratic formula yields \(x = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{20}}{2} = 1 \pm \sqrt{5}\), so the larger root is \(1 + \sqrt{5}\).

qs.q: If 3 is a root of the equation \(2x^4 - 5x^3 - 11x^2 + 20x + 12 = 0\), what is the smallest of the remaining roots?
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - 3\) gives \(2x^3 + x^2 - 8x - 4 = 0\), which factors by grouping as \((x^2 - 4)(2x + 1) = 0\). The remaining roots are \(-2\), \(-\frac{1}{2}\), and \(2\), so the smallest is \(-2\).

qs.q: If \(\frac{2}{3}\) is a root of the equation \(3x^3 + x^2 - 62x + 40 = 0\), what is the larger of the other two roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(3x^3 + x^2 - 62x + 40\) by \(x - \frac{2}{3}\) yields \(3x^2 + 3x - 60 = 3(x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\). The remaining roots are \(-5\) and \(4\), so the larger is \(4\).

qs.q: If \(-2\) is a root of the equation \(2x^4 - x^3 - 14x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\), what is the largest of the remaining roots?
qs.s: Dividing by \(x + 2\) yields \(2x^3 - 5x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0\), which has root \(x = -1\); further division gives \(2x^2 - 7x + 3 = (2x - 1)(x - 3) = 0\). The remaining roots are \(-1\), \(\frac{1}{2}\), and \(3\), of which the largest is \(3\).

qs.q: If 2 is a root of the equation \(x^4 + x^3 - 7x^2 - x + 6 = 0\), what is the smallest of the remaining roots?
qs.s: Dividing \(x^4 + x^3 - 7x^2 - x + 6\) by \(x - 2\) gives \(x^3 + 3x^2 - x - 3 = (x^2 - 1)(x + 3) = 0\), which factors as \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x + 3) = 0\). The remaining roots are \(-3\), \(-1\), and \(1\), of which the smallest is \(-3\).

qs.q: What is the smallest value of \(k\) for which 1 is a zero of \(P(x) = 2x^3 + 4x^2 - 7kx + k^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(1) = 0\) yields \(k^3 - 7k + 6 = 0\), which factors as \((k - 1)(k - 2)(k + 3) = 0\). The smallest solution is \(k = -3\).

qs.q: What is the real value of \(k\) for which 1 is a zero of \(P(x) = -8x^3 - 2k^2x^2 + 4kx + k^3\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = k^3 - 2k^2 + 4k - 8 = 0\). Factoring by grouping yields \((k - 2)(k^2 + 4) = 0\), which has only one real solution, \(k = 2\).

qs.q: What is the positive value of \(k\) for which 1 is a zero of \(P(x) = 5x^3 - 7x^2 - 3kx + k^3\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = 0\), which gives \(k^3 - 3k - 2 = 0\). Factoring gives \((k - 2)(k + 1)^2 = 0\), so the positive value of \(k\) is \(2\).

qs.q: What is the largest value of \(k\) for which \(-1\) is a zero of \(P(x) = -12x^3 - 4kx^2 + 3k^2x + k^3\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(-1) = k^3 - 3k^2 - 4k + 12 = 0\). Factoring by grouping gives \((k - 2)(k + 2)(k - 3) = 0\), so the largest value of \(k\) is \(3\).

qs.q: What is the largest value of \(k\) for which 1 is a zero of \(P(x) = 6x^3 - 5kx^2 - 2k^2x + k^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(1) = 0\) gives \(k^3 - 2k^2 - 5k + 6 = 0\). By the Rational Root Theorem, this factors into \((k - 1)(k - 3)(k + 2) = 0\), so the largest solution is \(k = 3\).

qs.q: The remainder when \(P(x) = k^3x^3 - 7kx + 2\) is divided by \(x - 1\) is equal to the remainder when \(Q(x) = k^2x^2 - x^3\) is divided by \(x - 2\). What is the largest value of \(k\)?
qs.s: Equating remainders gives \(P(1) = Q(2)\), so \(k^3 - 7k + 2 = 4k^2 - 8\), which simplifies to \(k^3 - 4k^2 - 7k + 10 = 0\). Factoring gives \((k - 1)(k - 5)(k + 2) = 0\), so the largest value is \(k = 5\).

qs.q: What is the positive, non-integer value of \(k\) for which 1 is a zero of \(P(x) = 2x^3 - 5kx^2 + k^2x + 2k^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(1) = 0\) gives \(2k^3 + k^2 - 5k + 2 = 0\). Testing rational roots factors this into \((k - 1)(2k - 1)(k + 2) = 0\), yielding the positive non-integer solution \(k = 1/2\).

qs.q: What is the negative real value of \(k\) for which 1 is a zero of \(P(x) = -2x^4 + kx^3 - k^2x^2 + k^3x + k^4\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(1) = 0\) gives \(k^4 + k^3 - k^2 + k - 2 = 0\). Factoring using the Rational Root Theorem yields \((k - 1)(k + 2)(k^2 + 1) = 0\), so the only negative real solution is \(k = -2\).
