qs.q: What is the smallest positive value of \(k\) for which \(2x - 1\) is a factor of \(P(x) = 64x^3 + 8kx^2 - 10k^2x + k^3\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1/2) = k^3 - 5k^2 + 2k + 8 = 0\), which factors as \((k + 1)(k - 2)(k - 4) = 0\). The positive solutions are \(2\) and \(4\), so the smallest positive value is \(2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - 3kx^3 + k^3x^2 - 10\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is 6. What is the integer value of \(k\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 4k^3 - 24k + 22 = 6\), which simplifies to \(k^3 - 6k + 4 = 0\). Factoring gives \((k - 2)(k^2 + 2k - 2) = 0\), where \(k = 2\) is the only integer solution.

qs.q: If \(P(4) = 0\) for a polynomial \(P(x)\), which binomial must be a factor of \(P(x)\)?
qs.s: According to the Factor Theorem, a polynomial \(P(x)\) has a factor \((x - a)\) if and only if \(P(a) = 0\). Since \(P(4) = 0\), \((x - 4)\) must be a factor.

qs.q: If \(x = -k\) is a root of the polynomial equation \(P(x) = 0\), which binomial must be a factor of \(P(x)\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, if \(x = r\) is a root of \(P(x) = 0\), then \((x - r)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\). Since the root is \(-k\), the factor is \(x - (-k) = x + k\).

qs.q: According to the Factor Theorem, if \((x - 7)\) is a factor of the polynomial \(P(x)\), what is the value of \(P(7)\)?
qs.s: The Factor Theorem states that \((x - a)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) if and only if \(P(a) = 0\). Therefore, if \((x - 7)\) is a factor, then \(P(7) = 0\).

qs.q: According to the Remainder Theorem, what represents the remainder when a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - c)\)?
qs.s: The Remainder Theorem states that when a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - c)\), the remainder is the constant value \(P(c)\).

qs.q: According to the Remainder Theorem, what represents the remainder when a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x + 6)\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder of dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x - a)\) is \(P(a)\). Rewriting \((x + 6)\) as \(x - (-6)\) gives a remainder of \(P(-6)\).

qs.q: If a polynomial \(P(x)\) leaves a remainder of \(5\) when divided by \((x - 3)\), and a new polynomial is defined as \(Q(x) = P(x) - 5\), which binomial must be a factor of \(Q(x)\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(3) = 5\), which implies \(Q(3) = P(3) - 5 = 0\). By the Factor Theorem, since \(Q(3) = 0\), \((x - 3)\) must be a factor of \(Q(x)\).

qs.q: If \(x = \frac{m}{n}\) is a rational root of the polynomial equation \(P(x) = 0\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive coprime integers, which binomial with integer coefficients must be a factor of \(P(x)\)?
qs.s: If \(x = \frac{m}{n}\) is a root, setting \(x - \frac{m}{n} = 0\) and clearing denominators gives the integer-coefficient factor \(nx - m\).

qs.q: According to the Remainder Theorem, what is the remainder when a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by the linear binomial \((3x - 2)\)?
qs.s: Setting the divisor \(3x - 2 = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{2}{3}\). By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: A polynomial \(P(x)\) satisfies \(P(x) = (x^2 - 4)Q(x) + 3x - 7\) for some polynomial \(Q(x)\). According to the Remainder Theorem, what is the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - 2)\)?
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - 2)\) is \(P(2)\). Evaluating gives \(P(2) = (2^2 - 4)Q(2) + 3(2) - 7 = 0 - 1 = -1\).

qs.q: If \(x = 3\) and \(x = -5\) are both roots of the polynomial equation \(P(x) = 0\), which monic quadratic expression must be a factor of \(P(x)\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \((x - 3)\) and \((x + 5)\) are both factors of \(P(x)\). Their product \((x - 3)(x + 5) = x^2 + 2x - 15\) must therefore also be a factor.

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(2x^3 - ax^2 - (a^2 - 5)x + 10\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = 2a^3 - a^3 - a^3 + 5a + 10 = 5a + 10 = 0\), which yields \(a = -2\).

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(x^3 - 2ax^2 + (a^2 + 2)x - 10\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = a^3 - 2a^3 + a^3 + 2a - 10 = 2a - 10 = 0\), which yields \(a = 5\).

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(x^3 + ax^2 - (2a^2 - 3)x - 12\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = a^3 + a^3 - 2a^3 + 3a - 12 = 3a - 12 = 0\), so \(3a = 12\) and \(a = 4\).

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(4x^3 - 3ax^2 - (a^2 + 2)x + 6\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = 4a^3 - 3a^3 - a^3 - 2a + 6 = -2a + 6 = 0\), which simplifies to \(a = 3\).

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(3x^3 - 2ax^2 - (a^2 - 1)x - 7\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = 3a^3 - 2a(a^2) - (a^2 - 1)a - 7 = a - 7 = 0\), which gives \(a = 7\).

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(2x^3 - 2ax^2 + (a - 8)x + 16\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = 2a^3 - 2a^3 + a(a - 8) + 16 = a^2 - 8a + 16 = (a - 4)^2 = 0\), which gives the single solution \(a = 4\).

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(3x^3 - (2a + 1)x^2 - x - 15\), what is the real value of \(a\)?
qs.s: Setting \(P(a) = 0\) gives \(a^3 - a^2 - a - 15 = 0\). By the Rational Root Theorem, testing divisors of \(-15\) reveals \((a - 3)(a^2 + 2a + 5) = 0\), so \(a = 3\) is the only real root.

qs.q: If \(x - 2a\) is a factor of \(x^3 - ax^2 - (2a^2 - 2)x - 20\), what is the value of \(a\)?
If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(2x^3 - (a + 1)x^2 + 2x - 8\), what is the real value of \(a\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(a) = a^3 - a^2 + 2a - 8 = 0\). Testing factors of \(-8\) with the Rational Root Theorem gives root \(a = 2\), and factoring yields \((a - 2)(a^2 + a + 4) = 0\), so \(a = 2\) is the unique real solution.

qs.q: If \(x - a\) is a factor of \(3x^4 - 2ax^3 - (a^2 - 2)x^2 - (2a + 5)x - 20\), what is the value of \(a\)?
qs.s: Substituting \(x = a\) yields \(3a^4 - 2a^4 - (a^4 - 2a^2) - (2a^2 + 5a) - 20 = -5a - 20 = 0\), which solves to \(a = -4\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(x + 2\) is a factor of \(2x^3 + (k - 1)x^2 - 5kx + 6\).
Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(x - 1\) is a factor of \(3x^4 - (k - 2)x^3 + 4kx - 17\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(1) = 3(1)^4 - (k - 2)(1)^3 + 4k(1) - 17 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(3k - 12 = 0\), so \(k = 4\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(x - 2\) is a factor of \(x^4 - 2x^3 + kx^2 - (k + 5)x + 6\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(2) = 2^4 - 2(2^3) + k(2^2) - (k + 5)(2) + 6 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(4k - 2k - 10 + 6 = 2k - 4 = 0\), so \(k = 2\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(x - 3\) is a factor of \(x^3 - (k + 1)x^2 + 2kx - 9\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(3) = 3^3 - (k + 1)(3^2) + 2k(3) - 9 = 0\). Simplifying gives \(27 - 9(k + 1) + 6k - 9 = -3k + 9 = 0\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(x + 1\) is a factor of \(3x^3 + (2k + 1)x^2 - (k - 4)x - 12\).
When \(P(x) = 2x^4 - (k + 1)x^3 + 3kx^2 - 4x - 8\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(-20\). Determine the value of \(k\).
Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(3x - 2\) is a factor of \(3x^3 + (k - 1)x^2 - (2k + 5)x + 2\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = 3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 + (k - 1)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 - (2k + 5)\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + 2 = 0\). Multiplying through by 9 yields \(8 + 4(k - 1) - 6(2k + 5) + 18 = -8k - 8 = 0\), so \(k = -1\).

qs.q: Determine the positive value of \(k\) so that \(x - 2\) is a factor of \(x^4 - k^2x^2 + 2kx + 32\).
Determine the value of \(k\) so that \(2x + 1\) is a factor of \(4x^4 - 2x^3 + (k - 5)x^2 + (2k + 3)x + 3\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 4\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 - 2\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 + (k - 5)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + (2k + 3)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) + 3 = 0\). Multiplying through by 4 gives \(1 + 1 + (k - 5) - 2(2k + 3) + 12 = -3k + 3 = 0\), so \(k = 1\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^3 + (k - 1)x^2 - 4x + 5\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is equal to the remainder when \(Q(x) = x^3 + 2kx^2 - 3x + 1\) is divided by \(x + 1\). Determine the value of \(k\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(2) = 16 + 4(k - 1) - 8 + 5 = 4k + 9\) and \(Q(-1) = -1 + 2k + 3 + 1 = 2k + 3\). Equating the two expressions gives \(4k + 9 = 2k + 3\), which yields \(2k = -6\), so \(k = -3\).

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^2 - 3x + 2\), \(x^2 - 4x + 3\), and \(x^2 - 5x + 6\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring the polynomials gives \((x - 1)(x - 2)\), \((x - 1)(x - 3)\), and \((x - 2)(x - 3)\). The least common multiple is \((x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)\), which has degree 3.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^2 - x\), \(x^2 + x\), and \(x^2 - 1\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring the polynomials gives \(x(x - 1)\), \(x(x + 1)\), and \((x - 1)(x + 1)\). The least common multiple is \(x(x - 1)(x + 1)\), which has degree 3.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^2 - 4\), \(x^2 + 2x\), and \(x^2 - 5x + 6\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring each polynomial yields \((x - 2)(x + 2)\), \(x(x + 2)\), and \((x - 2)(x - 3)\). The least common multiple is \(x(x + 2)(x - 2)(x - 3)\), which has degree 4.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^2 - 1\), \(x^2 - x\), and \(x^2 + 3x + 2\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring the polynomials gives \((x - 1)(x + 1)\), \(x(x - 1)\), and \((x + 1)(x + 2)\). The least common multiple is \(x(x - 1)(x + 1)(x + 2)\), so the lowest possible degree is 4.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^2 - 9\), \(x^2 + 3x\), and \(x^2 - 4x + 3\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring the given polynomials gives \((x - 3)(x + 3)\), \(x(x + 3)\), and \((x - 3)(x - 1)\). The least common multiple is \(x(x - 3)(x + 3)(x - 1)\), which has degree 4.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^3 - x^2\), \(x^3 - 2x^2 + x\), \(x^3 - 4x\), and \(x^2 - 3x + 2\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring completely gives \(x^2(x - 1)\), \(x(x - 1)^2\), \(x(x - 2)(x + 2)\), and \((x - 1)(x - 2)\). Taking the highest power of each prime factor yields \(x^2(x - 1)^2(x - 2)(x + 2)\), which has degree \(2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 6\).

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^3 - 2x^2 - x + 2\), \(x^2 - 4x + 4\), and \(x^2 + 2x - 3\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x - 1)(x + 1)\), \((x - 2)^2\), and \((x - 1)(x + 3)\). Taking the highest power of each unique linear factor gives \((x - 2)^2(x - 1)(x + 1)(x + 3)\), which has degree \(2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5\).

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x + 12\), \(x^3 - 2x^2 - 9x + 18\), and \(x^3 + 3x^2 - 4x - 12\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring by grouping gives \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 3)\), \((x - 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)\), and \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 3)\). The least common multiple is \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)\), which has degree 4.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(x^2 - 9\), \(x^2 - 5x + 6\), \(x^2 - 4\), and \(x^2 + x - 6\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring the polynomials gives \((x - 3)(x + 3)\), \((x - 2)(x - 3)\), \((x - 2)(x + 2)\), and \((x + 3)(x - 2)\). The least common multiple is \((x - 3)(x + 3)(x - 2)(x + 2)\), which has degree 4.

qs.q: A polynomial has among its factors \(2x^2 + 5x + 3\), \(2x^2 - x - 3\), \(4x^2 - 9\), and \(x^3 - x\). What is the lowest possible degree of the polynomial?
qs.s: Factoring yields \((2x + 3)(x + 1)\), \((2x - 3)(x + 1)\), \((2x - 3)(2x + 3)\), and \(x(x - 1)(x + 1)\). The least common multiple is \(x(x - 1)(x + 1)(2x - 3)(2x + 3)\), which consists of 5 linear factors and has degree 5.

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = x^3 + kx^2 - (2k^2 - 3)x - 18\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(f(k) = k^3 + k(k^2) - (2k^2 - 3)k - 18 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(3k - 18 = 0\), so \(k = 6\).

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 2x^3 + 3kx^2 - (5k^2 - 4)x + 4\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(2k^3 + 3k^3 - 5k^3 + 4k + 4 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(4k + 4 = 0\), so \(k = -1\).

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 3x^3 - kx^2 + (5 - 2k^2)x + 10\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(3k^3 - k^3 + (5 - 2k^2)k + 10 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(5k + 10 = 0\), so \(k = -2\).

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 3x^3 - kx^2 + (4 - 2k^2)x - 12\)?
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(f(k) = 0\), which gives \(3k^3 - k(k^2) + (4 - 2k^2)k - 12 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(4k - 12 = 0\), so \(k = 3\).

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = x^3 + kx^2 + (5 - 2k^2)x - 20\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(k^3 + k^3 + (5 - 2k^2)k - 20 = 0\). Simplifying yields \(5k - 20 = 0\), so \(k = 4\).

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 3x^3 - 3kx^2 + (k^2 - 5)x - 12\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(k^3 - 5k - 12 = 0\). Testing possible rational roots using the Rational Root Theorem gives \(k = 3\), with the remaining factor \(k^2 + 3k + 4\) having no real roots.

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = x^3 - kx^2 + (k^2 - 11)x - 20\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(k^3 - 11k - 20 = 0\). By the Rational Root Theorem, testing candidates gives the only real solution \(k = 4\), since \(k^2 + 4k + 5 = 0\) has no real roots.

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 2x^3 - 2kx^2 + (k^2 - 1)x + 6\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) simplifies to \(k^3 - k + 6 = 0\). Using the Rational Root Theorem, testing possible roots yields \(k = -2\), and the quotient \(k^2 - 2k + 3\) has no real zeros.

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 5x^3 - kx^2 + 3x - 2\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(4k^3 + 3k - 2 = 0\). Testing possible rational roots \(\pm 1, \pm 2, \pm \frac{1}{2}, \pm \frac{1}{4}\) yields \(k = \frac{1}{2}\), and the quadratic factor \(2k^2 + k + 2\) has no real roots.

qs.q: For what number \(k\) is \(k\) a zero of \(f(x) = 2x^3 - 2kx^2 + (k^2 + 1)x - 10\)?
qs.s: Setting \(f(k) = 0\) gives \(k^3 + k - 10 = 0\). Testing possible rational factors of 10 yields the only real zero \(k = 2\), since the remaining factor \(k^2 + 2k + 5\) has no real roots.

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^5 - 6x^4 - 6x^3 + 64x^2 - 27x - 90\) if \(P(-3) = P(-1) = P(3) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x + 3)(x - 3)(x + 1) = x^3 + x^2 - 9x - 9\) yields the quotient \(x^2 - 7x + 10\). Factoring the quadratic as \((x - 2)(x - 5)\) yields the complete factorization \((x + 3)(x + 1)(x - 3)(x - 2)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^5 - 6x^4 - 2x^3 + 36x^2 + x - 30\) if \(P(-2) = P(-1) = P(1) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by the product of known factors \((x + 2)(x + 1)(x - 1) = x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 2\) results in the quotient \(x^2 - 8x + 15\). Factoring this quadratic into \((x - 3)(x - 5)\) gives the complete factored form \((x + 2)(x + 1)(x - 1)(x - 3)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^5 - 3x^4 - 11x^3 + 27x^2 + 10x - 24\) if \(P(-3) = P(-1) = P(2) = 0\).
qs.s: By the factor theorem, \((x + 3)(x + 1)(x - 2) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 5x - 6\) is a factor of \(P(x)\). Dividing \(P(x)\) by this product yields the quotient \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = (x - 1)(x - 4)\), giving the full factorization \((x + 3)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x - 1)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^5 + x^4 - 15x^3 - 25x^2 + 14x + 24\) if \(P(-3) = P(-2) = P(1) = 0\).
qs.s: Multiplying the known factors gives \((x + 3)(x + 2)(x - 1) = x^3 + 4x^2 + x - 6\). Dividing \(P(x)\) by this cubic leaves \(x^2 - 3x - 4 = (x + 1)(x - 4)\), so \(P(x) = (x + 3)(x + 2)(x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^5 - 17x^3 + 12x^2 + 52x - 48\) if \(P(-2) = P(1) = P(2) = 0\).
qs.s: The known zeros correspond to the factor \((x^2 - 4)(x - 1) = x^3 - x^2 - 4x + 4\). Dividing \(P(x)\) by this cubic gives \(x^2 + x - 12 = (x + 4)(x - 3)\), so \(P(x) = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 2)(x + 4)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^5 - 6x^4 + x^3 + 36x^2 - 20x - 48\) if \(P(-1) = P(2) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x + 1)(x - 2) = x^2 - x - 2\) yields \(Q(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 - 2x + 24\). Testing factors of 24 via the rational root theorem reveals \(Q(-2) = 0\), and further division produces \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4)\), giving \((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 3)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = x^6 - 2x^5 - 20x^4 + 10x^3 + 79x^2 - 8x - 60\) if \(P(-2) = P(-1) = P(1) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x + 2)(x^2 - 1) = x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 2\) leaves the cubic \(x^3 - 4x^2 - 11x + 30\). Using the rational root theorem identifies \(x = 2\) as a root, and dividing by \((x - 2)\) gives \(x^2 - 2x - 15 = (x + 3)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = 3x^5 - 16x^4 + 9x^3 + 32x^2 - 12x - 16\) if \(P(-1) = P(1) = P(2) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x + 1)(x - 1)(x - 2) = x^3 - 2x^2 - x + 2\) produces the quotient \(3x^2 - 10x - 8\). Factoring this quadratic gives \((3x + 2)(x - 4)\), resulting in \((x + 1)(x - 1)(x - 2)(3x + 2)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = 2x^5 - 5x^4 - 11x^3 + 23x^2 + 9x - 18\) if \(P(-2) = P(1) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x + 2)(x - 1) = x^2 + x - 2\) yields \(2x^3 - 7x^2 + 9\). Applying the rational root theorem reveals the root \(x = -1\), and dividing by \((x + 1)\) leaves \(2x^2 - 9x + 9 = (x - 3)(2x - 3)\), completing the factorization.

qs.q: Find the complete factored form of \(P(x) = 2x^5 - 3x^4 - 13x^3 + 9x^2 + 11x - 6\) if \(P(-2) = P(-1) = P(1) = 0\).
qs.s: Dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x + 2)(x + 1)(x - 1) = x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 2\) gives the non-monic quadratic quotient \(2x^2 - 7x + 3\). Factoring this quadratic into \((2x - 1)(x - 3)\) gives \(P(x) = (x + 2)(x + 1)(x - 1)(2x - 1)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^5 - 2x^4 - 2x^3 + 4x^2 + x - 2\) if \(x - 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing repeatedly by \((x - 1)\) and \((x + 1)\) reduces the polynomial to \(x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1)\). Combining all linear factors gives \((x - 1)^2(x + 1)^2(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^5 - x^4 - 5x^3 + 5x^2 + 4x - 4\) if \(x - 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing the polynomial by \(x - 1\) gives the quotient \(x^4 - 5x^2 + 4\), which factors as \((x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4) = (x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\). Therefore, the complete factorization is \((x - 1)^2(x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^5 - 3x^4 + 7x^3 - 13x^2 + 12x - 4\) if \(x - 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - 1\) twice yields the cubic quotient \(x^3 - x^2 + 4x - 4\), which groups into \((x - 1)(x^2 + 4)\). Hence, the complete factorization is \((x - 1)^3(x^2 + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^5 + 2x^4 + 2x^3 + 4x^2 - 3x - 6\) if \(x + 2\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x + 2\) yields the quotient \(x^4 + 2x^2 - 3\), which factors as \((x^2 - 1)(x^2 + 3) = (x - 1)(x + 1)(x^2 + 3)\). Thus, the complete factorization is \((x + 2)(x - 1)(x + 1)(x^2 + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^5 + 3x^4 + 5x^3 + 7x^2 + 6x + 2\) if \(x + 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x + 1\) twice gives the quotient \(x^3 + x^2 + 2x + 2\), which factors by grouping into \((x + 1)(x^2 + 2)\). Thus, the polynomial factors completely as \((x + 1)^3(x^2 + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^5 + 12x^4 + x^3 - 18x^2 - 5x + 6\) if \(x - 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing successively by known and rational roots \(x = 1\), \(x = -1\), and \(x = -2\) gives \(4x^2 + 4x - 3 = (2x - 1)(2x + 3)\). Collecting all factors yields \((2x - 1)(2x + 3)(x + 2)(x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^5 + 4x^4 - 13x^3 - 18x^2 + 4x + 8\) if \(x + 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x + 1\) twice gives \(3x^3 - 2x^2 - 12x + 8\), which groups as \((3x - 2)(x^2 - 4) = (3x - 2)(x - 2)(x + 2)\). Thus, the complete factorization is \((3x - 2)(x + 1)^2(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^5 - x^4 - 5x^3 + 5x^2 - 7x + 6\) if \(x - 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - 1\) gives \(2x^4 + x^3 - 4x^2 + x - 6\), and finding the zero \(x = -2\) by the rational root theorem reduces it to \(2x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x - 3 = (2x - 3)(x^2 + 1)\). The complete factorization is \((2x - 3)(x - 1)(x + 2)(x^2 + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^5 - x^4 - 10x^3 + 5x^2 + 8x - 4\) if \(x - 2\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - 2\) gives \(2x^4 + 3x^3 - 4x^2 - 3x + 2\), and using the rational root theorem to divide by \(x - 1\) and \(x + 1\) leaves \(2x^2 + 3x - 2 = (2x - 1)(x + 2)\). The complete factorization is \((2x - 1)(x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^5 - 3x^4 + 6x^3 - 8x^2 + 3\) if \(x - 1\) is a factor.
qs.s: Dividing by \(x - 1\) twice yields \(2x^3 + x^2 + 6x + 3\), which factors by grouping into \((2x + 1)(x^2 + 3)\). Therefore, the complete factorization is \((2x + 1)(x - 1)^2(x^2 + 3)\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(a\) such that \(x - 3\) is a factor of both \(x^3 - x^2 + ax + b\) and \(x^3 - 3x^2 - ax + b\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, substituting \(x = 3\) gives \(3^3 - 3^2 + 3a + b = 0 \implies 3a + b = -18\) and \(3^3 - 3(3^2) - 3a + b = 0 \implies -3a + b = 0\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(6a = -18\), so \(a = -3\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(a\) such that \(x - 2\) is a factor of both \(x^3 - 4x^2 + ax + b\) and \(x^3 - x^2 - ax + b\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(2^3 - 4(2)^2 + 2a + b = 0 \implies 2a + b = 8\) and \(2^3 - 2^2 - 2a + b = 0 \implies -2a + b = -4\). Adding the equations yields \(2b = 4 \implies b = 2\), so \(2a + 2 = 8 \implies a = 3\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(b\) such that \(x + 2\) is a factor of both \(x^3 + x^2 + ax + b\) and \(x^3 + 2x^2 - ax + b\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, evaluating at \(x = -2\) gives \((-2)^3 + (-2)^2 - 2a + b = 0 \implies -2a + b = 4\) and \((-2)^3 + 2(-2)^2 + 2a + b = 0 \implies 2a + b = 0\). Adding both equations yields \(2b = 4\), which gives \(b = 2\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(a\) such that \(x - 1\) is a factor of both \(2x^3 - x^2 + ax + b\) and \(x^3 + 2x^2 - ax + b\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, substituting \(x = 1\) gives \(2(1)^3 - 1^2 + a + b = 0 \implies a + b = -1\) and \(1^3 + 2(1)^2 - a + b = 0 \implies -a + b = -3\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(2a = 2\), so \(a = 1\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(b\) such that \(x + 1\) is a factor of both \(x^3 + 4x^2 + ax + b\) and \(x^3 + 2x^2 - ax + b\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, substituting \(x = -1\) gives \((-1)^3 + 4(-1)^2 - a + b = 0 \implies -a + b = -3\) and \((-1)^3 + 2(-1)^2 + a + b = 0 \implies a + b = -1\). Adding the two equations gives \(2b = -4\), so \(b = -2\).

qs.q: When \(P(x) = 2x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 - 5x + 6\) is divided by \(x - 1\), the remainder is \(8\). When \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x + 2\), the remainder is \(32\). Determine the value of \(a\).
qs.s: By the Remainder Theorem, \(P(1) = 2 + a + b - 5 + 6 = 8 \implies a + b = 5\) and \(P(-2) = 32 - 8a + 4b + 10 + 6 = 32 \implies -2a + b = -4\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(3a = 9\), so \(a = 3\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(a \cdot b\) such that \(x + 2\) is a factor of both \(x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 - 4x - 8\) and \(x^3 + bx^2 + ax + 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(x = -2\) in each polynomial gives \((-2)^4 + a(-2)^3 + b(-2)^2 - 4(-2) - 8 = 0 \implies 2a - b = 4\) and \((-2)^3 + b(-2)^2 + a(-2) + 6 = 0 \implies -a + 2b = 1\). Solving the system gives \(a = 3\) and \(b = 2\), so \(a \cdot b = 6\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(a + b\) such that \(x + 3\) is a factor of both \(2x^3 + ax^2 - bx + 9\) and \(x^4 + 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 18\).
qs.s: Substituting \(x = -3\) into both polynomials yields \(2(-3)^3 + a(-3)^2 - b(-3) + 9 = 0 \implies 3a + b = 15\) and \((-3)^4 + 2(-3)^3 + a(-3)^2 + b(-3) - 18 = 0 \implies 3a - b = -3\). Adding and subtracting the equations gives \(a = 2\) and \(b = 9\), so \(a + b = 11\).

qs.q: Determine the value of \(a + b\) if both \(x - 2\) and \(x + 3\) are factors of \(P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 - 16x - 12\).
qs.s: By the Factor Theorem, \(P(2) = 16 + 8a + 4b - 32 - 12 = 0 \implies 2a + b = 7\) and \(P(-3) = 81 - 27a + 9b + 48 - 12 = 0 \implies -3a + b = -13\). Solving this system gives \(a = 4\) and \(b = -1\), so \(a + b = 3\).

qs.q: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^4 - 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 12\) is divisible by \(x^2 - 4\). Determine the value of \(b\).
qs.s: Since \(x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)\), both \(x - 2\) and \(x + 2\) are factors of \(P(x)\), giving \(P(2) = 4a + 2b - 12 = 0 \implies 2a + b = 6\) and \(P(-2) = 4a - 2b + 20 = 0 \implies 2a - b = -10\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(2b = 16\), so \(b = 8\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of length \(x\) from each corner of a 14 cm by 10 cm piece of cardboard, and then folding up the sides with \(x \ge 2\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(96\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(14 - 2x)(10 - 2x) = 96\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 12x^2 + 35x - 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x - 3)(x - 8) = 0\), and since \(x \ge 2\text{ cm}\) and \(x < 5\text{ cm}\), the required square size is 3 cm.

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner of a 10 cm by 8 cm piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides with \(x \ge 1.5\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(48\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(10 - 2x)(8 - 2x) = 48\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 9x^2 + 20x - 12 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 6) = 0\); since \(x \ge 1.5\text{ cm}\) and \(x < 4\text{ cm}\), the required cut size is 2 cm.

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of length \(x\) from each corner of a 20 cm by 16 cm sheet of cardboard, and then folding up the sides with \(x \ge 3\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(384\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(20 - 2x)(16 - 2x) = 384\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 18x^2 + 80x - 96 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x - 4)(x - 12) = 0\); since \(x \ge 3\text{ cm}\) and \(x < 8\text{ cm}\), the square size must be 4 cm.

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is made by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner of an 18 cm by 12 cm sheet of metal, then folding up the sides with \(x \ge 2\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to achieve a volume of \(160\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(18 - 2x)(12 - 2x) = 160\), simplifying to \(x^3 - 15x^2 + 54x - 40 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 1)(x - 4)(x - 10) = 0\); with \(x \ge 2\text{ cm}\) and \(x < 6\text{ cm}\), the solution is 4 cm.

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is formed by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner of a 16 cm by 14 cm sheet of plastic and folding up the sides with \(x \le 2.5\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(240\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume is given by \(x(16 - 2x)(14 - 2x) = 240\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 15x^2 + 56x - 60 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x - 3)(x - 10) = 0\), and applying \(x \le 2.5\text{ cm}\) yields \(x = 2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner of a 21 cm by 16 cm rectangular sheet of cardboard, then folding up the sides with \(x \le 3\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(440\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation \(x(21 - 2x)(16 - 2x) = 440\) simplifies to \(2x^3 - 37x^2 + 168x - 220 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 5)(x^2 - 16x + 44) = 0\), where the quadratic factor yields roots \(8 \pm 2\sqrt{5} \approx 3.53\text{ cm}\) and \(12.47\text{ cm}\), so \(x \le 3\text{ cm}\) leaves \(x = 2.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is formed by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner of a 25 cm by 19 cm rectangular sheet of sheet metal, then folding up the sides with \(x \le 3.5\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to obtain a volume of \(756\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The equation \(x(25 - 2x)(19 - 2x) = 756\) leads to \(4x^3 - 88x^2 + 475x - 756 = 0\). Testing rational zeros gives \((2x - 7)(2x^2 - 37x + 108) = 0\), whose remaining roots \(\frac{37 \pm \sqrt{505}}{4} \approx 3.63\text{ cm}\) and \(14.87\text{ cm}\) are both \(> 3.5\text{ cm}\), leaving \(x = 3.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is made by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner of a 26 cm by 18 cm rectangular sheet of metal, then folding up the sides with \(x \ge 3.5\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(720\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The equation \(x(26 - 2x)(18 - 2x) = 720\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 22x^2 + 117x - 180 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 3)(x - 4)(x - 15) = 0\). Since \(x < 9\text{ cm}\) and \(x \ge 3.5\text{ cm}\), the solution is \(x = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of length \(x\) from each corner of a 23 cm by 15 cm rectangle, and then folding up the sides with \(x \le 3\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(418\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(23 - 2x)(15 - 2x) = 418\), which simplifies to \(4x^3 - 76x^2 + 345x - 418 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(4x^2 - 68x + 209) = 0\), whose quadratic roots are \(\frac{17 \pm 4\sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 4.03\text{ cm}\) and \(12.97\text{ cm}\); applying \(x \le 3\text{ cm}\) yields \(x = 2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of length \(x\) from each corner of a 30 cm by 24 cm rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides with \(x \ge 4.5\text{ cm}\). What size square must be cut to have a volume of \(1296\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation \(x(30 - 2x)(24 - 2x) = 1296\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 27x^2 + 180x - 324 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 3)(x - 6)(x - 18) = 0\). Discarding \(x = 18\text{ cm}\) (exceeds sheet limits) and \(x = 3\text{ cm}\) (since \(x \ge 4.5\text{ cm}\)), the correct cut size is 6 cm.

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(16\text{ cm}\) by \(10\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What is the side length of the square that must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(144\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(16 - 2x)(10 - 2x) = 144\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 13x^2 + 40x - 36 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)^2(x - 9) = 0\), so the only physically possible solution in the domain \(0 < x < 5\) is \(x = 2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(16\text{ cm}\) by \(12\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What integer length must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(128\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(x(16 - 2x)(12 - 2x) = 128\) gives \(x^3 - 14x^2 + 48x - 32 = 0\). Factoring out \((x - 4)\) leaves \(x^2 - 10x + 8 = 0\), whose roots are irrational, making \(x = 4\text{ cm}\) the only integer solution.

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of an \(11\text{ cm}\) by \(9\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What integer length must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(63\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(x(11 - 2x)(9 - 2x) = 63\) results in \(4x^3 - 40x^2 + 99x - 63 = 0\). Factoring out \((x - 1)\) gives \((x - 1)(4x^2 - 36x + 63) = 0\), leaving \(x = 1\text{ cm}\) as the only integer solution.

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(14\text{ cm}\) by \(10\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What is the length of the square that must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(96\text{ cm}^3\) (\(x\) must be greater than \(2\))?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(14 - 2x)(10 - 2x) = 96\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 12x^2 + 35x - 24 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 1)(x - 3)(x - 8) = 0\), and since \(x > 2\) and \(x < 5\), the required length is \(x = 3\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(22\text{ cm}\) by \(16\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What integer length must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(360\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation \(x(22 - 2x)(16 - 2x) = 360\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 19x^2 + 88x - 90 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x^2 - 14x + 18) = 0\), which yields the unique integer solution \(x = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(15\text{ cm}\) by \(11\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What rational length \(x\) must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(144\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The equation is \(x(15 - 2x)(11 - 2x) = 144\), which simplifies to \(4x^3 - 52x^2 + 165x - 144 = 0\). Testing rational zeros gives \((2x - 3)(2x^2 - 23x + 48) = 0\), yielding the only rational solution \(x = \frac{3}{2}\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(30\text{ cm}\) by \(20\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What integer length \(x\) must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(1056\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The volume equation \(x(30 - 2x)(20 - 2x) = 1056\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 25x^2 + 150x - 264 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x^2 - 21x + 66) = 0\), where the quadratic factor has irrational roots, leaving \(x = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(36\text{ cm}\) by \(24\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What integer length \(x\) must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(1728\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: The equation \(x(36 - 2x)(24 - 2x) = 1728\) reduces to \(x^3 - 30x^2 + 216x - 432 = 0\). Factoring out \((x - 6)\) leaves \(x^2 - 24x + 72 = 0\), whose roots are irrational, so the only integer solution is \(x = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(32\text{ cm}\) by \(22\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard, then folding up the sides. What integer length \(x\) must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(1320\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(x(32 - 2x)(22 - 2x) = 1320\) gives \(x^3 - 27x^2 + 176x - 330 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 5)(x^2 - 22x + 66) = 0\), which gives \(x = 5\text{ cm}\) as the only integer solution.

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(21\text{ cm}\) by \(21\text{ cm}\) square piece of sheet metal, then folding up the sides. What rational length \(x\) must be cut from each corner if the volume of the box is \(640\text{ cm}^3\)?
qs.s: Setting \(x(21 - 2x)^2 = 640\) yields \(4x^3 - 84x^2 + 441x - 640 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 5)(2x^2 - 37x + 128) = 0\), which gives the unique rational root \(x = \frac{5}{2}\text{ cm}\).

exercises.name: Geometric dimensions from volume or area

qs.q: A rectangular storage container is built such that its length is \(1\text{ m}\) longer than its width, and its height is \(4\text{ times}\) its width. Find the width of the container if its volume is \(600\text{ m}^3\).
qs.s: The volume is \(w(w + 1)(4w) = 600\), which simplifies to \(w^3 + w^2 - 150 = 0\). Testing integer factors yields \(w = 5\text{ m}\), with the quadratic factor having no real roots.

qs.q: A vitamin capsule is designed in the shape of a cylinder with hemispherical ends. The total length of the capsule is \(11\text{ mm}\), and its volume is \(81\pi\text{ mm}^3\). Find the radius of the capsule.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(\pi r^2(11 - 2r) + \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = 81\pi\), which reduces to \(2r^3 - 33r^2 + 243 = 0\). Testing factors yields \(r = 3\text{ mm}\), as the other positive root is too large for the capsule's length.

qs.q: A grain storage bin has the shape of a cylinder topped by a cone. The height of the cone is equal to the radius of the bin, and the overall height of the bin is \(7\text{ m}\). Find the radius if the total volume is \(\frac{208\pi}{3}\text{ m}^3\).
qs.s: The volume is given by \(\pi r^2(7 - r) + \frac{1}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{208\pi}{3}\), which simplifies to \(2r^3 - 21r^2 + 208 = 0\). Factoring out \((r - 4)\) yields \(r = 4\text{ m}\), since the other positive root exceeds the total height.

qs.q: A water tower has the shape of a cylinder topped by a hemisphere. The overall height of the tower is \(14\text{ m}\), and its total volume is \(432\pi\text{ m}^3\). Find the radius of the water tower.
qs.s: The volume formula gives \(\pi r^2(14 - r) + \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = 432\pi\), leading to \(r^3 - 42r^2 + 1296 = 0\). Testing factors gives \(r = 6\text{ m}\), as the other positive root is greater than the total height.

qs.q: A storage silo is in the shape of a cylinder topped by a hemisphere. The overall height of the silo is \(9\text{ m}\), and its total volume is \(\frac{100\pi}{3}\text{ m}^3\). Find the radius of the silo.
qs.s: The total volume is \(\pi r^2(9 - r) + \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{100\pi}{3}\), which simplifies to \(r^3 - 27r^2 + 100 = 0\). Factoring gives \(r = 2\text{ m}\), since the other positive root exceeds the silo's overall height.

qs.q: A storage facility is in the shape of a cylinder topped by a right circular cone. The height of the cone is twice the radius of its base, and the overall height of the facility is \(30\text{ m}\). If the total volume is \(792\pi\text{ m}^3\), find the height of the cylindrical section.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(\pi r^2(30 - 2r) + \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(2r) = 792\pi\), which simplifies to \(2r^3 - 45r^2 + 1188 = 0\). This yields \(r = 6\text{ m}\), so the height of the cylinder is \(30 - 2(6) = 18\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A solid metal cylinder of height \(15\text{ cm}\) has a hemispherical cavity drilled into its top face. The cavity has the same radius as the cylinder. If the remaining volume of the cylinder is \(396\pi\text{ cm}^3\), find the radius of the cylinder.
qs.s: The remaining volume is \(\pi r^2(15) - \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = 396\pi\), which simplifies to \(2r^3 - 45r^2 + 1188 = 0\). Testing factors gives the radius \(r = 6\text{ cm}\), as the other positive root exceeds the cylinder height.

qs.q: A grain silo consists of a cylindrical main body topped by a hemisphere. The height of the cylindrical section is \(3\text{ m}\) greater than twice the radius of the silo. If the total volume of the silo is \(99\pi\text{ m}^3\), find the overall height of the silo.
qs.s: The volume is \(V = \pi r^2(2r + 3) + \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = 99\pi\), which simplifies to \(8r^3 + 9r^2 - 297 = 0\). Solving gives \(r = 3\text{ m}\), so the overall height is \((2(3) + 3) + 3 = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular shipping crate has a length that is \(3\text{ m}\) less than twice its width, and a height that is \(2\text{ m}\) greater than its width. If the volume of the crate is \(432\text{ m}^3\), find the length of the crate.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(w(2w - 3)(w + 2) = 432\), which expands to \(2w^3 + w^2 - 6w - 432 = 0\). Solving gives width \(w = 6\text{ m}\), so the length is \(2(6) - 3 = 9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A storage silo is in the shape of a cylinder topped by a hemisphere. The overall height of the silo is \(21\text{ m}\), and its total volume is \(684\pi\text{ m}^3\). Find the height of the cylindrical section of the silo.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(\pi r^2(21 - r) + \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = 684\pi\), which simplifies to \(r^3 - 63r^2 + 2052 = 0\). Solving gives \(r = 6\text{ m}\), so the height of the cylindrical section is \(21 - 6 = 15\text{ m}\).

exercises.name: Geometric dimensions from volume or area

qs.q: A right-triangular garden has a hypotenuse that is \(1\text{ m}\) longer than one of its perpendicular sides. If the area of the garden is \(84\text{ m}^2\), find the length of the longer perpendicular side.
qs.s: With hypotenuse \(c = a + 1\), we have \(a = \frac{b^2 - 1}{2}\), and the area equation \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 84\) simplifies to \(b^3 - b - 336 = 0\). Solving yields \(b = 7\text{ m}\), so the longer leg is \(a = \frac{7^2 - 1}{2} = 24\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular flag has a hypotenuse that is \(4\text{ cm}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the flag is \(96\text{ cm}^2\), find the length of its shorter leg.
qs.s: Let \(c = a + 4\), which gives \(a = \frac{b^2 - 16}{8}\). The area equation \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 96\) gives \(b^3 - 16b - 1536 = 0\), giving \(b = 12\text{ cm}\) and \(a = 16\text{ cm}\), so the shorter leg is \(12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular sail has a hypotenuse that is \(2\text{ m}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the sail is \(24\text{ m}^2\), find the length of its shorter leg.
qs.s: Let hypotenuse \(c = a + 2\), giving \(a = \frac{b^2 - 4}{4}\). The area equation \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 24\) leads to \(b^3 - 4b - 192 = 0\), which factors with root \(b = 6\text{ m}\), giving legs of \(6\text{ m}\) and \(8\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular sign has a hypotenuse that is \(1\text{ cm}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the sign is \(30\text{ cm}^2\), find the length of its hypotenuse.
qs.s: Let legs be \(a\) and \(b\) with hypotenuse \(c = a + 1\), so \(b^2 = (a+1)^2 - a^2 = 2a + 1\), which gives \(a = \frac{b^2 - 1}{2}\). Substituting into the area formula \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 30\) gives \(b^3 - b - 120 = 0\), yielding \(b = 5\text{ cm}\), \(a = 12\text{ cm}\), and hypotenuse \(c = 13\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular support brace has a hypotenuse that is \(3\text{ cm}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the brace is \(54\text{ cm}^2\), find the length of its hypotenuse.
qs.s: Let \(c = a + 3\), so \(b^2 = 6a + 9\) and \(a = \frac{b^2 - 9}{6}\). Substituting into \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 54\) gives \(b^3 - 9b - 648 = 0\), which yields \(b = 9\text{ cm}\), \(a = 12\text{ cm}\), and hypotenuse \(c = 15\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular metal plate has a hypotenuse that is \(2\text{ cm}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the plate is \(120\text{ cm}^2\), find the difference between the lengths of its two legs.
qs.s: Setting \(c = a + 2\) gives \(a = \frac{b^2 - 4}{4}\), and area \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 120\) yields \(b^3 - 4b - 960 = 0\). Solving gives \(b = 10\text{ cm}\) and \(a = 24\text{ cm}\), so the difference between the legs is \(24 - 10 = 14\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular plot of land has a hypotenuse that is \(2\text{ m}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the plot is \(60\text{ m}^2\), find its perimeter.
qs.s: Setting \(c = a + 2\) gives \(a = \frac{b^2 - 4}{4}\), and the area equation \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 60\) yields \(b^3 - 4b - 480 = 0\), which gives \(b = 8\text{ m}\), \(a = 15\text{ m}\), and \(c = 17\text{ m}\). The perimeter is \(8 + 15 + 17 = 40\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular park has a hypotenuse that is \(1\text{ m}\) longer than one of its boundary legs. If the area of the park is \(180\text{ m}^2\), find its perimeter.
qs.s: With \(c = a + 1\), we find \(a = \frac{b^2 - 1}{2}\), and the area equation gives \(b^3 - b - 720 = 0\), which solves to \(b = 9\text{ m}\). This gives legs \(9\text{ m}\) and \(40\text{ m}\) with hypotenuse \(41\text{ m}\), yielding a perimeter of \(9 + 40 + 41 = 90\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular sail has a hypotenuse that is \(3\text{ m}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the sail is \(270\text{ m}^2\), find the length of the hypotenuse.
qs.s: Setting \(c = a + 3\) gives \(a = \frac{b^2 - 9}{6}\), and the area equation \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 270\) leads to \(b^3 - 9b - 3240 = 0\). Solving gives \(b = 15\text{ m}\) and \(a = 36\text{ m}\), so the hypotenuse is \(c = 36 + 3 = 39\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A right-triangular courtyard has a hypotenuse that is \(4\text{ m}\) longer than one of its legs. If the area of the courtyard is \(240\text{ m}^2\), find its perimeter.
qs.s: Setting \(c = a + 4\) yields \(a = \frac{b^2 - 16}{8}\), and the area equation \(\frac{1}{2}ab = 240\) simplifies to \(b^3 - 16b - 3840 = 0\). Solving yields \(b = 16\text{ m}\), \(a = 30\text{ m}\), and \(c = 34\text{ m}\), giving a perimeter of \(16 + 30 + 34 = 80\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage container has dimensions 2 m by 3 m by 4 m. If each dimension is increased by the same amount, how much must you increase these dimensions to make the volume 5 times larger?
qs.s: The initial volume is \(2 \times 3 \times 4 = 24\text{ m}^3\), so the target volume is \(5 \times 24 = 120\text{ m}^3\). Expanding \((2+x)(3+x)(4+x) = 120\) gives \(x^3 + 9x^2 + 26x - 96 = 0\), which factors as \((x-2)(x^2+11x+48) = 0\), giving \(x = 2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A gift box measures 1 m by 2 m by 5 m. If each side is increased by the same amount, how much must you increase these sides to make the volume 16 times larger?
qs.s: The original volume is \(1 \times 2 \times 5 = 10\text{ m}^3\), so the target volume is \(16 \times 10 = 160\text{ m}^3\). The equation \((1+x)(2+x)(5+x) = 160\) expands to \(x^3 + 8x^2 + 17x - 150 = 0\), which factors as \((x-3)(x^2+11x+50) = 0\), giving \(x = 3\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular box is 1 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm. If each dimension is increased by the same amount, how much must each side be increased to make the volume 9 times larger?
qs.s: The original volume is \(1 \times 2 \times 4 = 8\text{ cm}^3\), so the new volume must be \(9 \times 8 = 72\text{ cm}^3\). Setting \((1+x)(2+x)(4+x) = 72\) gives \(x^3 + 7x^2 + 14x - 64 = 0\), which factors as \((x-2)(x^2+9x+32) = 0\), yielding \(x = 2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A box is 3 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm. If each side is increased by the same length, how much must you increase these sides to make the volume 2 times larger?
qs.s: The original volume is \(3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60\text{ cm}^3\), so the new volume is \(2 \times 60 = 120\text{ cm}^3\). Expanding \((3+x)(4+x)(5+x) = 120\) yields \(x^3 + 12x^2 + 47x - 60 = 0\), which factors as \((x-1)(x^2+13x+60) = 0\), giving \(x = 1\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A crate has dimensions 1 ft by 4 ft by 5 ft. If each dimension is increased by the same amount, how much must each dimension be increased to make the volume 3 times larger?
qs.s: The initial volume is \(1 \times 4 \times 5 = 20\text{ ft}^3\), so the desired volume is \(3 \times 20 = 60\text{ ft}^3\). Setting \((1+x)(4+x)(5+x) = 60\) simplifies to \(x^3 + 10x^2 + 29x - 40 = 0\), whose only positive root is \(x = 1\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage bin is 1 m by 5 m by 6 m. If each side is increased by the same amount, how much must each side be increased to make the volume 22 times larger?
qs.s: The initial volume is \(1 \times 5 \times 6 = 30\text{ m}^3\), so the target volume is \(22 \times 30 = 660\text{ m}^3\). Setting \((1+x)(5+x)(6+x) = 660\) gives \(x^3 + 12x^2 + 41x - 630 = 0\), which factors as \((x-5)(x^2+17x+126) = 0\), giving \(x = 5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A shipping crate is 1 ft by 4 ft by 8 ft. If each dimension is increased by the same amount, how much must you increase these dimensions to make the volume 15 times larger?
qs.s: The original volume is \(1 \times 4 \times 8 = 32\text{ ft}^3\), so the new volume is \(15 \times 32 = 480\text{ ft}^3\). Expanding \((1+x)(4+x)(8+x) = 480\) leads to \(x^3 + 13x^2 + 44x - 448 = 0\), which factors as \((x-4)(x^2+17x+112) = 0\), giving \(x = 4\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A solid block has dimensions 1 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm. If each side is increased by the same length, how much must each side be increased to make the volume 32 times larger?
qs.s: The initial volume is \(1 \times 3 \times 5 = 15\text{ cm}^3\), giving a new volume of \(32 \times 15 = 480\text{ cm}^3\). The equation \((1+x)(3+x)(5+x) = 480\) expands to \(x^3 + 9x^2 + 23x - 465 = 0\), which factors as \((x-5)(x^2+14x+93) = 0\), giving \(x = 5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A metal container is 1 m by 2 m by 6 m. If each dimension is increased by the same amount, how much must you increase these dimensions to make the volume 25 times larger?
qs.s: The initial volume is \(1 \times 2 \times 6 = 12\text{ m}^3\), so the target volume is \(25 \times 12 = 300\text{ m}^3\). Solving \((1+x)(2+x)(6+x) = 300\) simplifies to \(x^3 + 9x^2 + 20x - 288 = 0\), which factors as \((x-4)(x^2+13x+72) = 0\), yielding \(x = 4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A box has dimensions 2 m by 3 m by 6 m. If each dimension is increased by the same amount, how much must you increase these dimensions to make the volume 24 times larger?
qs.s: The original volume is \(2 \times 3 \times 6 = 36\text{ m}^3\), so the scaled volume is \(24 \times 36 = 864\text{ m}^3\). Expanding \((2+x)(3+x)(6+x) = 864\) yields \(x^3 + 11x^2 + 36x - 828 = 0\), which factors as \((x-6)(x^2+17x+138) = 0\), giving \(x = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A box measures 1 m × 2 m × 3 m. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 4 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(2)(3) = 6 m³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3) = 24 gives x³ + 6x² + 11x - 18 = 0, which factors as (x - 1)(x² + 7x + 18) = 0, yielding x = 1 m.

qs.q: A storage container measures 1 m × 2 m × 2 m. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 12 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(2)(2) = 4 m³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 2)² = 48 gives x³ + 5x² + 8x - 44 = 0, which factors as (x - 2)(x² + 7x + 22) = 0, giving x = 2 m.

qs.q: A gift box measures 1 cm × 2 cm × 4 cm. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 9 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(2)(4) = 8 cm³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 4) = 72 gives x³ + 7x² + 14x - 64 = 0, which factors as (x - 2)(x² + 9x + 32) = 0, yielding x = 2 cm.

qs.q: A rectangular block measures 2 cm × 3 cm × 4 cm. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 5 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 2(3)(4) = 24 cm³. Setting (x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4) = 120 gives x³ + 9x² + 26x - 96 = 0, which factors as (x - 2)(x² + 11x + 48) = 0, yielding x = 2 cm.

qs.q: A wooden crate measures 2 ft × 2 ft × 3 ft. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 3 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 2(2)(3) = 12 ft³. Setting (x + 2)²(x + 3) = 36 gives x³ + 7x² + 16x - 24 = 0, which factors as (x - 1)(x² + 8x + 24) = 0, giving x = 1 ft.

qs.q: A packing crate measures 1 ft × 3 ft × 8 ft. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 11 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(3)(8) = 24 ft³, so the new volume is 264 ft³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 3)(x + 8) = 264 gives x³ + 12x² + 35x - 240 = 0, which factors as (x - 3)(x² + 15x + 80) = 0, yielding x = 3 ft.

qs.q: A rectangular storage unit measures 1 m × 3 m × 4 m. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 36 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(3)(4) = 12 m³, so the new volume is 432 m³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 3)(x + 4) = 432 gives x³ + 8x² + 19x - 420 = 0, which factors as (x - 5)(x² + 13x + 84) = 0, yielding x = 5 m.

qs.q: A small container measures 1 cm × 2 cm × 5 cm. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 27 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(2)(5) = 10 cm³, so the new volume is 270 cm³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 5) = 270 gives x³ + 8x² + 17x - 260 = 0, which factors as (x - 4)(x² + 12x + 65) = 0, giving x = 4 cm.

qs.q: A rectangular tank measures 2 m × 3 m × 5 m. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 8 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 2(3)(5) = 30 m³, so the new volume is 240 m³. Setting (x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 5) = 240 gives x³ + 10x² + 31x - 210 = 0, which factors as (x - 3)(x² + 13x + 70) = 0, giving x = 3 m.

qs.q: A metal casing measures 1 in × 4 in × 5 in. Each dimension is increased by the same amount. How much is this increase if the new volume is 18 times the original volume?
qs.s: The original volume is 1(4)(5) = 20 in³, so the new volume is 360 in³. Setting (x + 1)(x + 4)(x + 5) = 360 gives x³ + 10x² + 29x - 340 = 0, which factors as (x - 4)(x² + 14x + 85) = 0, giving x = 4 in.

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a piece of cardboard measuring 6 in. × 7 in. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 15 in³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: Setting up the volume gives \(x(6 - 2x)(7 - 2x) = 15\), which simplifies to \(4x^3 - 26x^2 + 42x - 15 = 0\). Factoring out \((2x - 1)\) gives \((2x - 1)(2x^2 - 12x + 15) = 0\), yielding the solution \(x = 0.5\text{ in.}\)

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a piece of cardboard measuring 7 in. × 9 in. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 30 in³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(7 - 2x)(9 - 2x) = 30\), which expands to \(4x^3 - 32x^2 + 63x - 30 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(4x^2 - 24x + 15) = 0\), so the only rational root is \(x = 2\text{ in.}\)

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a sheet of cardboard measuring 8 cm × 9 cm. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 45 cm³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The box volume is \(x(8 - 2x)(9 - 2x) = 45\), which simplifies to \(4x^3 - 34x^2 + 72x - 45 = 0\). Factoring yields \((2x - 3)(2x^2 - 14x + 15) = 0\), giving the rational solution \(x = 1.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a piece of cardboard measuring 8 in. × 9 in. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 18 in³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The volume is given by \(x(8 - 2x)(9 - 2x) = 18\), which simplifies to \(2x^3 - 17x^2 + 36x - 9 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 3)(2x^2 - 11x + 3) = 0\), so the only rational solution is \(x = 3\text{ in.}\)

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a sheet of metal measuring 7 cm × 10 cm. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 40 cm³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(7 - 2x)(10 - 2x) = 40\), which simplifies to \(2x^3 - 17x^2 + 35x - 20 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 1)(2x^2 - 15x + 20) = 0\), giving the rational solution \(x = 1\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a piece of cardboard measuring 16 in. × 22 in. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 448 in³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(16 - 2x)(22 - 2x) = 448\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 19x^2 + 88x - 112 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x^2 - 15x + 28) = 0\), whose only rational root is \(x = 4\text{ in.}\)

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a sheet of cardboard measuring 15 cm × 20 cm. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 375 cm³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The equation \(x(15 - 2x)(20 - 2x) = 375\) simplifies to \(4x^3 - 70x^2 + 300x - 375 = 0\). Factoring gives \((2x - 5)(2x^2 - 30x + 75) = 0\), so the rational cut length is \(x = 2.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a piece of cardboard measuring 18 in. × 22 in. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 480 in³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: Setting \(x(18 - 2x)(22 - 2x) = 480\) leads to \(x^3 - 20x^2 + 99x - 120 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 5)(x^2 - 15x + 24) = 0\), which yields the rational root \(x = 5\text{ in.}\)

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a piece of metal measuring 20 cm × 24 cm. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 576 cm³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x(20 - 2x)(24 - 2x) = 576\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 22x^2 + 120x - 144 = 0\). Factoring yields \((x - 6)(x^2 - 16x + 24) = 0\), so the only rational root is \(x = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open-top box is made from a sheet of metal measuring 15 cm × 22 cm. Cutting out squares from each corner and folding the edges up makes a box with a volume of 420 cm³. How large a square must be cut from each corner?
qs.s: The volume is modeled by \(x(15 - 2x)(22 - 2x) = 420\), which simplifies to \(2x^3 - 37x^2 + 165x - 210 = 0\). Factoring produces \((2x - 7)(x^2 - 15x + 30) = 0\), so the square cut is \(x = 3.5\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 60x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 3x^2 + 57x + 18\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit occurs when \(P(x) = R(x) - C(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 6x^2 - 9x + 54) > 0\). Factoring gives \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)(x - 6)(x + 3) > 0\), which yields \(3 < x < 6\) for positive production levels.

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 100x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 5x^2 + 103x + 54\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit requires \(P(x) = R(x) - C(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 12x^2 + 9x + 162) > 0\). Factoring gives \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 6)(x - 9)(x + 3) > 0\), which is positive on the interval \(6 < x < 9\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 90x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 4x^2 + 72x + 72\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Setting \(P(x) = R(x) - C(x) > 0\) yields \(-\frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 9x^2 - 54x + 216) > 0\). Factoring into \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)(x - 12)(x + 6) > 0\) gives the profit range \(3 < x < 12\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 110x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 5x^2 + 98x + 144\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit requires \(P(x) = R(x) - C(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 12x^2 - 36x + 432) > 0\). Factoring yields \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 6)(x - 12)(x + 6) > 0\), so the company makes a profit when \(6 < x < 12\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 80x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 3x^2 + 65x + 54\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit occurs when \(P(x) = R(x) - C(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 6x^2 - 45x + 162) > 0\). Factoring the cubic gives \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 3)(x - 9)(x + 6) > 0\), so the company is profitable for \(3 < x < 9\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 300x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{3}x^3 - 11x^2 + 225x + 2250\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit requires \(P(x) = -\frac{1}{3}(x^3 - 30x^2 - 225x + 6750) > 0\). Testing factors of 6750 gives roots \(15\), \(30\), and \(-15\), so the cubic factors as \(-\frac{1}{3}(x - 15)(x - 30)(x + 15) > 0\), yielding \(15 < x < 30\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 200x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{2}x^3 - 10x^2 + 140x + 800\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Setting \(P(x) = -\frac{1}{2}(x^3 - 18x^2 - 120x + 1600) > 0\), we find the positive roots \(x = 8\) and \(x = 20\), and negative root \(x = -10\). Factoring gives \(-\frac{1}{2}(x - 8)(x - 20)(x + 10) > 0\), so profit occurs when \(8 < x < 20\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 50x - x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{2}{3}x^3 - 4x^2 + 41x + 18\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Setting \(P(x) = R(x) - C(x) > 0\) gives \(-\frac{1}{3}(2x^3 - 9x^2 - 27x + 54) > 0\). Factoring by rational roots yields \(-\frac{1}{3}(2x - 3)(x - 6)(x + 3) > 0\), which is positive for \(\frac{3}{2} < x < 6\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 150x - 2x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = x^3 - 13x^2 + 140x + 200\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit requires \(P(x) = -(x^3 - 11x^2 - 10x + 200) > 0\). Factoring the monic cubic via the Rational Root Theorem gives \(-(x - 5)(x - 10)(x + 4) > 0\), which is positive on \(5 < x < 10\).

qs.q: The production of \(x\) units produces revenue \(R(x) = 120x - 2x^2\) and costs \(C(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^3 - 4x^2 + 100x + 96\). For what range of production \(x\) does the company make a profit?
qs.s: Profit occurs when \(P(x) = -\frac{1}{4}(x^3 - 8x^2 - 80x + 384) > 0\). Using synthetic division, the polynomial factors into \(-\frac{1}{4}(x - 4)(x - 12)(x + 8) > 0\), giving \(4 < x < 12\).

exercises.name: Geometric dimensions from volume or area

qs.q: A rectangular storage bin has a length that is twice its width, and a height that is \(1\text{ m}\) less than its width. If the volume of the bin is \(96\text{ m}^3\), find the width of the bin.
qs.s: Setting the volume to \(V = (2x)(x)(x - 1) = 96\) yields \(x^3 - x^2 - 48 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x^2 + 3x + 12) = 0\), so the width is \(4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A feeding trough has the shape of a horizontal triangular prism. Its vertical cross-section is an inverted triangle with a height equal to half of its top width \(x\). The length of the trough is \(2\text{ m}\) longer than its top width. If the trough has a volume of \(4\text{ m}^3\), find its top width \(x\).
qs.s: The volume is given by \(\frac{1}{2}(x)\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)(x + 2) = 4\), which simplifies to \(x^3 + 2x^2 - 16 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x^2 + 4x + 8) = 0\), so the top width is \(2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A storage shed is built in the shape of a cube with a triangular prism forming the roof. The total height of the shed is \(7\text{ m}\) and its total volume is \(18\text{ m}^3\). Find the side length of the cube base.
qs.s: The volume is given by \(V = x^3 + \frac{1}{2}x^2(7 - x) = 18\), which simplifies to \(x^3 + 7x^2 - 36 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)(x + 3)(x + 6) = 0\), so the positive side length is \(2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is formed from a \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(16\text{ cm}\) sheet of cardboard by cutting a square of side length \(x\) from each corner and folding up the sides. If the volume of the box is \(144\text{ cm}^3\), find the value of \(x\).
qs.s: The box volume is \(x(16 - 2x)(10 - 2x) = 144\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 13x^2 + 40x - 36 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 2)^2(x - 9) = 0\), and since \(x < 5\) for positive dimensions, \(x = 2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A storage structure is built in the shape of a cube topped with a right square pyramid roof that has the same base. The total height of the structure is \(7\text{ m}\), and its total volume is \(39\text{ m}^3\). Find the side length of the cube.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x^3 + \frac{1}{3}x^2(7 - x) = 39\), which simplifies to \(2x^3 + 7x^2 - 117 = 0\). Testing factors gives the real root \(x = 3\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A storage warehouse is built with a square base of side length \(x\text{ m}\). The height of the rectangular walls is \(2\text{ m}\) greater than the base side length, and the roof is a right square pyramid whose height is \(3\text{ m}\) less than the base side length. If the total volume of the warehouse is \(324\text{ m}^3\), find the total height of the warehouse.
qs.s: The volume is \(x^2(x + 2) + \frac{1}{3}x^2(x - 3) = 324\), which simplifies to \(4x^3 + 3x^2 - 972 = 0\). Factoring yields \(x = 6\text{ m}\), so the total height of the warehouse is \((6 + 2) + (6 - 3) = 11\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A closed rectangular shipping crate has a length that is \(2\text{ m}\) greater than its width \(x\), and a height that is \(1\text{ m}\) greater than its width. If the volume of the crate is \(120\text{ m}^3\), find the total outside surface area of the crate.
qs.s: The volume equation \(x(x + 1)(x + 2) = 120\) simplifies to \(x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x - 120 = 0\), giving \(x = 4\text{ m}\). With dimensions \(4\text{ m} \times 6\text{ m} \times 5\text{ m}\), the total surface area is \(2(4 \times 6 + 4 \times 5 + 6 \times 5) = 148\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A monument consists of two solid cubical blocks of stone stacked on top of each other. The side length of the upper cube is \(2\text{ m}\) less than the side length of the lower cube. If the total volume of the monument is \(468\text{ m}^3\), find the total height of the monument.
qs.s: The volume equation is \(x^3 + (x - 2)^3 = 468\), which simplifies to \(x^3 - 3x^2 + 6x - 238 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 7)(x^2 + 4x + 34) = 0\), so \(x = 7\text{ m}\) and the total height is \(7 + (7 - 2) = 12\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A medicine capsule has the shape of a cylinder with hemispherical ends of radius \(x\text{ mm}\). The total length of the capsule is \(18\text{ mm}\), and its volume is \(144\pi\text{ mm}^3\). Find the length of the cylindrical section of the capsule.
qs.s: The volume equation \(\frac{4}{3}\pi x^3 + \pi x^2(18 - 2x) = 144\pi\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 27x^2 + 216 = 0\). The only valid positive root is \(x = 3\text{ mm}\), so the cylindrical section has length \(18 - 2(3) = 12\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: A storage building consists of a rectangular prism base and a triangular prism roof. The width of the base is \(x\text{ m}\), its length is \(4\text{ m}\) greater than its width, and the height of the rectangular base equals its width. The roof has the same width and length as the base, and the total height of the building is \(12\text{ m}\). If the total volume of the building is \(256\text{ m}^3\), what is the length of the building?
qs.s: The total volume is \(x^2(x + 4) + \frac{1}{2}x(12 - x)(x + 4) = 256\), which simplifies to \(x^3 + 16x^2 + 48x - 512 = 0\). Factoring gives \((x - 4)(x^2 + 20x + 128) = 0\), so \(x = 4\text{ m}\) and the length is \(x + 4 = 8\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An open box is made from a square piece of cardboard measuring 18 inches by 18 inches, by cutting equal square corners and turning up the sides. Find the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(18 - 2x)^2 = 4x^3 - 72x^2 + 324x\). Setting \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 144x + 324 = 0\) gives the critical value \(x = 3\text{ in}\), yielding a maximum volume of \(V(3) = 3(12)^2 = 432\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: An open box is constructed from a rectangular sheet of cardboard measuring 15 cm by 24 cm, by cutting equal square corners and folding up the sides. Find the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(15 - 2x)(24 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 78x^2 + 360x\). Setting \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 156x + 360 = 0\) yields the optimal cut length \(x = 3\text{ cm}\), giving a maximum volume of \(V(3) = 3(9)(18) = 486\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An open box is made from a piece of cardboard 9 inches by 24 inches, by cutting equal square corners and turning up the sides. Find the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(9 - 2x)(24 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 66x^2 + 216x\). Setting \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 132x + 216 = 0\) gives \(x = 2\text{ in}\), resulting in a maximum volume of \(V(2) = 2(5)(20) = 200\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: An open box is made from a rectangular piece of cardboard measuring 10 cm by 16 cm, by cutting equal square corners and turning up the sides. Find the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(10 - 2x)(16 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 52x^2 + 160x\). Setting \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 104x + 160 = 0\) gives the feasible critical point \(x = 2\text{ cm}\), which yields the maximum volume \(V(2) = 2(6)(12) = 144\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An open box is made from a piece of cardboard 16 inches by 21 inches, by cutting equal square corners and turning up the sides. Find the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(16 - 2x)(21 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 74x^2 + 336x\). Setting \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 148x + 336 = 0\) gives the feasible cut length \(x = 3\text{ in}\), producing a maximum volume of \(V(3) = 3(10)(15) = 450\text{ in}^3\).

qs.q: An open box is constructed from a piece of cardboard measuring 24 cm by 45 cm, by cutting equal square corners and turning up the sides. If the box is designed to have the maximum possible volume, what is the sum of its three dimensions (length, width, and height)?
qs.s: The volume \(V(x) = x(24 - 2x)(45 - 2x)\) is maximized when \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 276x + 1080 = 0\), giving \(x = 5\text{ cm}\). The dimensions are height \(5\text{ cm}\), width \(14\text{ cm}\), and length \(35\text{ cm}\), giving a sum of \(5 + 14 + 35 = 54\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open box is constructed from a rectangular sheet of cardboard measuring 33 cm by 40 cm, by cutting equal square corners and turning up the sides. Find the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(33 - 2x)(40 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 146x^2 + 1320x\). Solving \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 292x + 1320 = 0\) gives the feasible root \(x = 6\text{ cm}\), which gives the maximum volume \(V(6) = 6(21)(28) = 3528\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An open storage bin is made from a rectangular sheet of metal measuring 18 cm by 48 cm, by cutting equal square corners of side length x and folding up the sides. What is the total outside surface area of the bin when its volume is maximized?
qs.s: The volume \(V(x) = x(18 - 2x)(48 - 2x)\) is maximized when \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 264x + 864 = 0\), giving \(x = 4\text{ cm}\). The total outside surface area is the original sheet area minus the four removed corners: \(18(48) - 4(4^2) = 864 - 64 = 800\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is made from a piece of cardboard measuring 14 inches by 30 inches, by cutting congruent squares from each corner and turning up the sides. Find the total area of the four cut-out corner squares that results in the maximum volume of the box.
qs.s: Setting \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 176x + 420 = 0\) for \(V(x) = x(14 - 2x)(30 - 2x)\) yields the optimal cut length \(x = 3\text{ in}\). The combined area of the four cut squares is \(4x^2 = 4(3^2) = 36\text{ in}^2\).

qs.q: Two identical rectangular sheets of cardboard measuring 15 cm by 24 cm are used to make open boxes by cutting equal squares from each corner. Box A is made using the corner cut size that maximizes volume, while Box B is made using corner cuts that are 1 cm smaller than that optimal size. What is the difference between the volume of Box A and the volume of Box B?
qs.s: Maximizing \(V(x) = x(15 - 2x)(24 - 2x)\) gives optimal cut \(x = 3\text{ cm}\) with volume \(V(3) = 486\text{ cm}^3\) for Box A. For Box B, cut size \(x = 2\text{ cm}\) gives \(V(2) = 2(11)(20) = 440\text{ cm}^3\), so the difference is \(486 - 440 = 46\text{ cm}^3\).

exercises.name: Geometric dimensions from volume or area

qs.q: A gift box has a square base; the perimeter of the base plus the height is 60 cm. What length of the base yields a volume of 1296 cm³?
qs.s: Setting the base side length to \(x\), the height is \(h = 60 - 4x\). The volume is \(V = x^2(60 - 4x) = 1296\), simplifying to \(x^3 - 15x^2 + 324 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 6)(x^2 - 9x - 54) = 0\) to give the rational solution \(x = 6\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A storage bin has a square base; the sum of one side length of the base and the height is 14 m. What length of the base yields a volume of 160 m³?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the length of the base, so the height is \(h = 14 - x\). Setting the volume \(x^2(14 - x) = 160\) gives \(x^3 - 14x^2 + 160 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 4)(x^2 - 10x - 40) = 0\), giving the rational answer \(x = 4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A rectangular package has a square base; the perimeter of the base plus the height is 108 cm. What length of the base yields a volume of 11 664 cm³?
qs.s: With base side \(x\), the height is \(h = 108 - 4x\). The volume equation \(x^2(108 - 4x) = 11664\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 27x^2 + 2916 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 18)^2(x + 9) = 0\), yielding \(x = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A closed wooden box has a square base. The height of the box is 3 cm greater than the side length of the base. What is the side length of the base if the volume of the box is 112 cm³?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the side length of the base, so the height is \(x + 3\). The volume equation \(x^2(x + 3) = 112\) simplifies to \(x^3 + 3x^2 - 112 = 0\), which factors into \((x - 4)(x^2 + 7x + 28) = 0\), giving the real solution \(x = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A shipping carton has a square base. The perimeter of the base plus the height is 90 cm. What length of the base yields a volume of 5000 cm³?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the side length of the base, so the height is \(h = 90 - 4x\). The volume equation \(x^2(90 - 4x) = 5000\) simplifies to \(2x^3 - 45x^2 + 2500 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 10)(2x^2 - 25x - 250) = 0\), giving \(x = 10\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The length of a rectangular box is 2 cm greater than its width, and the height is 3 cm less than twice its width. If the volume of the box is 432 cm³, what is the total surface area of the box?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the width, so length is \(x + 2\) and height is \(2x - 3\). The volume equation \(x(x + 2)(2x - 3) = 432\) simplifies to \(2x^3 + x^2 - 6x - 432 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 6)(2x^2 + 13x + 72) = 0\), giving dimensions 6 cm, 8 cm, and 9 cm; the total surface area is \(2(6 \times 8 + 6 \times 9 + 8 \times 9) = 348\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A closed rectangular storage box has a width of \(x\) cm. Its length is 3 cm longer than its width, and its height is 1 cm longer than twice its width. If the volume of the box is 440 cm³, what is the length of the longest edge of the box?
qs.s: The volume is \(x(x + 3)(2x + 1) = 440\), which simplifies to \(2x^3 + 7x^2 + 3x - 440 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 5)(2x^2 + 17x + 88) = 0\), giving \(x = 5\text{ cm}\). The dimensions are 5 cm, 8 cm, and \(2(5) + 1 = 11\text{ cm}\), so the longest edge is 11 cm.

qs.q: A capsule is shaped like a right circular cylinder with a hemisphere on each end. The total length of the capsule is 16 mm, and its total volume is \(126\pi\text{ mm}^3\). What is the length of the cylindrical portion of the capsule?
qs.s: For radius \(x\), the cylinder length is \(16 - 2x\), and the volume is \(\frac{4}{3}\pi x^3 + \pi x^2(16 - 2x) = 126\pi\). This simplifies to \(x^3 - 24x^2 + 189 = 0\), which has the valid root \(x = 3\text{ mm}\), giving a cylinder length of \(16 - 2(3) = 10\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular shipping crate has a square base. The perimeter of the base plus the height is 240 cm. If the crate has a volume of 108 000 cm³, what is the height of the crate?
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the base side, so \(h = 240 - 4x\). The equation \(x^2(240 - 4x) = 108000\) simplifies to \(x^3 - 60x^2 + 27000 = 0\), which factors as \((x - 30)(x^2 - 30x - 900) = 0\), giving base \(x = 30\text{ cm}\) and height \(h = 240 - 4(30) = 120\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open box is constructed by cutting a square of integer side length \(x\) cm from each corner of a 24 cm by 24 cm square sheet of metal and folding up the sides. If the volume of the box is 800 cm³, what is the area of the base of the box?
qs.s: The volume is \(x(24 - 2x)^2 = 800\), which expands to \(x^3 - 24x^2 + 144x - 200 = 0\) and factors as \((x - 2)(x^2 - 22x + 100) = 0\), giving \(x = 2\text{ cm}\). The area of the base is \((24 - 2(2))^2 = 20^2 = 400\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is formed by cutting equal squares of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of an \(18\text{ cm}\) by \(18\text{ cm}\) square piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the maximum volume of the box?
qs.s: The volume is \(V(x) = x(18 - 2x)^2\) on \((0, 9)\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = \frac{18}{6} = 3\text{ cm}\). Substituting \(x = 3\) gives the maximum volume \(V(3) = 3(12)(12) = 432\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(12\text{ cm}\) by \(12\text{ cm}\) square piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the height of the box that achieves the maximum volume?
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(12 - 2x)^2\) for \(0 < x < 6\), which reaches its maximum at \(x = \frac{12}{6} = 2\text{ cm}\). Since the folded cut length forms the height, the height of the box is \(2\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(16\text{ cm}\) by \(10\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. To achieve the maximum volume of the box, what must be the length of the box?
qs.s: The volume \(V(x) = x(16 - 2x)(10 - 2x)\) is maximized on \((0, 5)\) when \(V'(x) = 4(3x - 20)(x - 2) = 0\), giving \(x = 2\text{ cm}\). Thus, the length of the box is \(16 - 2(2) = 12\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is formed by cutting equal squares of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(24\text{ cm}\) by \(9\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the maximum volume of the box?
qs.s: The volume function \(V(x) = x(24 - 2x)(9 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 66x^2 + 216x\) has derivative \(V'(x) = 12(x - 2)(x - 9) = 0\). On the domain \(0 < x < 4.5\), the maximum occurs at \(x = 2\text{ cm}\), giving a maximum volume of \(V(2) = 2(20)(5) = 200\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of an \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What value of \(x\) maximizes the volume of the box?
qs.s: The volume function is \(V(x) = x(8 - 2x)(5 - 2x) = 4x^3 - 26x^2 + 40x\) on the domain \(0 < x < 2.5\). Setting the derivative \(V'(x) = 12x^2 - 52x + 40 = 4(3x - 10)(x - 1) = 0\) yields \(x = 1\text{ cm}\) as the maximizing critical value.

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(24\text{ cm}\) by \(15\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. If the box is constructed to achieve its maximum volume, what is the total inside surface area of the open box?
qs.s: Solving \(V'(x) = 12(x - 3)(x - 10) = 0\) gives \(x = 3\text{ cm}\) for maximum volume on \((0, 7.5)\). The total inside surface area equals the original sheet area minus the four cut corners: \((24 \times 15) - 4(3^2) = 360 - 36 = 324\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(36\text{ cm}\) by \(36\text{ cm}\) square piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the difference between the maximum volume of the box and the volume obtained when \(x = 4\text{ cm}\)?
qs.s: The volume is maximized at \(x = \frac{36}{6} = 6\text{ cm}\), giving \(V(6) = 6(24)^2 = 3456\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x = 4\text{ cm}\), \(V(4) = 4(28)^2 = 3136\text{ cm}^3\), and the difference is \(3456 - 3136 = 320\text{ cm}^3\).
