qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(30\text{ cm}\) by \(14\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the area of the base of the box when its volume is maximized?
qs.s: Setting the derivative of \(V(x) = x(30 - 2x)(14 - 2x)\) to zero gives \(4(x - 3)(3x - 35) = 0\), so volume is maximized at \(x = 3\text{ cm}\) on \((0, 7)\). The dimensions of the base are \(30 - 2(3) = 24\text{ cm}\) and \(14 - 2(3) = 8\text{ cm}\), producing a base area of \(24 \times 8 = 192\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(32\text{ cm}\) by \(20\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the maximum volume of the box?
qs.s: The derivative of \(V(x) = x(32 - 2x)(20 - 2x)\) is \(V'(x) = 4(3x - 40)(x - 4) = 0\), giving \(x = 4\text{ cm}\) on \((0, 10)\). The maximum volume is \(V(4) = 4(24)(12) = 1152\text{ cm}^3\).

qs.q: An open rectangular box is constructed by cutting a square of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) from each corner of a \(40\text{ cm}\) by \(25\text{ cm}\) rectangular piece of cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the sum of the length, width, and height of the box that achieves the maximum volume?
qs.s: Setting \(V'(x) = 4(3x - 50)(x - 5) = 0\) gives \(x = 5\text{ cm}\) on \((0, 12.5)\). The optimal dimensions are height \(5\text{ cm}\), length \(40 - 2(5) = 30\text{ cm}\), and width \(25 - 2(5) = 15\text{ cm}\), whose sum is \(30 + 15 + 5 = 50\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: In the real number system, the expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) does not exist when \(n\) is an even integer and \(a\) is _____.
qs.s: An even root of a negative number does not exist in the real number system because no real number raised to an even power equals a negative number.

qs.q: The symbol \(\sqrt{}\) used in radical expressions is called the _____.
qs.s: The symbol \(\sqrt{}\) is called the radical symbol, or simply the radical.

qs.q: When a radical expression is written without an index, such as \(\sqrt{x}\), the index is understood to be _____.
qs.s: A radical written without a visible index represents a square root, which has an implied index of 2.

qs.q: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[3]{125}\), the number \(125\) is called the _____.
qs.s: The number or expression located under the radical sign is called the radicand.

qs.q: In the radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the positive integer \(n\) is called the _____.
qs.s: In the radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the natural number \(n\) indicates the order of the root and is called the index.

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the radical \(\sqrt[4]{20 - 5x}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Since the index 4 is even, the radicand must be non-negative: \(20 - 5x \ge 0\), which gives \(-5x \ge -20\), or \(x \le 4\).

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the expression \(\sqrt[6]{3x + 12} + \sqrt[3]{7 - x}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: The odd root \(\sqrt[3]{7 - x}\) is defined for all real numbers, so the expression is real as long as the even root's radicand is non-negative: \(3x + 12 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -4\).

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) do both \(\sqrt{2x - 8}\) and \(\sqrt{18 - 2x}\) represent real numbers?
qs.s: Both square roots require non-negative radicands: \(2x - 8 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 4\) and \(18 - 2x \ge 0 \implies x \le 9\). Combining these conditions gives \(4 \le x \le 9\).

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the radical \(\sqrt{x^2 - 25}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: An even root requires the radicand to be non-negative: \(x^2 - 25 \ge 0 \implies x^2 \ge 25\), which means \(x \le -5\) or \(x \ge 5\).

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the expression \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[4]{2x - 14}}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: The even root requires \(2x - 14 \ge 0\), and the denominator cannot be zero (\(2x - 14 \ne 0\)). Combining both requirements gives \(2x - 14 > 0\), so \(x > 7\).

qs.q: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the positive integer \(n\) is called the _____.
qs.s: In radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the natural number \(n\) indicates the order of the root and is called the index.

qs.q: When \(n\) is an even positive integer and \(a > 0\), the non-negative root \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) is called the _____ root of \(a\).
qs.s: By definition, the non-negative \(n^{\text{th}}\) root of a positive real number is called the principal \(n^{\text{th}}\) root.

qs.q: When a radical is written without an explicit index, as in \(\sqrt{49}\), the implied value of the index is _____.
qs.s: A radical symbol written without an index denotes a square root, which has an understood index of 2.

qs.q: In the real number system, the expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) does not exist when the radicand \(a\) is negative and the index \(n\) is _____.
qs.s: An even power of any real number is always non-negative, so an even root of a negative number does not exist in the real number system.

qs.q: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the quantity \(a\) under the radical sign is called the _____.
qs.s: In radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the quantity \(a\) placed under the radical symbol is defined as the radicand.

qs.q: In the expression \(-3\sqrt[6]{2x - 1} + 5\), let \(a\) be the index and \(b\) be the radicand. The value of \(a + b\) when \(x = 5\) is _____.
qs.s: The index is \(a = 6\) and the radicand is \(b = 2x - 1\). Substituting \(x = 5\) gives \(b = 2(5) - 1 = 9\), so \(a + b = 6 + 9 = 15\).

qs.q: For the expression \(\sqrt[3]{5x - 15}\) to exist in the real number system, the condition on \(x\) is _____.
qs.s: Because the index 3 is odd, the root exists for any real radicand, meaning the expression is defined for all real numbers.

qs.q: Among the expressions \(\sqrt[4]{12 - 5^2}\), \(\sqrt[3]{12 - 5^2}\), \(\sqrt[4]{5^2 - 12}\), and \(\sqrt[5]{-32}\), the one that does NOT exist in the real number system is _____.
qs.s: Evaluating the radicand gives \(12 - 5^2 = 12 - 25 = -13\); because the index 4 is even, \(\sqrt[4]{-13}\) does not exist in the real number system.

qs.q: For the expression \(\sqrt{3x + 12} + \sqrt{10 - 2x}\) to exist in the real number system, the condition on \(x\) is _____.
qs.s: Both even-index radicals must have non-negative radicands: \(3x + 12 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -4\) and \(10 - 2x \ge 0 \implies x \le 5\), giving the combined condition \(-4 \le x \le 5\).

qs.q: For the expression \(\sqrt{8 - 4x}\) to exist in the real number system, the condition on \(x\) is _____.
qs.s: Since the square root has an even index of 2, the radicand must be non-negative: \(8 - 4x \ge 0 \implies -4x \ge -8 \implies x \le 2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: For any negative real number \(a < 0\), \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) does not exist in the real number system if \(n\) is an _____ integer.
qs.s: An even root of a negative number has no real solution because any real number raised to an even power is non-negative.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: When \(n\) is an even positive integer and \(a > 0\), the non-negative real root \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) is called the _____ \(n^{\text{th}}\) root of \(a\).
qs.s: By definition, for an even index \(n\) and \(a > 0\), \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) denotes the non-negative or principal \(n^{\text{th}}\) root of \(a\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{x}\), the symbol \(\sqrt{}\) is called the _____.
qs.s: The symbol \(\sqrt{}\) used to indicate a root is called the radical symbol, or radical.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: When no index is written in a radical expression like \(\sqrt{x}\), the index is understood to be _____.
qs.s: A radical written without an explicit index denotes a square root, which has an understood index of 2.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{x}\), the expression \(x\) under the radical symbol is called the _____.
qs.s: In radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{x}\), the quantity \(x\) under the radical sign is called the radicand.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the real number system, the expression \(\sqrt[4]{3x - 21}\) is defined if and only if \(x \ge\) _____.
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even, the radicand must be non-negative: \(3x - 21 \ge 0\), which solves to \(x \ge 7\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: Among the five expressions \(\sqrt[3]{-27}\), \(\sqrt[4]{-16}\), \(\sqrt[5]{-32}\), \(\sqrt[6]{-1}\), and \(\sqrt[4]{0}\), exactly _____ of them exist in the real number system.
qs.s: The odd roots of negative numbers (\(\sqrt[3]{-27} = -3\), \(\sqrt[5]{-32} = -2\)) and the root of zero (\(\sqrt[4]{0} = 0\)) exist in the real numbers, while the even roots of negative numbers (\(\sqrt[4]{-16}\), \(\sqrt[6]{-1}\)) do not, giving exactly 3.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the real number system, the radical expression \(\sqrt[6]{36 - 4x}\) is defined if and only if \(x \le\) _____.
qs.s: Since the index 6 is even, the root is defined in the real numbers when \(36 - 4x \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(-4x \ge -36\) and reverses to \(x \le 9\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The expression \(\sqrt[4]{x^2 + 25}\) exists in the real number system for _____.
qs.s: Since \(x^2 \ge 0\) for every real number \(x\), the radicand satisfies \(x^2 + 25 \ge 25 > 0\) and is never negative, meaning the fourth root exists for all real numbers.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(-5x\sqrt[3]{8 - 2x^2}\), the radicand is _____.
qs.s: The radicand is the entire expression under the radical sign, which is \(8 - 2x^2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In the real number system, the expression \(\sqrt[6]{x}\) is defined only when _____.
qs.s: Because the index 6 is even, the radicand must be non-negative, meaning \(x \ge 0\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{9y}\), the expression \(9y\) is called the _____.
qs.s: The expression under the radical symbol is called the radicand, so \(9y\) is the radicand.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In the radical expression \(\sqrt[3]{11}\), the number \(3\) is called the _____.
qs.s: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the natural number \(n\) indicating the order of the root is called the index.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. The principal fifth root of \(m\) is written symbolically as _____.
qs.s: The principal fifth root of a number \(m\) is written in radical notation as \(\sqrt[5]{m}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In radical notation, the symbol \(\sqrt{}\) is called the _____.
qs.s: The symbol \(\sqrt{}\) is known as the radical symbol, or simply the radical.

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[5]{2x - 10}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: Because the index 5 is odd, the \(n^{\mathrm{th}}\) root exists for every real number, meaning the expression is defined for all real numbers.

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the expression \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x - 8}}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: The square root requires \(2x - 8 \ge 0\), and being in the denominator prevents it from being zero, resulting in \(2x - 8 > 0\), or \(x > 4\).

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{x^2 - 9}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Since the index 4 is even, the radicand must be non-negative: \(x^2 - 9 \ge 0\), which gives \(x^2 \ge 9\), meaning \(x \ge 3\) or \(x \le -3\).

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{12 - 3x}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even, the radicand must satisfy \(12 - 3x \ge 0\), which gives \(-3x \ge -12\), or \(x \le 4\).

qs.q: If \(a < 0\), which of the following expressions does not represent a real number?
qs.s: An even root of a negative number does not exist in the real number system, so with \(a < 0\) and even index 4, \(\sqrt[4]{a}\) is not a real number.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[5]{32}\), the number \(5\) is called the _____ of the radical.
qs.s: In the radical \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the positive integer \(n\) indicates the order or index of the radical.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: \(\sqrt[4]{81} = 3\) is read the (principal) _____ root of 81 equals 3.
qs.s: The index of the radical is \(4\), so \(\sqrt[4]{81} = 3\) represents the principal fourth root of 81.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[3]{64}\), the number \(64\) is called the _____.
qs.s: In radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the number or expression \(a\) under the radical sign is called the radicand.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(\sqrt{49}\), the unwritten index is understood to be _____.
qs.s: When no index is explicitly written on a radical symbol, it is by definition a square root with an index of \(2\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the real number system, the expression \(\sqrt{-36}\) _____.
qs.s: Because the index \(2\) is even and the radicand \(-36\) is negative, no real number squared equals \(-36\), so the root does not exist in the real number system.

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[5]{3x - 21}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: Because the index \(5\) is odd, the \(n^{\text{th}}\) root of any real number exists in the real number system, so \(x\) can be any real number.

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{40 - 8x}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: Since the index \(4\) is even, the radicand must be non-negative: \(40 - 8x \ge 0\), which gives \(-8x \ge -40\) and simplifies to \(x \le 5\).

qs.q: What is the smallest integer \(x\) for which the radical expression \(\sqrt{6x - 45}\) represents a real number?
qs.s: For the square root to exist in the real number system, we require \(6x - 45 \ge 0\), which yields \(x \ge 7.5\). The smallest integer satisfying this condition is \(8\).

qs.q: For how many integer values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[6]{64 - x^2}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: The index \(6\) is even, so the radicand must satisfy \(64 - x^2 \ge 0\), meaning \(x^2 \le 64\) and \(-8 \le x \le 8\). The number of integers in this range is \(8 - (-8) + 1 = 17\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[5]{32}\), the number 5 is called the _____.
qs.s: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the natural number \(n\) indicating the order of the root is called the index.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the real number system, the expression \(\sqrt[n]{a}\) does not exist if the index \(n\) is even and the radicand \(a\) is _____.
qs.s: An even root of a negative number does not exist in the real number system because no real number raised to an even power produces a negative result.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: When a radical is written without an index, such as \(\sqrt{49} = 7\), the understood index is _____.
qs.s: A radical symbol with no index written represents a square root, which has an understood index of 2.

qs.q: If the principal fourth root of a number \(k\) is 6, what is the value of the radicand \(k\)?
qs.s: The statement means \(\sqrt[4]{k} = 6\). Raising both sides to the fourth power gives the radicand \(k = 6^4 = 1296\).

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[6]{20 - 5x}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: An even root is defined in the real number system only when the radicand is greater than or equal to zero: \(20 - 5x \ge 0 \implies -5x \ge -20 \implies x \le 4\).

qs.q: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{-243} = -3\), what is the value of the index \(n\)?
qs.s: By the definition of radical notation, \(\sqrt[n]{a} = x\) means \(x^n = a\). Since \((-3)^5 = -243\), the index is \(n = 5\).

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{3x - 24}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Since the index 4 is an even number, the radical exists in the real number system when the radicand is non-negative: \(3x - 24 \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(x \ge 8\).

qs.q: For which values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[5]{7 - 2x}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Because the index 5 is an odd integer, the fifth root of any real number exists in the real number system, meaning the expression is defined for all real numbers.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The expression \(\sqrt[n]{x}\) represents a real number for every real number \(x\) if \(n\) is _____.
qs.s: Odd roots are defined for all real numbers (positive, negative, and zero), so \(\sqrt[n]{x}\) is always real when \(n\) is odd.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The principal \(n^{\text{th}}\) root \(\sqrt[n]{x}\) is not a real number if \(x < 0\) and \(n\) is _____.
qs.s: An even root of a negative number does not exist in the real number system because no real number raised to an even power is negative.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: If \(n\) is an even positive integer, the radical \(\sqrt[n]{x}\) represents a real number only if \(x\) satisfies _____.
qs.s: For an even index \(n\), the radicand must be greater than or equal to zero (\(x \ge 0\)) for the root to exist in the real number system.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{x}\), the natural number \(n\) is called the _____.
qs.s: In radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{x}\), the natural number \(n\) is called the index (or order) of the radical.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: In the radical expression \(\sqrt[n]{x}\), the quantity \(x\) under the radical symbol is called the _____.
qs.s: By definition of radical notation, the number or algebraic expression written under the radical sign is called the radicand.

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The expression \(\sqrt[3]{8 - x} - \sqrt[4]{2x + 14}\) is defined in the real number system if and only if \(x\) satisfies _____.
qs.s: The cube root has an odd index and is defined for all real numbers, while the fourth root has an even index and requires \(2x + 14 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -7\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The expression \(\sqrt[4]{2x - 6} + \sqrt{10 - x}\) represents a real number if and only if \(x\) satisfies _____.
qs.s: Both radicals have even indexes, so both radicands must be non-negative: \(2x - 6 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 3\) and \(10 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 10\). Thus, \(3 \le x \le 10\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The principal root \(\sqrt[4]{10 - 4x}\) is not a real number when \(x\) satisfies _____.
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even, the expression is not a real number when the radicand is negative: \(10 - 4x < 0 \implies -4x < -10 \implies x > \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The radical expression \(\sqrt{25 - x^2}\) does not represent a real number when \(x\) satisfies _____.
qs.s: The square root has an even index (2) and is not real when the radicand is strictly negative: \(25 - x^2 < 0 \implies x^2 > 25\), meaning \(x < -5\) or \(x > 5\).

qs.q: Fill in the blank: The radical expression \(\sqrt[6]{3x + 15}\) represents a real number if and only if \(x\) satisfies _____.
qs.s: An even root is defined in the real number system when its radicand is non-negative: \(3x + 15 \ge 0 \implies 3x \ge -15 \implies x \ge -5\).

qs.q: Fill in the missing inequality. For the expression \(\sqrt[6]{x}\) to represent a real number, the radicand must satisfy \(x\) _____.
qs.s: An even root of a real number exists in the real number system if and only if the radicand is non-negative (\(x \ge 0\)).

qs.q: For what values of the radicand \(a\) does the expression \(\sqrt[5]{a}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Since the index 5 is an odd integer, the fifth root is defined for all real values of the radicand \(a\).

qs.q: Complete the statement. In the real number system, the value of \(\sqrt[4]{-81}\) _____.
qs.s: An even root of a negative number does not exist in the real number system.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{3x - 5}\), the expression \(3x - 5\) located under the radical symbol is called the _____.
qs.s: The expression located under the radical symbol is defined as the radicand.

qs.q: Fill in the blank. In radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the natural number \(n\) is called the _____ of the radical.
qs.s: In the radical notation \(\sqrt[n]{a}\), the natural number \(n\) is referred to as the index (or order) of the radical.

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the expression \(\sqrt{2x - 6} + \sqrt[4]{20 - 4x}\) represent a real number?
qs.s: Both radicals have even indices, requiring \(2x - 6 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 3\) and \(20 - 4x \ge 0 \implies x \le 5\), which combine to give \(3 \le x \le 5\).

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) does the radical expression \(\sqrt[6]{\frac{2}{5}x - 14}\) exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Since the index 6 is even, the radicand must satisfy \(\frac{2}{5}x - 14 \ge 0 \implies \frac{2}{5}x \ge 14 \implies x \ge 35\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions does NOT exist in the real number system?
qs.s: Evaluating the radicand gives \((-4)^2 - 52 = 16 - 52 = -36\); since the index 4 is even and the radicand is negative, \(\sqrt[4]{-36}\) is not a real number.

qs.q: Find the condition on \(x\) for the radical expression \(\sqrt[4]{24 - 8x}\) to represent a real number.
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even, the radicand must be non-negative: \(24 - 8x \ge 0 \implies -8x \ge -24 \implies x \le 3\).

qs.q: For what values of \(x\) is the expression \(\sqrt[4]{3x + 15} - \sqrt[3]{2x - 7}\) defined in the real number system?
qs.s: The odd root \(\sqrt[3]{2x - 7}\) exists for all real numbers, so only the even root requires \(3x + 15 \ge 0\), which yields \(x \ge -5\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^2 = 49\)
qs.s: Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = \pm\sqrt{49}\), which simplifies to \(x = \pm 7\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^2 = 64\)
qs.s: Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = \pm\sqrt{64}\), which simplifies to \(x = \pm 8\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^2 = 36\)
qs.s: Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = \pm\sqrt{36}\), which simplifies to \(x = \pm 6\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^2 = 25\)
qs.s: Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = \pm\sqrt{25}\), which simplifies to \(x = \pm 5\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^2 = 100\)
qs.s: Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = \pm\sqrt{100}\), which simplifies to \(x = \pm 10\).
Add \(5\) to both sides to get \(4x^2 = 25\), then divide by \(4\) to obtain \(x^2 = \frac{25}{4}\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \pm\frac{5}{2}\).
Taking the square root of both sides gives \(x = \pm\sqrt{\frac{49}{121}}\), which simplifies to \(x = \pm\frac{7}{11}\).
Subtract \(11\) from both sides to get \(2x^3 = -54\), then divide by \(2\) to obtain \(x^3 = -27\). Taking the cube root gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{-27} = -3\).
Add \(14\) to both sides to get \(5x^4 = 80\), then divide by \(5\) to obtain \(x^4 = 16\). Taking the fourth root gives \(x = \pm\sqrt[4]{16} = \pm 2\).
Add \(7\) to both sides to get \(3x^2 = 75\), then divide by \(3\) to obtain \(x^2 = 25\). Taking the square root gives \(x = \pm 5\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^2 = -25\)
qs.s: Because \(x^2 \ge 0\) for all real numbers \(x\), there is no real solution to \(x^2 = -25\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^4 = -81\)
qs.s: Any real number raised to the fourth power is non-negative (\(x^4 \ge 0\)), so \(x^4 = -81\) has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^2 = -16\)
qs.s: Since the square of any real number is non-negative (\(x^2 \ge 0\)), there is no real number whose square is \(-16\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^2 = -64\)
qs.s: The square of a real number cannot be negative, meaning \(x^2 = -64\) has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^4 = -1\)
qs.s: Raising any real number to an even power yields a value greater than or equal to \(0\), so \(x^4 = -1\) has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(5x^2 + 31 = 3x^2 - 169\)
qs.s: Rearranging terms yields \(2x^2 = -200\), so \(x^2 = -100\). Since \(x^2 \ge 0\) for all real numbers, this equation has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(\frac{1}{3}x^2 + 25 = 13\)
qs.s: Subtracting \(25\) gives \(\frac{1}{3}x^2 = -12\), and multiplying by \(3\) gives \(x^2 = -36\). As a square cannot be negative over the real numbers, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(2x^2 + 98 = 0\)
qs.s: Subtracting \(98\) and dividing by \(2\) gives \(x^2 = -49\). Since the square of a real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(4(x^2 + 10) = 15\)
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(4x^2 = -25\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = -\frac{25}{4}\). Since \(x^2 \ge 0\) for all real numbers, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(2x^4 + 37 = 5\)
qs.s: Subtracting \(37\) gives \(2x^4 = -32\), which simplifies to \(x^4 = -16\). Because an even power cannot equal a negative number in the real number system, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^4 = 81\)
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even and 81 is positive, there are two real solutions: \(x = \pm\sqrt[4]{81} = \pm 3\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^3 = -64\)
qs.s: Since the index is odd, taking the cube root yields a single real solution: \(x = \sqrt[3]{-64} = -4\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^5 = 32\)
qs.s: Taking the fifth root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[5]{32} = 2\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^3 = 27\)
qs.s: Taking the cube root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{27} = 3\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(125x^3 + 64 = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract 64 and divide by 125 to get \(x^3 = -\frac{64}{125}\). Taking the cube root gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{-\frac{64}{125}} = -\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(4x^3 - 9 = 15\)
qs.s: Add 9 to both sides to obtain \(4x^3 = 24\), then divide by 4 to get \(x^3 = 6\). Taking the cube root yields the exact solution \(x = \sqrt[3]{6}\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \((2x + 1)^3 = -125\)
qs.s: Take the cube root of both sides to get \(2x + 1 = \sqrt[3]{-125} = -5\). Subtracting 1 gives \(2x = -6\), so \(x = -3\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(2x^4 + 175 = 13\)
qs.s: Subtract 175 from both sides and divide by 2 to get \(x^4 = -81\). Since an even power of a real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(3x^4 - 7 = 41\)
qs.s: Add 7 to both sides to obtain \(3x^4 = 48\), then divide by 3 to get \(x^4 = 16\). Since the exponent is even and 16 is positive, \(x = \pm\sqrt[4]{16} = \pm 2\).
Taking the cube root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{-125}\). Since \((-5)^3 = -125\), the solution is \(x = -5\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^3 = -1\)
qs.s: Taking the cube root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{-1}\). Since \((-1)^3 = -1\), the solution is \(x = -1\).
Subtract \(50\) from both sides to get \(3x^5 = -96\), then divide by \(3\) to get \(x^5 = -32\). Taking the fifth root gives \(x = \sqrt[5]{-32} = -2\).
Add \(7\) to both sides to get \(4x^3 = -108\), then divide by \(4\) to find \(x^3 = -27\). Taking the cube root gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{-27} = -3\).
Taking the cube root of both sides gives \(2x + 7 = \sqrt[3]{-125} = -5\). Subtracting \(7\) yields \(2x = -12\), so \(x = -6\).
Subtract \(8\) from both sides to get \(27x^3 = -8\), then divide by \(27\) to obtain \(x^3 = -\frac{8}{27}\). Taking the cube root yields \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\).
Take the cube root of both sides to get \(x - 5 = \sqrt[3]{-64} = -4\). Adding \(5\) to both sides gives \(x = 1\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^4 = 16\)
qs.s: Taking the fourth root of both sides gives \(x = \pm \sqrt[4]{16} = \pm 2\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^3 = -8\)
qs.s: Since the index 3 is odd, taking the cube root yields a single real solution: \(x = \sqrt[3]{-8} = -2\).
Adding 14 gives \(\frac{x^4}{4} = 64\), so \(x^4 = 256\). Taking the fourth root gives \(x = \pm 4\).
Subtracting 7 gives \(-2x^3 = 128\), so dividing by \(-2\) gives \(x^3 = -64\). Taking the cube root gives \(x = -4\).
Subtracting 12 and dividing by 5 gives \((x - 4)^3 = -8\). Taking the cube root yields \(x - 4 = -2\), so \(x = 2\).
Adding 7 gives \(81x^4 = 16\), so \(x^4 = \frac{16}{81}\). Taking the fourth root gives \(x = \pm \frac{2}{3}\).
Rearranging terms gives \(-3x^3 = 81\), which simplifies to \(x^3 = -27\). Taking the cube root gives \(x = -3\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^4 = -625\)
qs.s: Since 4 is an even index and \(-625\) is negative, no real number satisfies \(x^4 = -625\). Thus, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^2 = -49\)
qs.s: Since the exponent 2 is an even integer and \(-49 < 0\), there is no real number whose square is negative. Therefore, the equation has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^6 = -1\)
qs.s: Raising any real number to the even power of 6 yields a non-negative result, so \(x^6 = -1\) is impossible in the real number system. Hence, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^2 = -81\)
qs.s: An even root of a negative number is not defined in the real number system, so \(\sqrt{-81}\) does not exist as a real value. Therefore, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(x^4 = -16\)
qs.s: Because 4 is an even power, \(x^4 \ge 0\) for all real numbers \(x\), so \(x^4\) cannot equal \(-16\). Thus, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(2(x^2 + 30) = 10\)
qs.s: Dividing both sides by 2 yields \(x^2 + 30 = 5\), which simplifies to \(x^2 = -25\). Since the square of any real number must be non-negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(4x^2 + 250 = 54\)
qs.s: Subtracting 250 gives \(4x^2 = -196\), so dividing by 4 yields \(x^2 = -49\). Because the square of a real number is never negative, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(\frac{1}{2}x^4 + 150 = 22\)
qs.s: Subtracting 150 gives \(\frac{1}{2}x^4 = -128\), and multiplying by 2 yields \(x^4 = -256\). Since an even power of a real number cannot equal a negative number, there is no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(5x^4 + 19 = 2x^4 - 224\)
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x^4\) and 19 from both sides gives \(3x^4 = -243\), so \(x^4 = -81\). Because 4 is an even exponent, \(x^4 = -81\) has no real solution.

qs.q: Solve for \(x\) over the real numbers: \(3x^4 + 75 = 27\)
qs.s: Subtracting 75 and dividing by 3 gives \(x^4 = -16\). Since an even power of a real number cannot be negative, there is no real solution.
Taking the fifth root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[5]{-243}\). Since \((-3)^5 = -243\), the solution is \(x = -3\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^3 = 216\)
qs.s: Taking the cube root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[3]{216}\). Since \(6^3 = 216\), the solution is \(x = 6\).
Subtract 47 from both sides to get \(5x^5 = -160\), then divide by 5 to obtain \(x^5 = -32\). Taking the fifth root gives \(x = -2\).
Taking the cube root of both sides gives \(2x - 3 = -5\). Adding 3 gives \(2x = -2\), so \(x = -1\).
Add 73 to both sides to get \(2x^4 = 1250\), then divide by 2 to get \(x^4 = 625\). Because the index is even, \(x = \pm\sqrt[4]{625} = \pm 5\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^6 = 729\)
qs.s: Since the exponent 6 is even and \(729 > 0\), taking the sixth root yields \(x = \pm\sqrt[6]{729}\). Since \(3^6 = 729\), the solutions are \(x = \pm 3\).
Subtract 1 to get \(32x^5 = -1\), then divide by 32 to get \(x^5 = -\frac{1}{32}\). Taking the fifth root gives \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Solve for \(x\): \(x^5 = -1\)
qs.s: Taking the fifth root of both sides gives \(x = \sqrt[5]{-1}\). Since \((-1)^5 = -1\), the solution is \(x = -1\).
Subtract 45 from both sides to get \(2x^5 = -486\), then divide by 2 to get \(x^5 = -243\). Taking the fifth root yields \(x = \sqrt[5]{-243} = -3\).
Take the cube root of both sides to get \(3x + 1 = -2\). Subtracting 1 gives \(3x = -3\), and dividing by 3 yields \(x = -1\).
Take the fifth root of both sides to get \(3x - 2 = 3\). Adding 2 gives \(3x = 5\), and dividing by 3 yields \(x = \frac{5}{3}\).
Subtract \(2x^3\) and 30 from both sides to obtain \(3x^3 = -192\), which simplifies to \(x^3 = -64\). Taking the cube root gives \(x = -4\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{16y^2}, y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Taking the square root of each factor gives \(\sqrt{16} = 4\) and \(\sqrt{y^2} = y\) because \(y \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(4y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{9x^2}, x \ge 0\)
qs.s: Taking the principal square root of both factors gives \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) and \(\sqrt{x^2} = x\) since \(x \ge 0\), resulting in \(3x\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{64b^2}, b \ge 0\)
qs.s: Evaluating the square root of each factor gives \(\sqrt{64} = 8\) and \(\sqrt{b^2} = b\) for \(b \ge 0\), yielding \(8b\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{49a^2}, a \ge 0\)
qs.s: Since \(a \ge 0\), we have \(\sqrt{49} = 7\) and \(\sqrt{a^2} = a\), giving \(7a\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{\frac{25}{64}x^6y^4}, x \ge 0\)
qs.s: Take the square root of each component: \(\sqrt{\frac{25}{64}} = \frac{5}{8}\), \(\sqrt{x^6} = x^3\) since \(x \ge 0\), and \(\sqrt{y^4} = y^2\), which gives \(\frac{5}{8}x^3y^2\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{36x^4y^2}, y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Take the square root of each factor: \(\sqrt{36} = 6\), \(\sqrt{x^4} = x^2\), and \(\sqrt{y^2} = y\) since \(y \ge 0\), yielding \(6x^2y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-27a^6b^3}\)
qs.s: Since the index 3 is odd, \(\sqrt[3]{-27} = -3\), \(\sqrt[3]{a^6} = a^2\), and \(\sqrt[3]{b^3} = b\), giving \(-3a^2b\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[4]{16x^8y^4}, y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Evaluate the fourth root of each factor: \(\sqrt[4]{16} = 2\), \(\sqrt[4]{x^8} = x^2\), and \(\sqrt[4]{y^4} = y\) because \(y \ge 0\), resulting in \(2x^2y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{9y^2},\text{ where } y < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(y < 0\), we have \(\sqrt{y^2} = |y| = -y\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{9y^2} = 3|y| = 3(-y) = -3y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{25x^2},\text{ where } x < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), we have \(\sqrt{x^2} = |x| = -x\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{25x^2} = 5|x| = 5(-x) = -5x\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{49m^2},\text{ where } m < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(m < 0\), we have \(\sqrt{m^2} = |m| = -m\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{49m^2} = 7|m| = 7(-m) = -7m\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{16b^2},\text{ where } b < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(b < 0\), we have \(\sqrt{b^2} = |b| = -b\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{16b^2} = 4|b| = 4(-b) = -4b\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{64a^2},\text{ where } a < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(a < 0\), we have \(\sqrt{a^2} = |a| = -a\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{64a^2} = 8|a| = 8(-a) = -8a\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{25x^2y^4},\text{ where } x < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), \(\sqrt{x^2} = |x| = -x\), and since \(y^2 \ge 0\), \(\sqrt{y^4} = y^2\). Therefore, \(\sqrt{25x^2y^4} = 5(-x)y^2 = -5xy^2\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\sqrt{36x^2} + \sqrt{49x^2},\text{ where } x < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), \(\sqrt{36x^2} = -6x\) and \(\sqrt{49x^2} = -7x\). Adding these terms gives \(-6x + (-7x) = -13x\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(7x - \sqrt{16x^2},\text{ where } x < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), \(\sqrt{16x^2} = 4|x| = -4x\). Substituting gives \(7x - (-4x) = 7x + 4x = 11x\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{9(x - 5)^2},\text{ where } x < 5\)
Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{64x^6},\text{ where } x < 0\)
qs.s: Since \(x < 0\), \(x^3\) is negative, which means \(\sqrt{x^6} = |x^3| = -x^3\). Thus, \(\sqrt{64x^6} = 8(-x^3) = -8x^3\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[4]{16b^4}\), where \(b < 0\).
qs.s: Because the index 4 is even, \(\sqrt[4]{16b^4} = 2|b|\). With \(b < 0\), \(|b| = -b\), which simplifies to \(2(-b) = -2b\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{8x^3}\), where \(x < 0\).
qs.s: Since the index 3 is odd, \(\sqrt[3]{8x^3} = \sqrt[3]{8} \cdot \sqrt[3]{x^3} = 2x\). An odd root preserves the sign of the radicand, so no additional sign change is needed when \(x < 0\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{36x^2}\), where \(x < 0\).
qs.s: The principal square root must be non-negative: \(\sqrt{36x^2} = 6|x|\). Because \(x < 0\), \(|x| = -x\), which gives \(6(-x) = -6x\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{81a^2}\), where \(a < 0\).
qs.s: Since the radical has an even index, \(\sqrt{81a^2} = 9|a|\). Given that \(a < 0\), \(|a| = -a\), so the simplified form is \(-9a\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{125y^3}\), where \(y < 0\).
qs.s: Because the index 3 is odd, \(\sqrt[3]{125y^3} = \sqrt[3]{125} \cdot \sqrt[3]{y^3} = 5y\). Odd roots preserve the sign of the radicand, so the expression simplifies directly to \(5y\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(3x\sqrt{4x^2}\), where \(x < 0\).
qs.s: First simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{4x^2} = 2|x| = -2x\) because \(x < 0\). Multiplying by the outside factor yields \(3x(-2x) = -6x^2\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{49x^6}\), where \(x < 0\).
qs.s: Taking the square root gives \(\sqrt{49x^6} = 7|x^3|\). Because \(x < 0\), \(x^3\) is negative, so \(|x^3| = -x^3\), resulting in \(-7x^3\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[4]{81x^8y^4}\), where \(x > 0\) and \(y < 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the fourth root yields \(\sqrt[4]{81x^8y^4} = 3x^2|y|\) because \(x^2 \ge 0\). Since \(y < 0\), \(|y| = -y\), which simplifies to \(-3x^2y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt{25x^2y^4}\), where \(x < 0\) and \(y > 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the square root gives \(5|x|y^2\) since \(y^2 \ge 0\). Because \(x < 0\), \(|x| = -x\), giving \(5(-x)y^2 = -5xy^2\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt{25x^2} - \sqrt[3]{64x^3}\), where \(x < 0\).
qs.s: For \(x < 0\), the even root gives \(\sqrt{25x^2} = 5|x| = -5x\), and the odd root gives \(\sqrt[3]{64x^3} = 4x\). Subtracting them results in \(-5x - 4x = -9x\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-8y^3}, y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Since \((-2y)^3 = -8y^3\), the principal cube root evaluates directly to \(-2y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-64x^3}, x \ge 0\)
qs.s: Take the cube root of the coefficient and the variable: \(\sqrt[3]{-64} = -4\) and \(\sqrt[3]{x^3} = x\), giving \(-4x\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-125a^3}, a \ge 0\)
qs.s: Since \((-5a)^3 = -125a^3\), simplifying the cube root yields \(-5a\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-1000k^3}, k \ge 0\)
qs.s: Taking the cube root of \(-1000\) and \(k^3\) yields \(-10\) and \(k\), respectively, which gives \(-10k\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[5]{-243a^{10}b^5}, a \ge 0, b \ge 0\)
qs.s: Since \((-3)^5 = -243\), the fifth root of \(-243\) is \(-3\). Dividing the variable exponents by 5 gives \(a^{10/5} = a^2\) and \(b^{5/5} = b\), yielding \(-3a^2b\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(\sqrt[3]{-125x^3} - \sqrt[3]{-8x^3}, x \ge 0\)
qs.s: Simplify each radical first to get \(-5x\) and \(-2x\). Then subtract: \(-5x - (-2x) = -5x + 2x = -3x\).

qs.q: Simplify: \(-3\sqrt[3]{-8x^9}, x \ge 0\)
qs.s: First simplify the radical to get \(\sqrt[3]{-8x^9} = -2x^3\). Then multiply by the coefficient: \(-3(-2x^3) = 6x^3\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-64x^6y^3}, x \ge 0, y \ge 0\)
qs.s: Take the cube root of each factor: \(\sqrt[3]{-64} = -4\), \(\sqrt[3]{x^6} = x^{6/3} = x^2\), and \(\sqrt[3]{y^3} = y\), giving \(-4x^2y\).

qs.q: Simplify the radical: \(\sqrt[3]{-\frac{27x^3}{125y^6}}, x \ge 0, y > 0\)
qs.s: Compute the cube roots of the numerator and denominator separately: \(\sqrt[3]{-27x^3} = -3x\) and \(\sqrt[3]{125y^6} = 5y^2\), giving \(-\frac{3x}{5y^2}\).

exercises.name: Domain and Range of Radical Functions

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -x\)
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: The linear function \(y = -x\) has no restrictions on \(x\), so the domain is all real numbers. As \(x\) takes all real values, \(y\) also takes all real values, so the range is all real numbers.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{x}\)
d: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: The radicand of an even root must be non-negative, so the domain is \(x \ge 0\). The principal square root produces only non-negative outputs, so the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt[3]{x}\)
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Because the index 3 is odd, real cube roots exist for all real numbers, so the domain is all real numbers. The outputs can be any positive, negative, or zero value, so the range is all real numbers.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = 4\sqrt{12 - 3x} - 1\)
qs.s: Set \(12 - 3x \ge 0\), which gives \(-3x \ge -12\) and flips the inequality to \(x \le 4\) for the domain. Since \(4\sqrt{12 - 3x} \ge 0\), subtracting 1 yields the range \(y \ge -1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -2\sqrt{4x - 8} + 7\)
qs.s: Set \(4x - 8 \ge 0\) to get \(4x \ge 8\), which means \(x \ge 2\) for the domain. Because \(-2\sqrt{4x - 8} \le 0\), adding 7 sets an upper bound of 7, so the range is \(y \le 7\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = 2\sqrt{3x - 6} + 5\)
qs.s: Set the radicand \(3x - 6 \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(3x \ge 6\), or \(x \ge 2\) for the domain. Since \(2\sqrt{3x - 6} \ge 0\), adding 5 gives a minimum value of 5, so the range is \(y \ge 5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -2\sqrt[4]{5x + 15} - 3\)
qs.s: The index 4 is even, so set \(5x + 15 \ge 0\), which solves to \(x \ge -3\) for the domain. Since \(-2\sqrt[4]{5x + 15} \le 0\), subtracting 3 gives a maximum value of \(-3\), so the range is \(y \le -3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = 5 - 3\sqrt{10 - 2x}\)
qs.s: Set \(10 - 2x \ge 0\), yielding \(-2x \ge -10\), which divides by \(-2\) to give the domain \(x \le 5\). Since \(-3\sqrt{10 - 2x} \le 0\), adding 5 gives \(y \le 5\) for the range.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = \sqrt{x - 2}\).
qs.s: Set the radicand non-negative to get \(x - 2 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 2\). Since the principal square root is non-negative, the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = \sqrt[3]{x}\).
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Because the index 3 is odd, the cube root is defined for all real numbers and produces all real outputs. Therefore, both the domain and range are all real numbers.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x}\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x \ge 0\). Since the principal square root is non-negative, multiplying by \(-1\) gives \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{2x - 8} + 3\).
qs.s: The radicand requires \(2x - 8 \ge 0\), which solves to \(x \ge 4\). Since \(-\sqrt{2x - 8} \le 0\), adding 3 results in a range of \(y \le 3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{10 - 2x} - 4\).
qs.s: Setting \(10 - 2x \ge 0\) gives \(x \le 5\) after dividing by \(-2\). Since \(-\sqrt{10 - 2x} \le 0\), subtracting 4 yields \(y \le -4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = 2\sqrt{12 - 4x} + 5\).
qs.s: Solving \(12 - 4x \ge 0\) gives \(-4x \ge -12\), so \(x \le 3\). Since \(2\sqrt{12 - 4x} \ge 0\), adding 5 gives \(y \ge 5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt[4]{3x - 6} + 1\).
d: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: For an even index of 4, the radicand must satisfy \(3x - 6 \ge 0\), so \(x \ge 2\). Because \(-\sqrt[4]{3x - 6} \le 0\), adding 1 gives \(y \le 1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = \sqrt{x^2 - 25}\).
qs.s: The radicand must satisfy \(x^2 - 25 \ge 0\), which means \(x^2 \ge 25\), so \(x \le -5\) or \(x \ge 5\). The principal square root is always non-negative with a minimum value of 0, so \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{x + 4}\)
qs.s: Solve \(x + 4 \ge 0\) to find the domain, giving \(x \ge -4\). The principal square root is always non-negative, so the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{5 - x}\)
qs.s: For the domain, the radicand must be non-negative: \(5 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 5\). Since the principal square root produces non-negative values, the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{2 - x}\)
qs.s: Set the radicand to be non-negative: \(2 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 2\). The output of a principal square root is always greater than or equal to zero, giving the range \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{8 - x}\)
qs.s: The expression under the radical must be non-negative: \(8 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 8\). Because the square root function outputs non-negative real numbers, the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{x - 3}\)
qs.s: For the domain, set the radicand greater than or equal to zero: \(x - 3 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 3\). The principal square root cannot be negative, so the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{2x - 10} + 4\)
qs.s: For the domain, solve \(2x - 10 \ge 0 \implies 2x \ge 10 \implies x \ge 5\). Since \(\sqrt{2x - 10} \ge 0\), adding 4 yields the range \(y \ge 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{4x - 12} - 3\)
qs.s: Solve \(4x - 12 \ge 0 \implies 4x \ge 12 \implies x \ge 3\) for the domain. Since \(-\sqrt{4x - 12} \le 0\), subtracting 3 gives the range \(y \le -3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = \sqrt{18 - 3x} - 2\)
qs.s: The domain requires \(18 - 3x \ge 0 \implies -3x \ge -18 \implies x \le 6\). Since \(\sqrt{18 - 3x} \ge 0\), subtracting 2 gives the range \(y \ge -2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{x + 8} + 5\)
qs.s: The radicand must satisfy \(x + 8 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -8\). Because \(-\sqrt{x + 8} \le 0\), adding 5 results in the range \(y \le 5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = 3\sqrt{7 - x} - 6\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(7 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 7\). Since \(3\sqrt{7 - x} \ge 0\), subtracting 6 yields the range \(y \ge -6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{5 - x}\).
qs.s: Setting the radicand \(5 - x \ge 0\) gives \(-x \ge -5\), so \(x \le 5\). Because \(-\sqrt{5 - x} \le 0\), the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = \sqrt{8 - x}\).
qs.s: The expression under the radical must be non-negative: \(8 - x \ge 0\), which gives \(x \le 8\). The output of a principal square root is non-negative, so the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x + 7}\).
qs.s: Setting the radicand \(x + 7 \ge 0\) gives \(x \ge -7\) for the domain. Because of the negative sign in front of the radical, the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x - 4}\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x - 4 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 4\). Since the principal square root is non-negative and multiplied by \(-1\), the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = \sqrt{x - 6}\).
qs.s: For the square root to exist, \(x - 6 \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(x \ge 6\). Since the radical is positive, the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{16 - 4x} + 6\).
qs.s: The radicand requires \(16 - 4x \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(-4x \ge -16\) or \(x \le 4\). Since \(-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{16 - 4x} \le 0\), adding \(6\) gives the range \(y \le 6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt[4]{5x - 15} - 2\).
d: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Because the index \(4\) is even, the radicand must satisfy \(5x - 15 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 3\). Since \(-\sqrt[4]{5x - 15} \le 0\), subtracting \(2\) gives a range of \(y \le -2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -2\sqrt[3]{x - 5} + 4\).
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Since the index is odd (\(n = 3\)), the radicand can take any real value and the output takes all real values. Thus, both the domain and range are all real numbers.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = 2\sqrt{12 - 3x} - 5\).
qs.s: For the square root to be real, \(12 - 3x \ge 0 \implies -3x \ge -12 \implies x \le 4\). Since \(2\sqrt{12 - 3x} \ge 0\), subtracting \(5\) gives a range of \(y \ge -5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y - 2 = \sqrt{5 - x}\).
qs.s: The radicand must satisfy \(5 - x \ge 0\), which gives \(x \le 5\). Since \(\sqrt{5 - x} \ge 0\), isolating \(y\) gives \(y = \sqrt{5 - x} + 2 \ge 2\), so the range is \(y \ge 2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y - 1 = \sqrt{x + 6}\).
qs.s: The radicand must satisfy \(x + 6 \ge 0\), so \(x \ge -6\). Since \(\sqrt{x + 6} \ge 0\), \(y = \sqrt{x + 6} + 1 \ge 1\), which gives range \(y \ge 1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y + 6 = \sqrt{x + 9}\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x + 9 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -9\). Since \(\sqrt{x + 9} \ge 0\), we have \(y = \sqrt{x + 9} - 6 \ge -6\), giving range \(y \ge -6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y + 5 = \sqrt{7 - x}\).
qs.s: For the radicand to be non-negative, \(7 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 7\). Since \(\sqrt{7 - x} \ge 0\), isolating \(y\) gives \(y = \sqrt{7 - x} - 5 \ge -5\), so the range is \(y \ge -5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y - 4 = \sqrt{x - 3}\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x - 3 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 3\). Since \(\sqrt{x - 3} \ge 0\), we have \(y = \sqrt{x - 3} + 4 \ge 4\), giving range \(y \ge 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(6 - 2y = \sqrt{15 - 6x}\).
qs.s: The radicand requires \(15 - 6x \ge 0 \implies x \le \frac{5}{2}\). Since the principal square root is non-negative, \(6 - 2y \ge 0 \implies -2y \ge -6 \implies y \le 3\), giving range \(y \le 3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y + 3 = -\sqrt[4]{12 - 3x}\).
d: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Because the root index is even, \(12 - 3x \ge 0 \implies x \le 4\). Since \(-\sqrt[4]{12 - 3x} \le 0\), isolating \(y\) gives \(y \le -3\), so the range is \(y \le -3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y - 7 = -3\sqrt{2x - 10}\).
qs.s: The radicand requires \(2x - 10 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 5\). Because the radical is multiplied by \(-3\), we have \(-3\sqrt{2x - 10} \le 0\), which yields \(y \le 7\), giving range \(y \le 7\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y - 6 = -2\sqrt[3]{5 - x}\).
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Since the index is odd, the radicand can be any real number, so the domain is all real numbers. Likewise, the output of a cube root can take any real value, giving a range of all real numbers.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(3y + 12 = \sqrt{20 - 5x}\).
qs.s: Setting the radicand non-negative gives \(20 - 5x \ge 0 \implies x \le 4\). Since \(\sqrt{20 - 5x} \ge 0\), we have \(3y + 12 \ge 0 \implies y \ge -4\), so the range is \(y \ge -4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 6 = \sqrt{x - 8}\)
qs.s: The domain requires \(x - 8 \ge 0\), which yields \(x \ge 8\). Since \(\sqrt{x - 8} \ge 0\), isolating \(y\) gives the range \(y = \sqrt{x - 8} + 6 \ge 6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 3 = \sqrt{x - 5}\)
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x - 5 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 5\). Since \(\sqrt{x - 5} \ge 0\), solving for \(y\) gives \(y = \sqrt{x - 5} - 3 \ge -3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 1 = \sqrt{x + 6}\)
qs.s: Setting the radicand \(x + 6 \ge 0\) gives the domain \(x \ge -6\). Because the principal square root is non-negative, \(y = \sqrt{x + 6} + 1 \ge 1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 5 = \sqrt{x + 2}\)
qs.s: The radicand requires \(x + 2 \ge 0\), giving \(x \ge -2\). Since \(\sqrt{x + 2} \ge 0\), we have \(y = \sqrt{x + 2} - 5 \ge -5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 4 = \sqrt{x - 3}\)
qs.s: For the square root to be defined, \(x - 3 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 3\). Since \(\sqrt{x - 3} \ge 0\), isolating \(y\) yields \(y = \sqrt{x - 3} + 4 \ge 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 3 = -\sqrt{2x - 8}\)
qs.s: Setting the radicand \(2x - 8 \ge 0\) gives \(2x \ge 8\), so the domain is \(x \ge 4\). Since \(-\sqrt{2x - 8} \le 0\), the range is \(y = -\sqrt{2x - 8} + 3 \le 3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 5 = -\sqrt{12 - 3x}\)
qs.s: The domain requires \(12 - 3x \ge 0 \implies -3x \ge -12 \implies x \le 4\). The negative radical gives \(-\sqrt{12 - 3x} \le 0\), so the range is \(y = -\sqrt{12 - 3x} + 5 \le 5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 4 = \sqrt[3]{x - 7}\)
qs.a: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Because the index \(n = 3\) is odd, the radicand can be any real number and produces all real outputs. Thus, both the domain and range are all real numbers.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 2 = -\sqrt[4]{5x - 15}\)
d: Domain: all real numbers, Range: all real numbers
qs.s: Since the index 4 is even, the domain requires \(5x - 15 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 3\). The principal fourth root is non-negative, so \(-\sqrt[4]{5x - 15} \le 0\), yielding the range \(y = -\sqrt[4]{5x - 15} + 2 \le 2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 1 = \sqrt{6 - 2x}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(6 - 2x \ge 0 \implies -2x \ge -6\), so dividing by \(-2\) reverses the inequality to give \(x \le 3\). Since \(\sqrt{6 - 2x} \ge 0\), the range is \(y = \sqrt{6 - 2x} - 1 \ge -1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 1 = \sqrt{5x - 10}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(5x - 10 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 2\). For the range, since \(\sqrt{5x - 10} \ge 0\), we have \(y + 1 \ge 0 \implies y \ge -1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 4 = \sqrt{4x - 12}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(4x - 12 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 3\). For the range, since \(\sqrt{4x - 12} \ge 0\), we have \(y - 4 \ge 0 \implies y \ge 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 5 = \sqrt{2x + 8}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(2x + 8 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -4\). For the range, since \(\sqrt{2x + 8} \ge 0\), we have \(y + 5 \ge 0 \implies y \ge -5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 7 = \sqrt{2x + 6}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(2x + 6 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -3\). For the range, since \(\sqrt{2x + 6} \ge 0\), we have \(y - 7 \ge 0 \implies y \ge 7\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 2 = \sqrt{3x - 6}\)
qs.s: For the domain, the radicand must be non-negative: \(3x - 6 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 2\). For the range, since \(\sqrt{3x - 6} \ge 0\), we have \(y - 2 \ge 0 \implies y \ge 2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 7 = \sqrt{24 - 6x}\)
qs.s: Solving \(24 - 6x \ge 0\) gives \(-6x \ge -24\), so reversing the inequality yields the domain \(x \le 4\). Since the square root is non-negative, \(y + 7 \ge 0 \implies y \ge -7\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(3y - 9 = -2\sqrt{15 - 5x}\)
qs.s: Solving \(15 - 5x \ge 0\) gives \(-5x \ge -15 \implies x \le 3\) for the domain. Since \(-2\sqrt{15 - 5x} \le 0\), the range is \(3y - 9 \le 0 \implies 3y \le 9 \implies y \le 3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 1 = -\sqrt{20 - 4x}\)
qs.s: Solving \(20 - 4x \ge 0\) gives \(x \le 5\) for the domain. Because the radical has a negative coefficient outside, \(-\sqrt{20 - 4x} \le 0\), which gives \(y - 1 \le 0 \implies y \le 1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(2y + 6 = \sqrt{8x - 12}\)
qs.s: The domain requires \(8x - 12 \ge 0 \implies x \ge \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2}\). For the range, \(\sqrt{8x - 12} \ge 0 \implies 2y + 6 \ge 0 \implies y \ge -3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 8 = -\sqrt{3x - 15}\)
qs.s: The domain requires \(3x - 15 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 5\). Since \(-\sqrt{3x - 15} \le 0\), the range is given by \(y - 8 \le 0 \implies y \le 8\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 3 = \sqrt{2x - 10}\)
qs.s: For the domain, solve \(2x - 10 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 5\). For the range, \(y = \sqrt{2x - 10} - 3 \ge -3\) because the principal root is non-negative.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 1 = -\sqrt{2x - 8}\)
qs.s: For the domain, solve \(2x - 8 \ge 0\) to get \(x \ge 4\). For the range, \(y = -\sqrt{2x - 8} - 1\), and since \(-\sqrt{2x - 8} \le 0\), it follows that \(y \le -1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 6 = \sqrt{5x + 15}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(5x + 15 \ge 0 \implies 5x \ge -15 \implies x \ge -3\). For the range, \(y = \sqrt{5x + 15} + 6 \ge 6\) because the square root is non-negative.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 4 = -\sqrt{3x + 9}\)
qs.s: For the domain, solve \(3x + 9 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -3\). For the range, since \(-\sqrt{3x + 9} \le 0\), we have \(y = 4 - \sqrt{3x + 9} \le 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y + 8 = -\sqrt[4]{42 - 6x}\)
qs.s: Since the index 4 is even, the radicand must satisfy \(42 - 6x \ge 0 \implies x \le 7\). Because \(-\sqrt[4]{42 - 6x} \le 0\), we have \(y = -8 - \sqrt[4]{42 - 6x} \le -8\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(4 - y = \sqrt{20 - 5x}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(20 - 5x \ge 0 \implies -5x \ge -20 \implies x \le 4\). Isolating \(y\) gives \(y = 4 - \sqrt{20 - 5x}\), so \(y \le 4\) because the radical is non-negative.

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(2y + 5 = -\sqrt{6x - 15}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(6x - 15 \ge 0 \implies 6x \ge 15 \implies x \ge \frac{5}{2}\). For the range, \(2y = -5 - \sqrt{6x - 15} \le -5 \implies y \le -\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y - 7 = -2\sqrt{12 - 3x}\)
qs.s: Set \(12 - 3x \ge 0 \implies -3x \ge -12 \implies x \le 4\), reversing the inequality upon dividing by \(-3\). Since \(-2\sqrt{12 - 3x} \le 0\), we have \(y = 7 - 2\sqrt{12 - 3x} \le 7\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(2y - 9 = -3\sqrt{14 - 4x}\)
qs.s: For the domain, \(14 - 4x \ge 0 \implies -4x \ge -14 \implies x \le \frac{7}{2}\). For the range, \(2y = 9 - 3\sqrt{14 - 4x} \le 9 \implies y \le \frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{-5x - 15} + 2\).
qs.s: Set \(-5x - 15 \ge 0\), leading to \(-5x \ge 15\) and \(x \le -3\). Since \(-\sqrt{-5x - 15} \le 0\), the maximum value is \(2\), yielding the range \(y \le 2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{-x - 5} + 4\).
qs.s: For the domain, \(-x - 5 \ge 0 \implies -x \ge 5 \implies x \le -5\). Because \(-\sqrt{-x - 5} \le 0\), adding \(4\) yields the range \(y \le 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{-4x - 8} + 6\).
qs.s: The radicand must satisfy \(-4x - 8 \ge 0\), which gives \(-4x \ge 8\) and thus \(x \le -2\). The negative radical ensures \(-\sqrt{-4x - 8} \le 0\), resulting in the range \(y \le 6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{-2x + 10} - 5\).
qs.s: Solving \(-2x + 10 \ge 0\) gives \(-2x \ge -10\), so \(x \le 5\). Since \(-\sqrt{-2x + 10} \le 0\), subtracting \(5\) gives the range \(y \le -5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{-3x + 12} - 1\).
qs.s: Set the radicand greater than or equal to zero: \(-3x + 12 \ge 0 \implies -3x \ge -12 \implies x \le 4\). Since the square root is non-negative, \(-\sqrt{-3x + 12} \le 0\), which gives the range \(y \le -1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt[4]{14 - 4(x - 2)} - 3\).
qs.s: Expand the radicand to get \(14 - 4x + 8 = 22 - 4x \ge 0\), which yields \(-4x \ge -22\) and \(x \le \frac{11}{2}\). Because the fourth root has an even index, its principal value is non-negative, giving \(-\sqrt[4]{22 - 4x} \le 0\) and range \(y \le -3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^2 - 25} + 6\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x^2 - 25 \ge 0 \implies x^2 \ge 25\), yielding \(x \le -5\) or \(x \ge 5\). The radical takes all values in \([0, \infty)\), so \(-\sqrt{x^2 - 25} \le 0\), giving the range \(y \le 6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{45 - \frac{5}{3}(2x - 3)} - 8\).
qs.s: Simplify the radicand: \(45 - \frac{10}{3}x + 5 = 50 - \frac{10}{3}x \ge 0 \implies -\frac{10}{3}x \ge -50\), so multiplying by \(-\frac{3}{10}\) yields \(x \le 15\). Since the negative square root is at most \(0\), subtracting \(8\) gives the range \(y \le -8\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{18 - \frac{3}{5}x} + \frac{7}{2}\).
qs.s: Set \(18 - \frac{3}{5}x \ge 0\), which gives \(-\frac{3}{5}x \ge -18\), so multiplying by \(-\frac{5}{3}\) flips the inequality to \(x \le 30\). Since \(-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{18 - \frac{3}{5}x} \le 0\), the range is \(y \le \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{11 - 3(2x + 1)} + 4\).
qs.s: Expanding the radicand gives \(11 - 6x - 3 = 8 - 6x \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(-6x \ge -8\) or \(x \le \frac{4}{3}\). Since \(-\sqrt{8 - 6x} \le 0\), adding \(4\) gives the range \(y \le 4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain of the function \(y = \sqrt{25 - x^2}\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(25 - x^2 \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 \le 25\). Taking the square root yields \(-5 \le x \le 5\).

qs.q: Determine the range of the function \(y = \sqrt{x^2 - 16}\).
qs.s: For any \(x\) in the domain, the radicand \(x^2 - 16 \ge 0\) takes all non-negative values, with a minimum of \(0\) when \(x = \pm 4\). Since the principal square root is always non-negative, the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain of the function \(y = \sqrt{x^2 - 9}\).
qs.s: Set the radicand greater than or equal to zero: \(x^2 - 9 \ge 0\), which gives \(x^2 \ge 9\). Taking the square root gives the domain \(x \le -3\) or \(x \ge 3\).

qs.q: Determine the range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^2 - 36}\).
qs.s: The principal square root \(\sqrt{x^2 - 36} \ge 0\) with a minimum value of \(0\) at \(x = \pm 6\). Multiplying by \(-1\) reflects the values, giving the range \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain of the function \(y = \sqrt{x^2 - 1}\).
qs.s: Set the radicand greater than or equal to zero: \(x^2 - 1 \ge 0\), so \(x^2 \ge 1\). This gives the domain \(x \le -1\) or \(x \ge 1\).

qs.q: Determine the range of the function \(y = \sqrt{x^2 - 64} + 7\).
qs.s: The expression \(\sqrt{x^2 - 64} \ge 0\) reaches its minimum value of \(0\) at \(x = \pm 8\). Adding \(7\) shifts all output values up by \(7\), so the range is \(y \ge 7\).

qs.q: Determine the domain of the function \(y = \sqrt{100 - 9x^2}\).
qs.s: Set \(100 - 9x^2 \ge 0\), which gives \(-9x^2 \ge -100\). Dividing by \(-9\) reverses the inequality to \(x^2 \le \frac{100}{9}\), giving \(-\frac{10}{3} \le x \le \frac{10}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the range of the function \(y = -2\sqrt{x^2 - 9} + 6\).
qs.s: The radical \(\sqrt{x^2 - 9} \ge 0\) reaches its minimum of \(0\) at \(x = \pm 3\), so \(-2\sqrt{x^2 - 9} \le 0\). Adding \(6\) shifts the maximum value to \(0 + 6 = 6\), giving the range \(y \le 6\).

qs.q: Determine the domain of the function \(y = \sqrt{4x^2 - 49}\).
qs.s: Set \(4x^2 - 49 \ge 0\), which gives \(4x^2 \ge 49\) and \(x^2 \ge \frac{49}{4}\). Taking the square root gives \(x \le -\frac{7}{2}\) or \(x \ge \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^2 - 25} - 4\).
qs.s: For \(x\) in the domain, \(\sqrt{x^2 - 25} \ge 0\) with a minimum of \(0\) at \(x = \pm 5\), so \(-\sqrt{x^2 - 25} \le 0\). Subtracting \(4\) yields \(y \le 0 - 4\), so the range is \(y \le -4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{25 - x^2}\)

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{9 - x^2}\)
qs.s: The radicand requires \(9 - x^2 \ge 0\), giving the domain \(-3 \le x \le 3\). Since \(0 \le \sqrt{9 - x^2} \le 3\), multiplying by \(-1\) gives the range \(-3 \le y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{81 - x^2}\)

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{49 - x^2}\)

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{16 - x^2}\)

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{x^2 - 25}\)

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{9 - x^2} + 5\)
qs.s: The radicand requires \(9 - x^2 \ge 0\), giving \(-3 \le x \le 3\). Since \(0 \le \sqrt{9 - x^2} \le 3\), we have \(-3 \le -\sqrt{9 - x^2} \le 0\), and adding 5 gives the range \(2 \le y \le 5\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -2\sqrt{16 - x^2} + 3\)
qs.s: The radicand requires \(16 - x^2 \ge 0\), giving the domain \(-4 \le x \le 4\). Since \(0 \le \sqrt{16 - x^2} \le 4\), multiplying by \(-2\) and adding 3 yields a minimum of \(-2(4) + 3 = -5\) and a maximum of \(-2(0) + 3 = 3\), giving the range \(-5 \le y \le 3\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt[4]{16 - x^2}\)
qs.s: Since the radical index is even, the radicand must satisfy \(16 - x^2 \ge 0\), so \(-4 \le x \le 4\). Since \(0 \le \sqrt[4]{16 - x^2} \le \sqrt[4]{16} = 2\), multiplying by \(-1\) produces the range \(-2 \le y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the following function: \(y = -\sqrt{36 - 4x^2}\)
qs.s: The radicand requires \(36 - 4x^2 \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(x^2 \le 9\) and gives the domain \(-3 \le x \le 3\). The maximum value of \(\sqrt{36 - 4x^2}\) is \(6\) and the minimum is \(0\), so the range is \(-6 \le y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^3 - 125}\).
qs.s: Setting \(x^3 - 125 \ge 0\) yields \(x^3 \ge 125\), which simplifies to \(x \ge 5\). Because of the negative sign in front of the radical, the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = \sqrt{x^3 - 1}\).
qs.s: The expression inside the radical must be non-negative, so \(x^3 - 1 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 1\). The principal square root always outputs non-negative values, so the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^3 + 64}\).
qs.s: Setting the radicand non-negative gives \(x^3 + 64 \ge 0\), which leads to \(x^3 \ge -64\) and \(x \ge -4\). The negative sign outside the radical reflects the graph across the \(x\)-axis, so the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{1 - x^3}\).
qs.s: For the square root to be real, \(1 - x^3 \ge 0\), which means \(x^3 \le 1\) and therefore \(x \le 1\). The negative sign in front makes all output values non-positive, giving a range of \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^3 - 27}\).
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative, so \(x^3 - 27 \ge 0\), which gives \(x^3 \ge 27\) and thus \(x \ge 3\). Since the principal square root is non-negative and multiplied by \(-1\), the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt[4]{x^3 - 125} - 4\).
qs.s: Since the radical has an even index of 4, the radicand must be non-negative: \(x^3 - 125 \ge 0\), which gives \(x \ge 5\). The fourth root outputs non-negative values, so \(-\sqrt[4]{x^3 - 125} - 4 \le -4\), making the range \(y \le -4\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -2\sqrt{54 - 2x^3} - 1\).
qs.s: Setting \(54 - 2x^3 \ge 0\) gives \(-2x^3 \ge -54\), which flips the inequality to \(x^3 \le 27\), so \(x \le 3\). Since \(-2\sqrt{54 - 2x^3} \le 0\), subtracting 1 gives a range of \(y \le -1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}x^3 - 16} + 1\).
qs.s: Setting \(\frac{1}{4}x^3 - 16 \ge 0\) gives \(\frac{1}{4}x^3 \ge 16\), so \(x^3 \ge 64\) and \(x \ge 4\). Since the negative radical term is at most 0, adding 1 yields a range of \(y \le 1\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{x^2 - 16} + 2\).
qs.s: The radicand requires \(x^2 - 16 \ge 0\), which means \(x^2 \ge 16\), giving \(x \le -4\) or \(x \ge 4\). Since \(-\sqrt{x^2 - 16} \le 0\), adding 2 results in a range of \(y \le 2\).

qs.q: Determine the domain and range of the function \(y = -\sqrt{8x^3 - 27} + 5\).
qs.s: The radicand must satisfy \(8x^3 - 27 \ge 0\), so \(x^3 \ge \frac{27}{8}\), giving \(x \ge \frac{3}{2}\). Since \(-\sqrt{8x^3 - 27} \le 0\), adding 5 gives a maximum value of 5, so the range is \(y \le 5\).

qs.s: The graph is the upper half of a circle centered at the origin with radius \(2\), which corresponds to \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\) for \(y \ge 0\), or \(f(x) = \sqrt{4 - x^2}\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the graph of the radical function shown below?
qs.s: The function is defined for \(|x| \ge 3\) with \(x\)-intercepts at \((-3, 0)\) and \((3, 0)\) and passes through \((\pm 5, 4)\), which matches \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^2 - 9}\).

qs.q: Identify the function equation represented by the graph below.
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((-3, 0)\) and the graph passes through \((-1, 2)\) and \((5, 4)\), which satisfies \(f(-1) = \sqrt{2(-1) + 6} = \sqrt{4} = 2\), identifying the equation as \(f(x) = \sqrt{2x + 6}\).

qs.q: Which equation corresponds to the radical function displayed in the graph below?
qs.s: The graph has an endpoint at \((3, 0)\) and extends to the left through \((-1, 2)\) and \((-6, 3)\), showing a reflection across the \(y\)-axis and a shift right by \(3\), given by \(f(x) = \sqrt{-(x - 3)} = \sqrt{3 - x}\).

qs.q: Use the key features in the graph below to identify the corresponding equation.
qs.s: The graph has an endpoint at \((-4, 0)\) and opens downward and to the right through \((0, -2)\) and \((5, -3)\), representing a reflection across the \(x\)-axis and a shift left by \(4\): \(f(x) = -\sqrt{x + 4}\).

qs.q: Which equation represents the vertically compressed radical function shown in the graph below?
qs.s: The graph has \(x\)-intercepts at \((-4, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\) but a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, 2)\) instead of \((0, 4)\), indicating a vertical compression by a factor of \(\frac{1}{2}\) applied to \(\sqrt{16 - x^2}\).

qs.q: Determine which function equation matches the transformed radical graph shown below.
qs.s: The endpoint is \((4, 3)\) and the curve passes through \((3, 1)\), \((0, -1)\), and \((-5, -3)\), indicating reflections across both axes, a vertical stretch by \(2\), and shifts, giving \(f(x) = -2\sqrt{-(x - 4)} + 3 = -2\sqrt{4 - x} + 3\).

qs.q: Use the intercepts and points plotted on the graph below to find its matching radical equation.
qs.s: The two branches are symmetric about the vertical line \(x = 1\) with \(x\)-intercepts at \((-2, 0)\) and \((4, 0)\) and passing through \((6, 4)\) and \((-4, 4)\), which corresponds to \(f(x) = \sqrt{(x - 1)^2 - 9}\).

qs.q: Which function equation matches the graph shown below?
qs.s: Completing the square under the radical gives \(f(x) = \sqrt{9 - (x - 3)^2}\), which is an upper semicircle centered at \((3, 0)\) of radius \(3\) with intercepts \((0, 0)\) and \((6, 0)\) and peak \((3, 3)\), matching \(f(x) = \sqrt{6x - x^2}\).

qs.q: Which equation represents the translated radical function shown in the graph below?
qs.s: The graph is the upper semicircle of radius \(3\) translated \(2\) units to the right with center \((2, 0)\) and maximum at \((2, 3)\), which gives \(f(x) = \sqrt{9 - (x - 2)^2}\).

qs.q: Which function represents the graph shown below?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((-2, 3)\) and the curve opens downward to the right, showing a vertical reflection across the \(x\)-axis. Shifting the parent function \(y = -\sqrt{x}\) left \(2\) units and up \(3\) units yields \(f(x) = -\sqrt{x + 2} + 3\).

qs.q: Which function matches the graph shown below?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((3, -2)\) and the graph opens to the left, which indicates a reflection across the \(y\)-axis. In standard form \(y = \sqrt{-(x - h)} + k\), substituting \((h, k) = (3, -2)\) yields \(f(x) = \sqrt{-(x - 3)} - 2\).

qs.q: Which function is represented by the graph shown below?
qs.s: The graph has an endpoint at \((0, 1)\) and opens to the left (\(x \le 0\)), which indicates a horizontal reflection across the \(y\)-axis (replacing \(x\) with \(-x\)) and a vertical shift up by \(1\) unit. Therefore, the equation is \(f(x) = \sqrt{-x} + 1\).

qs.q: Which function is shown in the graph below?
qs.s: The graph has an endpoint at \((-1, -3)\) and curves upward to the left (\(x \le -1\)). The leftward direction indicates a horizontal reflection across the \(y\)-axis, giving \(f(x) = \sqrt{-(x - (-1))} - 3 = \sqrt{-(x + 1)} - 3\).

qs.q: Which equation corresponds to the radical function displayed in the figure?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((-3, 4)\) and the curve extends downward and to the left (\(x \le -3\), \(y \le 4\)). Factoring out the negative gives \(f(x) = -\sqrt{-(x + 3)} + 4 = -\sqrt{-x - 3} + 4\).

qs.q: Which radical function is represented by the given graph?
qs.s: The endpoint of the function is at \((-2, 3)\), and the curve extends upward and to the left (\(x \le -2\), \(y \ge 3\)). This indicates a reflection across the y-axis and translations of 2 units left and 3 units up, yielding \(f(x) = \sqrt{-(x + 2)} + 3\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the radical function shown in the graph?
qs.s: The endpoint is located at \((3, 2)\) and the curve opens downward to the right (\(x \ge 3\), \(y \le 2\)). This corresponds to a reflection across the x-axis and translations of 3 units right and 2 units up: \(f(x) = -\sqrt{x - 3} + 2\).

qs.q: Which radical function matches the graph shown?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((-4, -3)\) and the curve extends upward and to the right without reflections. This corresponds to the parent function \(y = \sqrt{x}\) translated 4 units left and 3 units down: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x + 4} - 3\).

qs.q: Which equation is represented by the graph below?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((4, 1)\), and the graph opens downward and to the left (\(x \le 4\), \(y \le 1\)). This requires reflections across both axes along with shifts of 4 units right and 1 unit up, resulting in \(f(x) = -\sqrt{-(x - 4)} + 1 = -\sqrt{4 - x} + 1\).

qs.q: Which equation represents the radical function graphed below?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((-3, 1)\) and the curve opens downward to the right. Using the key point \((-1, -1)\), we solve \(-1 = -\sqrt{b(-1 + 3)} + 1 \implies \sqrt{2b} = 2 \implies b = 2\), resulting in \(f(x) = -\sqrt{2(x + 3)} + 1 = -\sqrt{2x + 6} + 1\).

qs.q: Use the key features and points on the graph to determine which equation matches the function.
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((1, 2)\) and the graph opens downward to the left. Testing the y-intercept at \((0, -1)\), we have \(-1 = -a\sqrt{1 - 0} + 2 \implies a = 3\), giving \(f(x) = -3\sqrt{1 - x} + 2\).

qs.q: Which equation corresponds to the transformed radical function shown in the graph?
qs.s: The endpoint is \((3, -4)\) and the curve opens upward to the left. Using the grid point \((-1, 0)\), we find \(0 = a\sqrt{3 - (-1)} - 4 \implies 2a = 4 \implies a = 2\), which gives \(f(x) = 2\sqrt{3 - x} - 4\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the graph of the radical function shown?
qs.s: The endpoint is at \((-4, 1)\) and the graph opens upward to the right. Using the point \((4, 3)\), we have \(3 = \sqrt{b(4 + 4)} + 1 \implies 2 = \sqrt{8b} \implies 4 = 8b \implies b = \frac{1}{2}\), giving \(f(x) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{2}(x + 4)} + 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine which equation represents the radical function shown.
qs.s: The endpoint of the radical function is at \((3, -2)\) and the graph opens upward to the right. This corresponds to a horizontal translation of \(3\) units right and a vertical translation of \(2\) units down: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x - 3} - 2\).

exercises.name: Graphing Functions and Determining Domain and Range

qs.q: What is the range of the function \(f(x) = -5\sqrt{x}\)?
qs.s: Because the principal square root satisfies \(\sqrt{x} \ge 0\), multiplying by \(-5\) reverses the inequality to \(-5\sqrt{x} \le 0\), giving a range of \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{6x}\)?
qs.s: For the square root to be defined in the real number system, the radicand must be non-negative: \(6x \ge 0\), which simplifies to \(x \ge 0\).

qs.q: What is the range of the function \(f(x) = 3x^2\)?
qs.s: Since \(x^2 \ge 0\) for all real numbers \(x\), multiplying by \(3\) gives \(3x^2 \ge 0\), so the range is \(y \ge 0\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{-3x}\)?
qs.s: The expression under the square root must be non-negative: \(-3x \ge 0\). Dividing both sides by \(-3\) reverses the inequality, yielding \(x \le 0\).

qs.q: What is the range of the function \(f(x) = -4x\)?
qs.s: The linear function \(f(x) = -4x\) represents a non-horizontal line that extends indefinitely in both vertical directions, so its range is all real numbers.

qs.q: What is the range of the function \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 8\)?
qs.s: Since \(x^2 \ge 0\) for all real numbers, \(2x^2 \ge 0\), which means \(2x^2 - 8 \ge -8\). Thus, the range is \(y \ge -8\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(g(x) = \sqrt{20 - 5x}\)?
qs.s: Set the radicand greater than or equal to zero: \(20 - 5x \ge 0 \implies -5x \ge -20\). Dividing by \(-5\) flips the inequality, giving \(x \le 4\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^2 - 9}\)?
qs.s: The radicand must be non-negative: \(x^2 - 9 \ge 0 \implies x^2 \ge 9\), which is satisfied when \(x \le -3\) or \(x \ge 3\).

qs.q: What is the range of the function \(h(x) = -\sqrt{x + 7} + 5\)?
qs.s: Since \(\sqrt{x + 7} \ge 0\), multiplying by \(-1\) gives \(-\sqrt{x + 7} \le 0\), and adding \(5\) yields \(-\sqrt{x + 7} + 5 \le 5\), so the range is \(y \le 5\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{4x - 12}\)?
qs.s: Set the radicand greater than or equal to zero: \(4x - 12 \ge 0 \implies 4x \ge 12 \implies x \ge 3\).

qs.q: What is the range of the function \(p(x) = -\sqrt{6x}\)?
qs.s: Since \(\sqrt{6x} \ge 0\) for all \(x \ge 0\), multiplying by \(-1\) reflects the values downward to give \(-\sqrt{6x} \le 0\). Thus, the range is \(y \le 0\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(k(x) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}x}\)?
qs.s: The expression under the radical must be non-negative, so \(\frac{1}{4}x \ge 0\). Multiplying both sides by 4 gives \(x \ge 0\).

qs.q: What is the domain of the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{5x}\)?
