qs.q:
Which function has \(f(x) = g(x)\) for all \(x\)?
\(f(x) = 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 1)\right) - 3\)
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{\pi/4} = 8\), so a quarter-period shift of \(2\) units right converts the sine curve into a cosine curve: \((x - 1) - 2 = x - 3\).

qs.q:
Which function has \(f(x) = g(x)\) for all \(x\)?
\(f(x) = 4\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x + \pi\right) - 2\)
qs.s: Because \(\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x + \pi\right) = -\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)\), \(f(x) = -4\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right) - 2\); using \(\sin\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -\cos\theta\) confirms \(g(x) = f(x)\).

qs.q:
Which function has \(f(x) = g(x)\) for all \(x\)?
\(f(x) = -5\sin(3x - \pi)\)
qs.s: Since \(\sin(3x - \pi) = -\sin(3x)\), \(f(x) = 5\sin(3x)\); applying \(\cos\left(3x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -\sin(3x)\) gives \(-5\cos\left(3x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 5\sin(3x)\).

qs.q: What is the amplitude of the function \(y = -\frac{3}{5}\sin\left(2x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 3\)?
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the coefficient \(a\), so \(|a| = |-\frac{3}{5}| = \frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift of the function \(y = \frac{1}{2}\sin\left(3x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) - 2\)?
qs.s: Set the argument of the sine function equal to zero: \(3x + \frac{\pi}{4} = 0\), which gives \(3x = -\frac{\pi}{4}\), so \(x = -\frac{\pi}{12}\).

qs.q: What is the period of the function \(y = \frac{2}{3}\cos\left(4x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right) + 1\)?
qs.s: The period is given by \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b = 4\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the vertical displacement of the function \(y = \frac{1}{4}\cos\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) - 5\)?
qs.s: In the standard form \(y = a\cos(bx - c) + d\), the constant term represents the vertical displacement, which is \(d = -5\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift of the function \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\cos\left(2x - \frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + 4\)?
qs.s: Set the argument equal to zero: \(2x - \frac{2\pi}{3} = 0\), giving \(2x = \frac{2\pi}{3}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the vertical displacement of the function defined by \(2y + 9 = -4\sin\left(\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) - 5\)?
qs.s: Subtract 9 from both sides to get \(2y = -4\sin\left(\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) - 14\), then divide by 2 to get \(y = -2\sin\left(\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) - 7\). The vertical displacement is \(-7\).

qs.q: What is the period of the function \(y = 6\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{5}x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right) - 2\)?
qs.s: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{4\pi}{5}} = 2\pi \cdot \frac{5}{4\pi} = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift of the function \(y = -\frac{2}{5}\sin\left(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) + 3\)?
qs.s: Set the inside of the sine function to zero: \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{\pi}{6} = 0 \implies \frac{3}{4}x = -\frac{\pi}{6}\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{4}{3}\) gives \(x = -\frac{4\pi}{18} = -\frac{2\pi}{9}\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift of the function \(y = 4\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 1\)?
qs.s: Set the argument equal to zero: \(\frac{2\pi}{3}x - \frac{\pi}{2} = 0 \implies \frac{2\pi}{3}x = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{3}{2\pi}\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the amplitude of the function defined by \(3y - 6 = -12\cos\left(4x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 15\)?
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) by adding 6 to both sides to get \(3y = -12\cos\left(4x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 21\), then divide by 3 to find \(y = -4\cos\left(4x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 7\). The amplitude is \(|-4| = 4\).

qs.q: What is the period of the function \(y = -\frac{3}{5} \sin \frac{\pi}{2}\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right) + \frac{1}{2}\)?
qs.s: The period is calculated as \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{2}} = 2\pi \cdot \frac{2}{\pi} = 4\).

qs.q: What is the amplitude of the function \(y = -\frac{7}{2} \sin \frac{\pi}{4}(x + 1) + 3\)?
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the coefficient \(a\), which is \(\left|-\frac{7}{2}\right| = \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the period of the function \(y = -\frac{3}{4} \cos \pi\left(x - \frac{1}{3}\right) - 2\)?
qs.s: The period of a cosine function is given by \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b = \pi\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2\).

qs.q: What is the period of the function \(y = -\frac{5}{6} \sin\left(\frac{8\pi}{7}x - \frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + \frac{1}{3}\)?
qs.s: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{8\pi}{7}} = 2\pi \cdot \frac{7}{8\pi} = \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift of the function \(y = -4 \cos\left(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 5\).
qs.s: Set the argument to zero: \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{\pi}{2} = 0 \implies \frac{3}{4}x = -\frac{\pi}{2} \implies x = -\frac{2\pi}{3}\), which is a phase shift of \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) to the left.

qs.q: Determine the phase shift of the function \(y = 8 - 3 \cos\left(\frac{5}{3}x + \frac{5\pi}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Set the inside expression equal to zero: \(\frac{5}{3}x + \frac{5\pi}{6} = 0 \implies x = -\frac{5\pi}{6} \cdot \frac{3}{5} = -\frac{\pi}{2}\), indicating a phase shift of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) to the left.

qs.q: For the function \(y = -7 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 3\), what is the sum of the amplitude and the period?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|-7| = 7\) and the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}} = 12\). Their sum is \(7 + 12 = 19\).

qs.q: What is the period of the graph of the function \(y = 2 \sin \frac{\pi}{8}(x + 5) - 3\)?
qs.s: The period is calculated using \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{8}} = 16\).

qs.q: What is the amplitude of the graph of the function \(y = -7 \sin \frac{\pi}{2}(x + 3) - 4\)?
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the leading coefficient, \(|a| = |-7| = 7\).

qs.q: What is the period of the graph of the function \(y = -3 \cos \frac{\pi}{4}(x - 2) + 5\)?
qs.s: The period of a cosine function is given by \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b = \frac{\pi}{4}\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{4}} = 8\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift of the graph of the function \(y = -3 \cos\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) + 4\)?
qs.s: Setting the argument \(2x + \frac{\pi}{3} = 0\) gives \(2x = -\frac{\pi}{3}\), which solves to \(x = -\frac{\pi}{6}\), corresponding to a phase shift of \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) units to the left.

qs.q: For the graph of the function \(y = -8 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) - 5\), what is the sum of the amplitude and the period?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|-8| = 8\) and the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}} = 12\). Their sum is \(8 + 12 = 20\).

qs.q: What is the period of the graph of the function \(y = -5 \sin\left(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 2\)?
qs.s: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{8\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the amplitude for the graph of the function \(y = -5\cos 2\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - x\right)\)?
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the leading coefficient \(a\), giving \(|a| = |-5| = 5\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift for the graph of the function \(y = -\cos 2\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - x\right)\)?
qs.s: Setting the argument to zero gives \(2\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - x\right) = 0\), which yields \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\). Since \(x > 0\), the phase shift is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) to the right.

qs.q: What is the phase shift for the graph of the function \(y = -\sin 4\left(\frac{\pi}{8} - x\right)\)?
qs.s: Setting the argument equal to zero gives \(4\left(\frac{\pi}{8} - x\right) = 0\), which solves to \(x = \frac{\pi}{8}\), meaning a phase shift of \(\frac{\pi}{8}\) to the right.

qs.q: What is the period for the graph of the function \(y = -\cos 3\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)\)?
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) inside the cosine function is \(b = -3\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{|-3|} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the period for the graph of the function \(y = 4\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{8} - \frac{5}{6}x\right) - 7\)?
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) is \(b = -\frac{5}{6}\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{|-5/6|} = 2\pi \cdot \frac{6}{5} = \frac{12\pi}{5}\).

qs.q: For the graph of the function \(y = -5\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{3}x\right) + 4\), what is the sum of its amplitude, period, and vertical displacement?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|-5| = 5\), the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|-\pi/3|} = 6\), and the vertical displacement is \(d = 4\). Their sum is \(5 + 6 + 4 = 15\).

qs.q: What is the phase shift for the graph of the function \(y = -3\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6} - \frac{2}{3}x\right) + 1\)?
qs.s: Setting the argument to zero gives \(\frac{5\pi}{6} - \frac{2}{3}x = 0\), so \(\frac{2}{3}x = \frac{5\pi}{6}\), which yields \(x = \frac{5\pi}{6} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5\pi}{4}\) to the right.

qs.q: For the graph of the function \(y = -\frac{7}{3}\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 3x\right) + \frac{5}{3}\), what is the product of the amplitude and the period?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|a| = |-\frac{7}{3}| = \frac{7}{3}\) and the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|-3|} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\). Multiplying them gives \(\frac{7}{3} \cdot \frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{14\pi}{9}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift of the function \(y = -2 \sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{5} - \pi x\right) + 4\).
qs.s: Set the inside of the sine function equal to zero: \(\frac{3\pi}{5} - \pi x = 0 \implies \pi x = \frac{3\pi}{5}\), which yields \(x = \frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = 3 \cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6} - 4\pi x\right) - 7\).
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) is \(b = -4\pi\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the amplitude of the function \(y = -\frac{7}{2} \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - 2\pi x\right) - 5\).
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the leading coefficient: \(|a| = \left|-\frac{7}{2}\right| = \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift of the function \(y = 2 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\pi x\right) + 1\).
qs.s: Set the argument equal to zero: \(\frac{\pi}{2} - 2\pi x = 0 \implies 2\pi x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), which gives \(x = \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = -4 \sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{2} x\right) - 3\).
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) is \(b = -\frac{\pi}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\pi/2} = 4\).

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = 4 \sin\left(\frac{5\pi - 18\pi x}{12}\right) - 6\).
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) simplifies to \(b = -\frac{18\pi}{12} = -\frac{3\pi}{2}\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{3\pi/2} = \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: For the function \(y = -6 \sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4} - \frac{4\pi}{3} x\right) + 5\), what is the sum of its amplitude and its period?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|-6| = 6\) and the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|-4\pi/3|} = \frac{3}{2}\); their sum is \(6 + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{15}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = 7 \cos\left(\frac{11\pi - 16\pi x}{15}\right) - 3\).
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) is \(b = -\frac{16\pi}{15}\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{16\pi/15} = \frac{30}{16} = \frac{15}{8}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift of the function \(y = -\frac{3}{4} \cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6} - \frac{15\pi}{8} x\right) + 2\).
qs.s: Set the argument to zero: \(\frac{5\pi}{6} - \frac{15\pi}{8}x = 0 \implies x = \frac{5\pi}{6} \cdot \frac{8}{15\pi} = \frac{4}{9}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift of the function \(y = -5 \cos\left(\frac{7\pi - 12\pi x}{8}\right) + 3\).
qs.s: Set the numerator equal to zero: \(7\pi - 12\pi x = 0 \implies 12\pi x = 7\pi\), giving a phase shift of \(x = \frac{7}{12}\).

qs.q: Determine the amplitude of the function \(y = -\frac{5}{4} \cos 2\left(x - \frac{\pi}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the coefficient \(a\). Here, the amplitude is \(\left|-\frac{5}{4}\right| = \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift for the graph of the function \(y = \frac{1}{2} \sin 2\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: In the factored form \(y = a \sin b(x - c)\), setting \(x + \frac{\pi}{3} = 0\) yields \(x = -\frac{\pi}{3}\), which corresponds to a phase shift of \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) to the left.

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = \frac{3}{4} \sin \frac{1}{2}\left(x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
qs.s: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = \frac{1}{2}\), the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{1/2} = 4\pi\).

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = \frac{5}{2} \cos 3\left(x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \cos b(x - c)\) is given by \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|}\). Since \(b = 3\), the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift for the graph of the function \(y = 5 \cos\left(\frac{7x - 3\pi}{4}\right) + 8\).
qs.s: Set the argument of cosine to zero: \(\frac{7x - 3\pi}{4} = 0 \implies 7x = 3\pi \implies x = \frac{3\pi}{7}\). Therefore, the phase shift is \(\frac{3\pi}{7}\) to the right.

qs.q: Determine the period of the function \(y = \frac{7}{3} \cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}x - \frac{2\pi}{3}\right) + 1\).
qs.s: The period is \(\frac{2\pi}{|b|} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{4\pi}{9}} = 2\pi \cdot \frac{9}{4\pi} = \frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the amplitude of the function \(y = -\frac{13}{3} - \frac{17}{4} \cos\left(\frac{5}{2}x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is given by the absolute value of the coefficient of the cosine term, \(|a| = \left|-\frac{17}{4}\right| = \frac{17}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the phase shift for the graph of the function \(y = -4 \sin\left(\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{9\pi}{10}\right) - 2\).
qs.s: Set the inside of the sine function equal to zero: \(\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{9\pi}{10} = 0 \implies x = -\frac{9\pi}{10} \cdot \frac{5}{3} = -\frac{3\pi}{2}\). This corresponds to a phase shift of \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) to the left.

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 4 \tan \frac{1}{5} x\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan bx\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = \frac{1}{5}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{1/5} = 5\pi\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -5 \tan \frac{1}{6} x\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan bx\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = \frac{1}{6}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{1/6} = 6\pi\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -2 \tan \frac{1}{4} x\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan bx\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = \frac{1}{4}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{1/4} = 4\pi\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = \frac{1}{2} \tan 3x\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan bx\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = 3\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 3 \tan 4x\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan bx\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = 4\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 5 \tan\left(\frac{\pi - 6x}{4}\right)\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the argument as \(-\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{\pi}{4}\), which gives \(b = -\frac{3}{2}\). Because the period must be positive, \(P = \frac{\pi}{|-3/2|} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -4 \tan\left(\frac{3}{7}x - \frac{\pi}{6}\right) + 2\)?
qs.s: For \(y = a \tan(bx - c) + d\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b = \frac{3}{7}\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{3/7} = \frac{7\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 3 \tan\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}x + \pi\right) - 7\)?
qs.s: For \(y = a \tan(bx - c) + d\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). Here \(b = \frac{2\pi}{5}\), so the period is \(\frac{\pi}{\frac{2\pi}{5}} = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -7 \tan\left(-\frac{5}{8}x + \frac{3\pi}{2}\right) + 4\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan(bx - c) + d\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = -\frac{5}{8}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{|-5/8|} = \frac{8\pi}{5}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -2 \tan\left(\frac{5\pi}{12}x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) + 1\)?
qs.s: The period is given by \(\frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = \frac{5\pi}{12}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{\frac{5\pi}{12}} = \frac{12}{5}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 2 \tan \frac{\pi}{5} x\)?
qs.s: Using \(P = \frac{\pi}{|b|}\) with \(b = \frac{\pi}{5}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{\pi/5} = 5\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 5 \tan \frac{\pi}{3} x\)?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{\pi}{|b|}\). Substituting \(b = \frac{\pi}{3}\) gives \(P = \frac{\pi}{\pi/3} = 3\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 3 \tan \frac{\pi}{4} x\)?
qs.s: The period of \(y = a \tan bx\) is given by \(P = \frac{\pi}{|b|}\). Since \(b = \frac{\pi}{4}\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{\pi/4} = 4\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -\frac{1}{2} \tan 4x\)?
qs.s: Using the formula \(P = \frac{\pi}{|b|}\) with \(b = 4\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -\tan 3x\)?
qs.s: The period of a tangent function is \(P = \frac{\pi}{|b|}\). With \(b = 3\), the period is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = \frac{1}{3} \tan\left(\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) - 7\)?
qs.s: The coefficient of \(x\) is \(b = \frac{2}{5}\). Therefore, the period is \(P = \frac{\pi}{2/5} = \frac{5\pi}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 4 \tan\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 1\)?
qs.s: The period depends solely on the horizontal coefficient \(b = \frac{3\pi}{4}\). Thus, the period is \(P = \frac{\pi}{|3\pi/4|} = \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -5 \tan\left(\frac{\pi x - 2\pi}{6}\right) + 2\)?
qs.s: Expanding the argument gives \(\frac{\pi}{6}x - \frac{\pi}{3}\), so \(b = \frac{\pi}{6}\). The period is \(P = \frac{\pi}{\pi/6} = 6\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = 7 \tan\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}(x + 3)\right) - 5\)?
qs.s: In the factored form \(y = a \tan b(x - c) + d\), \(b = \frac{4\pi}{9}\). The period is \(P = \frac{\pi}{|4\pi/9|} = \frac{9}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the period of \(y = -2 \tan\left(-\frac{5\pi}{6}x + \pi\right) + 3\)?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{\pi}{|b|}\). Since \(b = -\frac{5\pi}{6}\), we take the absolute value to get \(P = \frac{\pi}{|-5\pi/6|} = \frac{6}{5}\).

qs.q: Determine an equation for the graph shown below in the form \(y = a\cos(b(x-c))\), where \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(c\) is the least non-negative real number.
qs.s: The maximum value is \(3\) and the minimum is \(-3\), so the amplitude is \(a = 3\). The distance between consecutive peaks at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 5\) gives period \(T = 4\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). The first peak for \(x \ge 0\) occurs at \(x = 1\), giving \(c = 1\), so the equation is \(y = 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(x - 1)\right)\).

qs.q: Determine an equation for the graph shown below in the form \(y = a\sin(b(x-c))\), where \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(c\) is the least non-negative real number.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = 2\). The distance from the peak at \(x = 3\) to the trough at \(x = 7\) is half a period, so \(T = 8\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). The graph crosses the midline \(y = 0\) while increasing at \(x = 1\), so the least non-negative phase shift for sine is \(c = 1\), giving \(y = 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 1)\right)\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine equations in the forms \(y = a\sin(b(x-c))\) and \(y = a\cos(b(x-c))\), where \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\), and each \(c\) is the least non-negative real number.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = 1\) and the period is \(T = 4\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). The first increasing midline intercept for \(x \ge 0\) is at \(x = 2\), giving sine phase shift \(c = 2\), while the first peak for \(x \ge 0\) is at \(x = 3\), giving cosine phase shift \(c = 3\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((4, -1)\) and the closest minimum point of \((12, -9)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{-1 - (-9)}{2} = 4\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{-1 + (-9)}{2} = -5\). The period is \(2(12 - 4) = 16\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{16} = \frac{\pi}{8}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((6, 1)\) and the closest minimum point of \((18, -5)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{1 - (-5)}{2} = 3\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{1 + (-5)}{2} = -2\). The period is \(2(18 - 6) = 24\), giving \(b = \frac{2\pi}{24} = \frac{\pi}{12}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((5, 11)\) and the closest minimum point of \((15, -3)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{11 - (-3)}{2} = 7\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{11 + (-3)}{2} = 4\). The period is \(2(15 - 5) = 20\), which yields \(b = \frac{2\pi}{20} = \frac{\pi}{10}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((3, 8)\) and the closest minimum point of \((9, 2)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{8 - 2}{2} = 3\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{8 + 2}{2} = 5\). The period is \(2(9 - 3) = 12\), giving \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((1, 5)\) and the closest minimum point of \((3, -1)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{5 - (-1)}{2} = 3\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{5 + (-1)}{2} = 2\). The distance between the maximum and minimum is half a period, so the period is \(2(3 - 1) = 4\), which gives \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{7}{2}\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \(\left(2, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{\frac{7}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2} = 2\) and the midline is \(c = \frac{\frac{7}{2} + \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\). The period is \(2\left(2 - \frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{8}{3}\), which gives \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8/3} = \frac{3\pi}{4}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((15, 62)\) and the closest minimum point of \((45, -18)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{62 - (-18)}{2} = 40\) and the vertical displacement is \(c = \frac{62 + (-18)}{2} = 22\). The period is \(2(45 - 15) = 60\), giving \(b = \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{\pi}{30}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}, 7\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, -3\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{7 - (-3)}{2} = 5\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{7 + (-3)}{2} = 2\). The period is \(2\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\), which yields \(b = \frac{2\pi}{2\pi/3} = 3\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \sin bx + c\) (where \(b > 0\)) if it has a minimum point of \((2, -5)\) and the closest maximum point of \((6, 7)\).
qs.s: The period is \(2(6 - 2) = 8\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). Because \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4} \cdot 2\right) = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1\) coincides with the minimum point, the graph is reflected across the midline, giving \(a = -\frac{7 - (-5)}{2} = -6\) and \(c = \frac{7 + (-5)}{2} = 1\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - d)) + c\) (where \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(d\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of the maximum) if it has a maximum point of \((5, 9)\) and the closest minimum point of \((11, -3)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{9 - (-3)}{2} = 6\) and the vertical shift is \(c = \frac{9 + (-3)}{2} = 3\). The period is \(2(11 - 5) = 12\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\), and since the cosine function peaks when its argument is zero, the phase shift is \(d = 5\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((3, 8)\) and the closest minimum point of \((7, 2)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{8 - 2}{2} = 3\) and the vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{8 + 2}{2} = 5\). Half the period is \(7 - 3 = 4\), so \(P = 8\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\), with phase shift \(c = 3\) from the maximum.

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((5, 6)\) and the closest minimum point of \((11, -4)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{6 - (-4)}{2} = 5\) and the vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{6 + (-4)}{2} = 1\). The horizontal distance between the maximum and minimum gives half the period, \(\frac{P}{2} = 6 \implies P = 12\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\), with \(c = 5\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((1, 5)\) and the closest minimum point of \((4, -1)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{5 - (-1)}{2} = 3\) and the vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{5 + (-1)}{2} = 2\). The distance between the maximum and closest minimum is half the period, so \(\frac{P}{2} = 4 - 1 = 3 \implies P = 6\), giving \(b = \frac{2\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}\), and since the maximum occurs at \(x = 1\), \(c = 1\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((1, 4)\) and the closest minimum point of \((3, -2)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{4 - (-2)}{2} = 3\) and the vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{4 + (-2)}{2} = 1\). The half-period is \(3 - 1 = 2\), so \(P = 4\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\), with \(c = 1\) from the maximum.

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \((4, 1)\) and the closest minimum point of \((9, -5)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{1 - (-5)}{2} = 3\) and the vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{1 + (-5)}{2} = -2\). Half the period is \(9 - 4 = 5\), giving \(P = 10\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{10} = \frac{\pi}{5}\), with \(c = 4\) at the maximum.

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}, 5\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \(\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}, -19\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{5 - (-19)}{2} = 12\) and vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{5 + (-19)}{2} = -7\). Half the period is \(\frac{5\pi}{4} - \left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{3\pi}{2}\), so \(P = 3\pi\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{3\pi} = \frac{2}{3}\), with phase shift \(c = -\frac{\pi}{4}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(-\frac{1}{4}, 9\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, -15\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{9 - (-15)}{2} = 12\) and vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{9 + (-15)}{2} = -3\). Half the period is \(\frac{5}{4} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{3}{2}\), giving \(P = 3\), \(b = \frac{2\pi}{3}\), and phase shift \(c = -\frac{1}{4}\) gives \(x - c = x + \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{11}{4}\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \(\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}, -\frac{13}{4}\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{11/4 - (-13/4)}{2} = 3\) and vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{11/4 + (-13/4)}{2} = -\frac{1}{4}\). Half the period is \(\frac{3\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{4\pi}{3}\), giving \(P = \frac{8\pi}{3}\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8\pi/3} = \frac{3}{4}\), with \(c = \frac{\pi}{6}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{7}{2}\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \(\left(\frac{5}{3}, -\frac{9}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{7/2 - (-9/2)}{2} = 4\) and vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{7/2 + (-9/2)}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}\). Half the period is \(\frac{5}{3} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{3}\), giving \(P = \frac{8}{3}\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8/3} = \frac{3\pi}{4}\), with \(c = \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find a function in the form \(y = a \cos b(x - c) + d\) (\(a > 0, b > 0\)) if it has a maximum point of \(\left(\frac{\pi}{4}, 8\right)\) and the closest minimum point of \((\pi, -6)\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{8 - (-6)}{2} = 7\) and vertical displacement is \(d = \frac{8 + (-6)}{2} = 1\). Half the period is \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{4}\), so \(P = \frac{3\pi}{2}\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{3\pi/2} = \frac{4}{3}\), with phase shift \(c = \frac{\pi}{4}\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to determine a sine equation of the form \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\) with \(a > 0\) and \(0 \le c < 4\).
qs.s: The maximum value is \(2\) and the minimum is \(-4\), giving amplitude \(a = 3\) and vertical shift \(d = -1\). The cycle repeats every \(4\) units, so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). The function crosses its midline going upward at \(x = 1\), giving \(c = 1\) and \(y = 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(x - 1)\right) - 1\).

qs.q: The graph below shows a trigonometric function. Determine a cosine equation in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a < 0\) and \(0 \le c < 4\).
qs.s: The midline is \(y = 0\) and the amplitude is \(2\), so with \(a < 0\) we have \(a = -2\). The period is \(4\), giving \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Because \(a < 0\), the phase shift \(c\) corresponds to the location of a minimum, which occurs at \(x = 1\), yielding \(y = -2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(x - 1)\right)\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to find an equation of the function in the form \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a > 0\) and \(c\) is the smallest non-negative phase shift.
qs.s: The midline is \(y = 1\) and the amplitude is \(3 - 1 = 2\). The period is \(5 - 1 = 4\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Since the graph crosses the midline going upward at \(x = 1\), the phase shift is \(c = 1\), giving \(y = 2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(x - 1)\right) + 1\).

qs.q: The graph below shows a trigonometric function. Which cosine equation of the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\) (with \(a > 0\)) represents the graph?
qs.s: The maximum is \(1\) and minimum is \(-5\), giving amplitude \(a = \frac{1 - (-5)}{2} = 3\) and midline \(d = \frac{1 + (-5)}{2} = -2\). The distance between the peak at \(x = 2\) and trough at \(x = 5\) is half the period, so \(T = 6\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}\). A peak occurs at \(x = 2\), so \(c = 2\), yielding \(y = 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}(x - 2)\right) - 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to find an equation in the form \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a < 0\) and \(c = 0\).
qs.s: The midline is \(d = \frac{6 + (-2)}{2} = 2\) and the amplitude is \(|a| = \frac{6 - (-2)}{2} = 4\), so \(a = -4\). One full cycle runs from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 8\), giving period \(T = 8\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). With no horizontal shift (\(c = 0\)), the equation is \(y = -4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}x\right) + 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to write a sine equation in the form \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a > 0\) and \(-3 \le c \le 0\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{7 - (-3)}{2} = 5\) and midline is \(d = \frac{7 + (-3)}{2} = 2\). The distance between the peak at \(x = 2\) and trough at \(x = 8\) is half a period, so \(T = 12\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). The graph crosses the midline going upward one quarter-period before the peak, at \(x = 2 - 3 = -1\), giving \(c = -1\) and equation \(y = 5\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(x + 1)\right) + 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to find a cosine equation in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a < 0\) and \(0 \le c < 6\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|a| = \frac{8 - (-4)}{2} = 6\), giving \(a = -6\), and the midline is \(d = \frac{8 + (-4)}{2} = 2\). The distance between the peak at \(x = -2\) and the trough at \(x = 4\) is half a cycle, so the period is \(12\) and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). For an inverted cosine curve (\(a < 0\)), the phase shift \(c\) corresponds to a minimum, which is at \(x = 4\), yielding \(y = -6\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(x - 4)\right) + 2\).

qs.q: The trigonometric graph below is to be modeled by \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a < 0\) and \(0 \le c < 8\). Which equation represents the graph?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(|a| = \frac{4 - (-2)}{2} = 3\), so \(a = -3\), and the midline is \(d = 1\). The period is \(2(7 - 3) = 8\), giving \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). A vertically reflected sine curve (\(a < 0\)) crosses the midline moving downward at the phase shift; here that occurs midway between the peak at \(x = 3\) and trough at \(x = 7\), which is \(x = 5\). Thus, \(y = -3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 5)\right) + 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following equations does NOT represent the trigonometric function graphed below?
qs.s: The graph has a period of \(4\), midline \(y = -1\), amplitude \(2\), and a maximum at \(x = 1\). Evaluating \(y = 2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(x + 1)\right) - 1\) at \(x = 1\) gives \(2\cos(\pi) - 1 = -3\), which produces a minimum rather than a maximum, so it does not represent the graph.

qs.q: Use the graph below to find an equivalent equation written in the expanded form \(y = a \cos(Bx - C) + d\), where \(a > 0\) and \(B > 0\).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = \frac{5 - (-1)}{2} = 3\) and midline is \(d = 2\). The period is \(2(5 - 1) = 8\), giving \(B = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). Since a maximum occurs at \(x = 1\), the factored form is \(y = 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 1)\right) + 2\); distributing \(B\) yields \(y = 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) + 2\).

qs.q: The graph below shows a trigonometric function. Which equation in the form \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\), describes the graph?
qs.s: The graph has a maximum of \(4\) and a minimum of \(-2\), giving amplitude \(a = 3\) and midline \(d = 1\). The curve crosses the midline going upward at \(x = -1\) and completes a full cycle at \(x = 7\), yielding a period of \(T = 8\) (\(b = \frac{\pi}{4}\)) and a horizontal shift of \(c = -1\).

qs.q: The graph below shows a trigonometric function. Which equation in the form \(y = a \cos(bx) + d\), where \(a < 0\) and \(b > 0\), describes the graph?
qs.s: The graph reaches a minimum of \(-3\) at \(x = 0\) and a maximum of \(1\) at \(x = 3\), giving amplitude \(|a| = 2\) and vertical shift \(d = -1\). Because the minimum is located on the \(y\)-axis and \(a < 0\), no horizontal shift is required (\(a = -2\)), and the period \(T = 6\) gives \(b = \frac{2\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

qs.q: The graph of a trigonometric function is shown below. Which equation in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\), with \(a < 0\) and \(b > 0\), describes the graph?
qs.s: The maximum is \(5\) and the minimum is \(-1\), so the amplitude is \(|a| = 3\) and the midline is \(d = 2\). For \(a < 0\), a cosine curve begins at its minimum, which occurs at \(x = 1\), and with period \(T = 4\) (\(b = \frac{\pi}{2}\)), the equation is \(y = -3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}(x - 1)\right) + 2\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine which equation in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\), with \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\), represents the function.
qs.s: The maximum occurs at \((2, 2)\) and the minimum at \((5, -4)\), which gives amplitude \(a = 3\) and vertical shift \(d = -1\). The distance between consecutive peaks is \(T = 8 - 2 = 6\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}\), and the peak at \(x = 2\) corresponds to \(c = 2\).

qs.q: The graph of a trigonometric function is shown below. Which equation in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\), where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\), correctly represents this graph?
qs.s: The maximum is at \((1, 4)\) and the minimum is at \((3, -2)\), giving an amplitude of \(a = \frac{4 - (-2)}{2} = 3\) and midline \(d = \frac{4 + (-2)}{2} = 1\). The period is \(T = 5 - 1 = 4\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\), and the maximum at \(x = 1\) gives a phase shift of \(c = 1\).

qs.q: The function shown in the graph is written in the form \(y = a \cos(bx - c) + d\), where \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\), and \(0 \le c < 2\pi\). Which equation represents the graph?
qs.s: From the peak at \((2, 3)\) and trough at \((6, -5)\), we find amplitude \(a = 4\), midline \(d = -1\), and period \(T = 2(6 - 2) = 8\), so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). The factored form is \(4\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 2)\right) - 1\), which expands inside the cosine to \(4\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 1\).

qs.q: The graph below shows a periodic function. Which equation in the form \(y = a \sin(b(x - c)) + d\), with \(a < 0\) and \(b > 0\), correctly models this graph?
qs.s: The maximum is at \((1, 5)\) and the minimum is at \((7, -3)\), giving amplitude \(|a| = 4\), midline \(d = 1\), and half-period \(7 - 1 = 6\) (\(T = 12\), so \(b = \frac{\pi}{6}\)). A negative sine wave starts at its midline and moves downward, which happens midway between the peak and trough at \(x = 4\), so \(c = 4\).

qs.q: The graph of a trigonometric function is shown below. Which of the following equations does NOT represent this graph?
qs.s: The graph has midline \(d = 3\), amplitude \(2\), and period \(T = 8\) (\(b = \frac{\pi}{4}\)), with a maximum at \(x = 3\). Evaluating \(y = -2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}(x - 1)\right) + 3\) at \(x = 3\) yields \(-2\sin(\pi/2) + 3 = 1\), which is a minimum rather than the required maximum of \(5\).

qs.q: The graph below can be modeled by the equation \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\). Which pair of equations correctly describes the graph for \(a > 0\) and for \(a < 0\) using the phase shifts of smallest absolute value \(|c|\)?
qs.s: The graph has amplitude \(3\), midline \(d = 2\), and period \(T = 6\) (\(b = \frac{\pi}{3}\)). For \(a > 0\), the maximum closest to the \(y\)-axis is at \(x = 1\) (\(c = 1\)); for \(a < 0\), the minimum closest to the \(y\)-axis is at \(x = -2\) (\(c = -2\), giving \(x + 2\)).

qs.q: The graph below models a trigonometric function. Which equation in the form \(y = a \cos(b(x - c)) + d\), with \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\), and the smallest non-negative phase shift \(c \ge 0\), describes the graph?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(a = 5\), midline is \(d = -1\), and the half-period is \(3 - (-2) = 5\), giving \(T = 10\) and \(b = \frac{\pi}{5}\). For \(a > 0\), phase shifts correspond to maximums at \(x = -2 + 10k\); the smallest non-negative value is \(c = 8\) (since \(x = -2\) is negative).

qs.q: A weight attached to a spring oscillates vertically such that its displacement is given by \(y = 8 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right)\), where \(y\) is in centimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. At what time \(t > 0\) does the weight first pass through its rest position (\(y = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) gives \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{4}\right) = 0\), which first occurs when \(\frac{\pi t}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{4}{\pi}\) gives \(t = 2\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The prong of a tuning fork vibrates according to the equation \(d = 2 \cos(10\pi t)\), where \(d\) is the displacement in millimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. At what time \(t > 0\) does the prong first pass through the origin (\(d = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(d = 0\) gives \(\cos(10\pi t) = 0\), so \(10\pi t = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Dividing by \(10\pi\) gives \(t = \frac{1}{20}\text{ s}\).

qs.q: A buoy floats in the ocean such that its height above sea level is modeled by \(h = 3 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)\), where \(h\) is in meters and \(t\) is in seconds. What is the second time \(t > 0\) that the buoy passes through sea level (\(h = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = 0\), whose second positive solution occurs at \(\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{3\pi}{2}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{6}{\pi}\) gives \(t = 9\text{ s}\).

qs.q: A spring moves in simple harmonic motion according to the equation \(d = 5 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)\), where \(d\) is the displacement in centimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. At what time \(t > 0\) does the spring first pass through the origin (\(d = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(d = 0\) gives \(5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right) = 0\), so \(\frac{\pi t}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Solving for \(t\) yields \(t = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The horizontal displacement of a swinging pendulum is given by \(x = 6 \sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right)\), where \(x\) is in centimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. At what time \(t > 0\) does the pendulum first pass through the origin (\(x = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{5}\right) = 0\), which first occurs for \(t > 0\) when \(\frac{\pi t}{5} = \pi\). Solving for \(t\) gives \(t = 5\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The motion of a pendulum is described by the equation \(d = 12 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right)\), where \(d\) is the displacement in centimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. What is the sum of all times \(t\) in the interval \(0 \leq t \leq 9\) at which the pendulum passes through the origin (\(d = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(d = 0\) gives \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{3}\right) = 0\), so \(\frac{\pi t}{3} = \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}\), giving times \(t = 1.5\), \(4.5\), and \(7.5\) seconds in the interval \([0, 9]\). The sum of these times is \(1.5 + 4.5 + 7.5 = 13.5\text{ s}\).

qs.q: The average daily temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) in a mountain town is modeled by \(T = -16 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 8\), where \(t\) is the month of the year (\(t = 1\) is January, \(t = 2\) is February, etc.). In which month of the year does the temperature first reach \(0^\circ\text{C}\)?
qs.s: Setting \(T = 0\) yields \(-16\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 8 = 0\), which simplifies to \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\). The first positive solution is \(\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3}\), so \(t = 2\), which corresponds to February.

qs.q: The depth \(h\) of water in an experimental drainage canal relative to a sensor is given by \(h = 24 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 12\), where \(h\) is in centimeters and \(t\) is the time in hours. At what time \(t > 0\) does the depth first reach zero (\(h = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(24\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) + 12 = 0\), so \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\). The smallest positive angle where cosine equals \(-\frac{1}{2}\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\), so \(\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\), which gives \(t = 4\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: The water level \(h\) (in meters) relative to a pier during a tidal cycle is modeled by \(h = 6 \sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) - 3\), where \(t\) is the time in hours (\(0 \leq t \leq 12\)). At what time \(t > 0\) does the water level reach zero (\(h = 0\)) for the second time?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(6\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) - 3 = 0\), so \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\). The second positive solution is \(\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6}\), which yields \(t = 5\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A mass on a spring oscillates according to the equation \(S = 6 \cos\left(\frac{2\pi t}{3}\right)\), where \(S\) is in centimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. How many times does the mass pass through the origin (\(S = 0\)) during the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 12\)?
qs.s: The period of \(S = 6\cos\left(\frac{2\pi t}{3}\right)\) is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{2\pi/3} = 3\text{ s}\), during which the cosine function equals zero twice. In the interval \(0 \leq t \leq 12\), there are \(\frac{12}{3} = 4\) full periods, so the mass passes through the origin \(4 \times 2 = 8\) times.

qs.q: A buoy floats in the ocean such that its height \(h\) (in meters) relative to sea level is given by \(h = 3 \cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{5} t\right)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. What is the period of the buoy's motion, in seconds?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{2\pi}{5}} = 5\) seconds.

qs.q: The alternating voltage \(V\) (in volts) in an electric generator is given by \(V = 110 \sin(100\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. What is the frequency of the voltage, in cycles per second?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{100\pi} = \frac{1}{50}\) second, so the frequency is \(\frac{1}{P} = 50\) cycles per second.

qs.q: The alternating current \(I\) (in amperes) in an electrical circuit is modeled by \(I = 6 \sin(120\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. What is the period of the current, in seconds?
qs.s: The period is given by \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b}\). Here \(b = 120\pi\), so \(P = \frac{2\pi}{120\pi} = \frac{1}{60}\) second.

qs.q: The acoustic pressure \(p\) (in pascals) produced by a speaker is modeled by \(p = 8 \cos(250\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. What is the period of the sound wave, in seconds?
qs.s: The period is given by \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{2\pi}{250\pi} = \frac{1}{125}\) second.

qs.q: The horizontal displacement \(x\) (in centimeters) of a swinging pendulum from its rest position is given by \(x = -7 \cos(4\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. What is the amplitude of the pendulum's motion, in centimeters?
qs.s: The amplitude is the absolute value of the coefficient of the cosine function, so the amplitude is \(|-7| = 7\) centimeters.

qs.q: The height \(h\) (in meters) of a passenger on a Ferris wheel at time \(t\) (in seconds) is modeled by \(h = 28 - 25 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{30} t\right)\). What is the maximum height, in meters, reached by the passenger?
qs.s: The maximum height occurs when the cosine function equals \(-1\), which gives \(h_{\max} = 28 - 25(-1) = 28 + 25 = 53\) meters.

qs.q: The water depth \(h\) (in meters) in a harbor is modeled by \(h = 7 + 3 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6} t\right)\), where \(t\) is the time in hours after midnight (\(t = 0\)). At what time \(t > 0\) does the water level first reach low tide (minimum depth), in hours?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{\pi/6} = 12\) hours. Since the cosine function starts at its maximum at \(t = 0\), the first minimum occurs at half of the period: \(t = \frac{12}{2} = 6\) hours.

qs.q: A mass attached to a spring oscillates vertically so that its displacement \(d\) (in centimeters) from its equilibrium position at time \(t\) (in seconds) is given by \(d = 8 \sin(6\pi t)\). At what time \(t > 0\) does the mass first reach its maximum displacement, in seconds?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{6\pi} = \frac{1}{3}\) second. For a sine function starting at 0, the first maximum occurs at one-quarter of the period: \(t = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{12}\) second.

qs.q: The temperature \(T\) (in degrees Celsius) inside a greenhouse over a 24-hour period is modeled by \(T = 19 - 8 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{12} t\right)\), where \(t\) is the number of hours after midnight. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum temperatures, in degrees Celsius?
qs.s: The maximum temperature is \(19 + 8 = 27^\circ\text{C}\) and the minimum temperature is \(19 - 8 = 11^\circ\text{C}\). The difference between the extremes is \(27 - 11 = 16^\circ\text{C}\) (or twice the amplitude: \(2 \times 8 = 16\)).

qs.q: A piston in an engine moves according to the equation \(x = 5 \cos(40\pi t)\), where \(x\) is displacement in centimeters and \(t\) is time in seconds. How many complete cycles does the piston make in 4 seconds?
qs.s: The period of one cycle is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{40\pi} = \frac{1}{20}\) second, which means the frequency is 20 cycles per second. In 4 seconds, the piston completes \(20 \times 4 = 80\) cycles.

qs.q: The horizontal displacement \(x\) (in centimeters) of a swinging pendulum from its center is given by \(x = 12 \cos(3\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. Find the frequency of the pendulum in cycles per second.
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{3\pi} = \frac{2}{3}\text{ seconds}\). The frequency is the reciprocal of the period, giving \(f = \frac{3}{2}\text{ cycles per second}\).

qs.q: The electric current \(I\) (in amperes) in an alternating circuit is given by \(I = 6 \sin(100\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. Find the frequency in cycles per second.
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{2\pi}{100\pi} = \frac{1}{50}\text{ s}\). The frequency is the reciprocal of the period, so \(f = \frac{1}{P} = 50\text{ cycles per second}\).

qs.q: The pressure variation \(P\) (in pascals) produced by a sound wave is modeled by \(P = 3 \cos(500\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. Find the frequency of the sound wave in cycles per second.
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{500\pi} = \frac{1}{250}\text{ s}\), so the frequency is \(f = \frac{1}{P} = 250\text{ cycles per second}\).

qs.q: A weight bouncing on a spring has its displacement \(d\) (in centimeters) from equilibrium given by \(d = 8 \cos(10\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. Find the period of the motion in seconds.
qs.s: The period of the cosine function is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{2\pi}{10\pi} = \frac{1}{5}\text{ second}\).

qs.q: The height \(h\) (in meters) of a buoy bobbing in ocean waves is modeled by \(h = 2.5 \sin(0.4\pi t)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. Find the period of the buoy's motion in seconds.
qs.s: Using \(b = 0.4\pi\), the period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b} = \frac{2\pi}{0.4\pi} = 5\text{ seconds}\).

qs.q: A weight suspended from a spring bounces such that its displacement \(d\) (in centimeters) from its rest position is given by \(d = 16 \sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{5} t\right)\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. At what time \(t > 0\) (in seconds) does the weight first reach its minimum displacement?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{4\pi / 5} = \frac{5}{2}\text{ seconds}\). For a standard sine function, the first minimum occurs at \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the period, which is \(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{15}{8}\text{ seconds}\).

qs.q: An alternating current generator produces a voltage modeled by \(E = A \cos(bt)\), where \(t\) is in seconds and \(b > 0\). The voltage completes 50 full cycles every half second. What is the value of \(b\)?
qs.s: The frequency is \(\frac{50}{0.5} = 100\text{ cycles per second}\), so the period is \(P = \frac{1}{100}\text{ s}\). Since \(P = \frac{2\pi}{b}\), we have \(b = \frac{2\pi}{P} = 2\pi(100) = 200\pi\).

qs.q: The monthly average temperature \(T\) (in degrees Celsius) of a city is modeled by \(T = 12 - 15 \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right)\), where \(t\) is time in months. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum average monthly temperatures in degrees Celsius?
qs.s: The maximum temperature is \(12 - 15(-1) = 27^\circ\text{C}\) and the minimum is \(12 - 15(1) = -3^\circ\text{C}\). The difference between the extremes is \(27 - (-3) = 30^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: An alternating current is given by \(I = 15 \cos(120\pi t)\), where \(I\) is in amperes and \(t\) is in seconds. The frequency is the number of cycles completed in one second. How many complete cycles does the current make in 25 seconds?
qs.s: The frequency is \(f = \frac{b}{2\pi} = \frac{120\pi}{2\pi} = 60\text{ cycles per second}\). In 25 seconds, the total number of cycles completed is \(60 \times 25 = 1500\).

qs.q: The height \(h\) (in meters) of a rider on a Ferris wheel at time \(t\) (in seconds) is given by \(h = -28 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{45} t\right) + 32\). At what time \(t > 0\) (in seconds) does the rider first reach the maximum height?
qs.s: The period is \(P = \frac{2\pi}{\pi / 45} = 90\text{ seconds}\). Since the rider begins at the lowest point when \(t = 0\), the maximum height is reached at half of the period, so \(t = \frac{90}{2} = 45\text{ seconds}\).

qs.q: The temperature in a northern town is modelled by \(T = 20\sin\left[\frac{2\pi}{12}(x-3)\right]+10\) in °C, where x is the time in months and the pattern repeats every 12 months. For how many months of each year is the temperature below 0°? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: T < 0 means sin θ < −1/2, which happens for 1/3 of each cycle (from 7π/6 to 11π/6), so 12 ÷ 3 = 4 months.

qs.q: A Ferris wheel passenger's height is \(H = 10\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{15}t\right)+12\) metres, where t is in seconds. For how many seconds of each turn is the passenger higher than 17 m? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: H > 17 means sin θ > 1/2, which happens for 1/3 of each cycle (from π/6 to 5π/6); the period is 30 s, so 30 ÷ 3 = 10 s.

qs.q: The temperature in a greenhouse is \(T = 6\sin\left[\frac{2\pi}{24}(t-9)\right]+14\) in °C, where t is in hours. For how many hours of each day is the temperature above 11°C? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: T > 11 means 6 sin θ > −3, i.e. sin θ > −1/2, which holds for 2/3 of each cycle, so 2/3 × 24 = 16 hours.

qs.q: A mass on a spring has displacement \(y = 8\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}t\right)\) cm, where t is in seconds. For how many seconds of each cycle is y below −4 cm? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: y < −4 means sin θ < −1/2, which is 1/3 of each cycle; the period is 6 s, so 6 ÷ 3 = 2 s.

qs.q: The temperature in a lab is \(T = 10\sin\left[\frac{2\pi}{24}(t-6)\right]+15\) in °C, where t is in hours. For how many hours of each day is the temperature between 10°C and 20°C? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: 10 < T < 20 means −1/2 < sin θ < 1/2, which is 1/3 of each cycle (from −π/6 to π/6 and from 5π/6 to 7π/6), so 24 ÷ 3 = 8 hours.

qs.q: A predator population is \(P = 400\sin\left[\frac{2\pi}{12}(t-3)\right]+1000\), where t is in months and the pattern repeats every 12 months. For how many months of each cycle is the population above 800? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: P > 800 means 400 sin θ > −200, i.e. sin θ > −1/2, which holds for 2/3 of each cycle, so 2/3 × 12 = 8 months.

qs.q: A rider's height on a wheel is \(H = 12\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{18}(t-4)\right]+13\) metres, where t is in minutes. For how many minutes of each turn is the rider higher than 7 m? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: H > 7 means 12 sin θ > −6, i.e. sin θ > −1/2, which holds for 2/3 of each cycle; the period is 36 min, so 2/3 × 36 = 24 minutes.

qs.q: A buoy's height above its rest level is \(y = 6\sin\left[\frac{2\pi}{9}(t-2)\right]\) metres, where t is in seconds. For how many seconds of each wave cycle is the buoy more than 3 m below its rest level (y < −3)? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: y < −3 means sin θ < −1/2, which is 1/3 of each cycle; the period is 9 s, so 9 ÷ 3 = 3 s.

qs.q: In a simplified 360-day year, the temperature is \(T = 14\sin\left[\frac{2\pi}{360}(x-80)\right]+5\) in °C, where x is the day of the year. For how many days of each year is the temperature below −2°C? (Use exact values; no calculator.)
qs.s: T < −2 means 14 sin θ < −7, i.e. sin θ < −1/2, which is 1/3 of each cycle, so 360 ÷ 3 = 120 days.

qs.q: The monthly sales of hot chocolate kits at a café are approximated by \(S = 120 + 120 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t + 1) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. For what month are sales equal to 0?
qs.s: Setting \(S = 0\) gives \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t+1)\right] = -1\), so \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t+1) = \pi\) and \(t = 5\). Since \(t = 0\) is January, \(t = 5\) corresponds to June.

qs.q: Sales of heavy winter boots at a retail store are modeled by \(S = 250 + 250 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t + 4) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. For what month are sales equal to 0?
qs.s: Setting \(S = 0\) yields \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t+4)\right] = -1\), which implies \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t+4) = \pi\) and \(t = 2\). Since \(t = 0\) corresponds to January, \(t = 2\) corresponds to March.

qs.q: Sales of space heaters at a home improvement store are modeled by \(S = 80 + 80 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t + 3) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. For what month are sales equal to 0?
qs.s: Setting \(S = 0\) yields \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t+3)\right] = -1\), so \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t+3) = \pi\) and \(t = 3\). Counting from \(t = 0\) as January, \(t = 3\) is April.

qs.q: The sales of seasonal pool passes at a community center are approximated by \(S = 60 + 60 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t - 5) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. In which month are sales equal to 0?
qs.s: Setting \(S = 0\) gives \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t-5)\right] = -1\), which yields \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t-5) = \pi\) and \(t = 11\). Since \(t = 0\) corresponds to January, \(t = 11\) corresponds to December.

qs.q: The monthly sales of winter parkas at an outdoor store are modeled by \(S = 150 + 150 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t - 1) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. In which month are sales equal to 0?
qs.s: Setting \(S = 0\) gives \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t-1)\right] = -1\), which means \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t-1) = \pi\) and \(t = 7\). Since \(t = 0\) represents January, \(t = 7\) corresponds to August.

qs.q: The water level \(h\) (in centimeters) relative to a pier mark is approximated by \(h = 150 - 300 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t + 2) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. In which month does the water level reach 0 for the second time in the year?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) yields \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t+2)\right] = \frac{1}{2}\). The second solution in one period occurs at \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t+2) = \frac{5\pi}{3}\), which gives \(t = 8\), corresponding to September.

qs.q: A wildlife conservation group models the monthly net change in water volume \(V\) (in megaliters) of a wetland by \(V = 30 + 60 \cos \left( \frac{\pi}{6} t \right)\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. How many months elapse between the first and second times that the net change is zero (\(V = 0\)) during the year?
qs.s: Setting \(V = 0\) gives \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\), which yields \(t_1 = 4\) and \(t_2 = 8\). The time elapsed between these two occurrences is \(8 - 4 = 4\text{ months}\).

qs.q: The monthly profit \(P\) (in thousands of dollars) of a ski resort is modeled by \(P = 25 + 50 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{6} (t - 1) \right]\), where \(t\) is the time in months with \(t = 0\) corresponding to January. In which month does the resort break even (\(P = 0\)) for the second time in the year?
qs.s: Setting \(P = 0\) gives \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(t-1)\right] = -\frac{1}{2}\). The second solution in the cycle occurs at \(\frac{\pi}{6}(t-1) = \frac{4\pi}{3}\), giving \(t - 1 = 8\) and \(t = 9\), which corresponds to October.

qs.q: A floating oceanographic sensor bobs vertically in the water. Its height \(h\) (in meters) relative to mean sea level is given by \(h = 4 - 8 \cos \left[ \frac{\pi}{9} (t + 1) \right]\), where \(t\) is time in seconds. At what time \(t > 0\) does the sensor first reach mean sea level (\(h = 0\))?
qs.s: Setting \(h = 0\) gives \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{9}(t+1)\right] = \frac{1}{2}\). The first positive angle gives \(\frac{\pi}{9}(t+1) = \frac{\pi}{3}\), which simplifies to \(t + 1 = 3\), so \(t = 2\text{ seconds}\).

exercises.name: Modeling periodic phenomena with sinusoidal equations

qs.q: A buoy bobs up and down with ocean waves, completing a full cycle every 10 seconds. Its height reaches a maximum of 5 m and a minimum of 1 m. The buoy passes through its average height of 3 m moving upward at \(t = 2\) seconds. Write a sine equation for the buoy's height \(h\) (in meters) as a function of time \(t\) (in seconds).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{5 - 1}{2} = 2\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{5 + 1}{2} = 3\), and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{10} = \frac{\pi}{5}\). The buoy is at the midline moving upward at \(t = 2\), giving phase shift \(C = 2\).

qs.q: In a desert town, the temperature reaches a high of \(32^\circ\text{C}\) at 4:00 PM (\(t = 16\)) and a low of \(12^\circ\text{C}\) at 4:00 AM (\(t = 4\)). The temperature reaches its average value of \(22^\circ\text{C}\) at 10:00 AM (\(t = 10\), rising) and at 10:00 PM (\(t = 22\), falling). Assuming a 24-hour cycle, write a sine equation for the temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) as a function of time \(t\) (in hours after midnight).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{32 - 12}{2} = 10\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{32 + 12}{2} = 22\), and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{24} = \frac{\pi}{12}\). The temperature rises through the midline at \(t = 10\), so the phase shift is \(C = 10\).

qs.q: A Ferris wheel has a maximum height of 32 m and a minimum height of 2 m, completing one full revolution every 60 seconds. A rider reaches the average height of 17 m while ascending at \(t = 5\) seconds. Write a sine equation for the rider's height \(h\) (in meters) as a function of time \(t\) (in seconds).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{32 - 2}{2} = 15\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{32 + 2}{2} = 17\), and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{60} = \frac{\pi}{30}\). Because the rider is at the midline and ascending at \(t = 5\), the horizontal shift is \(C = 5\).

qs.q: At a coastal port, the water depth reaches a high tide of 14 m at 4:00 AM and a low tide of 6 m at 10:00 AM. The depth is at its average level of 10 m at 1:00 AM (rising) and 7:00 AM (falling). Assuming a 12-hour tidal cycle, write a sine equation for the water depth \(y\) (in meters) as a function of time \(t\) (in hours after midnight).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{14 - 6}{2} = 4\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{14 + 6}{2} = 10\), and the period is 12 hours so \(B = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Since the water depth is at the average level and rising at 1:00 AM, the horizontal shift is \(C = 1\).

qs.q: In a northern community, the daylight length reaches a maximum of 18 hours in late June (\(t = 6\)) and a minimum of 6 hours in late December (\(t = 12\)). The community experiences its average daylight of 12 hours in late March (\(t = 3\), increasing) and late September (\(t = 9\), decreasing). Write a sine equation for the daylight hours \(H\) as a function of time \(t\) in months.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{18 - 6}{2} = 6\), the midline is \(D = \frac{18 + 6}{2} = 12\), and the period is 12 months, giving \(B = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). The daylight is at the midline and increasing at month \(t = 3\), giving phase shift \(C = 3\).

qs.q: A child is swinging on a playground swing. The height of the seat reaches a maximum of 2.8 m above the ground at \(t = 0.6\) seconds and the subsequent minimum of 0.8 m at \(t = 1.4\) seconds. Assuming the height varies sinusoidally, write a sine equation of the form \(h = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D\) (with \(A > 0\)) for the height \(h\) (in meters) as a function of time \(t\) (in seconds).
qs.s: The half-period is \(1.4 - 0.6 = 0.8\) s, so \(P = 1.6\) s and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{1.6} = \frac{5\pi}{4}\). The amplitude is \(A = \frac{2.8 - 0.8}{2} = 1\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{2.8 + 0.8}{2} = 1.8\), and the rising midline occurs at \(C = 0.6 - \frac{1.6}{4} = 0.2\).

qs.q: Over a 24-hour cycle in an alpine valley, the temperature reaches a minimum of \(-6.5^\circ\text{C}\) at 5:00 AM (\(t = 5\)) and a maximum of \(9.5^\circ\text{C}\) at 5:00 PM (\(t = 17\)). Write a sine equation of the form \(T = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D\) (with \(A > 0\) and \(0 \le C < 24\)) for the temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) as a function of time \(t\) (in hours after midnight).
qs.s: The period is 24 hours, so \(B = \frac{2\pi}{24} = \frac{\pi}{12}\). The amplitude is \(A = \frac{9.5 - (-6.5)}{2} = 8\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{9.5 + (-6.5)}{2} = 1.5\), and the rising midline occurs a quarter-period before the maximum at \(C = 17 - \frac{24}{4} = 11\).

qs.q: A large Ferris wheel with a diameter of 70 m has its boarding platform at the lowest point, 4 m above the ground. The wheel rotates at a constant speed, completing one full revolution every 80 seconds. A rider boards a capsule at the lowest point at \(t = 0\). Write a sine equation of the form \(h = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D\) (with \(A > 0\) and \(0 \le C < 80\)) for the rider's height \(h\) (in meters) as a function of time \(t\) (in seconds).
qs.s: The wheel radius is the amplitude \(A = \frac{70}{2} = 35\), the midline is \(D = 4 + 35 = 39\), and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{80} = \frac{\pi}{40}\). Starting from the minimum at \(t = 0\), the rider ascends to the midline after one quarter-period at \(C = \frac{80}{4} = 20\).

qs.q: At a coastal monitoring station, water depth reaches a high tide of 15.6 m at 4:30 AM (\(t = 4.5\)) and the next low tide of 2.4 m at 10:30 AM (\(t = 10.5\)). Assuming the water depth varies sinusoidally, write a sine equation of the form \(y = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D\) (with \(A > 0\)) for the water depth \(y\) (in meters) as a function of time \(t\) (in hours after midnight).
qs.s: The half-period is \(10.5 - 4.5 = 6\) hours, so the full period is 12 hours and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). The amplitude is \(A = \frac{15.6 - 2.4}{2} = 6.6\), the midline is \(D = \frac{15.6 + 2.4}{2} = 9\), and the rising midline occurs a quarter-period before the maximum at \(C = 4.5 - \frac{12}{4} = 1.5\).

qs.q: At an Arctic weather station, the average monthly temperature follows a 12-month sinusoidal cycle, reaching a minimum of \(-28^\circ\text{C}\) in February (\(t = 2\)) and a maximum of \(8^\circ\text{C}\) in August (\(t = 8\)). Write a sine equation of the form \(T = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D\) (with \(A > 0\) and \(0 \le C < 12\)) for the temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) as a function of time \(t\) in months.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{8 - (-28)}{2} = 18\), the vertical shift is \(D = \frac{8 + (-28)}{2} = -10\), and \(B = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). The rising midline occurs a quarter-period before the maximum at \(C = 8 - \frac{12}{4} = 5\).

exercises.name: Modeling periodic phenomena with sinusoidal equations

qs.q: A windmill has blades that are 6 meters long, and its central hub is located 14 meters above the ground. The blades make one complete rotation every 8 seconds. A marker is placed at the tip of one blade, which starts at its lowest point at \(t = 0\) seconds. Which cosine equation models the height \(h(t)\) (in meters) of the marker above the ground at time \(t\) (in seconds)?
qs.s: The amplitude is the blade length (\(A = 6\) m) and the midline height is the hub height (\(D = 14\) m). For a period of \(P = 8\) s, \(b = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\), and starting at the lowest point gives \(h(t) = -6\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}t\right) + 14\).

qs.q: The water depth at the end of a dock varies periodically with the tide between a minimum of 1.5 meters and a maximum of 4.5 meters, completing a full cycle every 12 hours. High tide occurs at \(t = 0\) hours. Which cosine equation models the water depth \(d(t)\) (in meters) at time \(t\) (in hours)?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{4.5 - 1.5}{2} = 1.5\) m and the vertical displacement is \(D = \frac{4.5 + 1.5}{2} = 3\) m. With period \(P = 12\) h, \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\), and starting at high tide (maximum) at \(t = 0\) gives \(d(t) = 1.5\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right) + 3\).

qs.q: A weight attached to a vertical spring bounces up and down, completing one full cycle every 2 seconds. The total vertical distance between its lowest and highest positions is 10 cm. The weight is pulled down to its lowest position and released at \(t = 0\) seconds, where its height is 15 cm above the floor. Which cosine equation models the height \(y(t)\) (in cm) of the weight above the floor at time \(t\) (in seconds)?
qs.s: The amplitude is half the total range (\(A = 10 / 2 = 5\) cm) and the midline is \(D = 15 + 5 = 20\) cm. With period \(P = 2\) s, \(b = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\), and starting at the minimum height at \(t = 0\) yields \(y(t) = -5\cos(\pi t) + 20\).

qs.q: During light exercise, an athlete breathes in and exhales about 1.6 litres of air every 3 seconds. The volume of air in the lungs reaches its minimum of 0.4 litres at \(t = 0\) seconds. Which cosine equation models the volume of air \(V(t)\) (in litres) in the athlete's lungs at time \(t\) (in seconds)?
qs.s: The amplitude is half the exchanged volume (\(A = 1.6 / 2 = 0.8\) L) and the midline is \(D = 0.4 + 0.8 = 1.2\) L. With a period of \(P = 3\) s, \(b = \frac{2\pi}{3}\), and because the function starts at a minimum at \(t = 0\), \(V(t) = -0.8\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}t\right) + 1.2\).

qs.q: A small Ferris wheel has a radius of 8 meters and completes one full revolution every 40 seconds. A rider boards the wheel at its lowest point, 2 meters above the ground, at \(t = 0\) seconds. Which cosine equation models the rider's height \(h(t)\) (in meters) above the ground at time \(t\) (in seconds)?
qs.s: The amplitude is the wheel's radius (\(A = 8\) m) and the midline height is \(D = 2 + 8 = 10\) m. With period \(P = 40\) s, \(b = \frac{2\pi}{40} = \frac{\pi}{20}\), and starting at the lowest point requires an inverted cosine: \(h(t) = -8\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{20}t\right) + 10\).

qs.q: A giant observation wheel has a diameter of 150 meters and completes 2 full revolutions per hour. Passengers board capsules from a platform located 6 meters above the ground at the wheel's lowest point. Let \(t\) be the time in minutes after a passenger boards at \(t = 0\). Which cosine equation models the passenger's height \(h(t)\) (in meters) above the ground at time \(t\) (in minutes)?
qs.s: The radius gives \(A = 150 / 2 = 75\) m and the midline is \(D = 6 + 75 = 81\) m. Completing 2 revolutions in 60 minutes gives \(P = 30\) min, so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{30} = \frac{\pi}{15}\), leading to \(h(t) = -75\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{15}t\right) + 81\).

qs.q: An oceanographic research buoy bobs up and down with passing ocean waves. The crest of a wave lifts the buoy to a maximum height of 4.2 meters above the seabed, and the trough lowers it to a minimum height of 1.4 meters. A sensor records that the buoy takes 2.5 seconds to travel from a trough directly to the consecutive crest. Assuming the buoy is at a trough at \(t = 0\) seconds, which cosine equation models the height \(h(t)\) (in meters) of the buoy above the seabed at time \(t\) (in seconds)?
qs.s: Moving from trough to crest is half a period, so \(P = 2 \times 2.5 = 5\) s and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{5}\). The amplitude is \(A = \frac{4.2 - 1.4}{2} = 1.4\) m, the midline is \(D = \frac{4.2 + 1.4}{2} = 2.8\) m, and starting at a trough at \(t = 0\) gives \(h(t) = -1.4\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{5}t\right) + 2.8\).

qs.q: A piston inside an engine cylinder moves vertically in harmonic motion. The engine operates at 1200 revolutions per minute (rpm). The piston reaches its maximum height of 18 cm at \(t = 0\) seconds and has a stroke length (the distance between its minimum and maximum heights) of 6 cm. Which cosine equation models the height \(y(t)\) (in cm) of the piston at time \(t\) (in seconds)?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = 6 / 2 = 3\) cm and midline is \(D = 18 - 3 = 15\) cm. With 1200 rpm, the period is \(P = \frac{60}{1200} = \frac{1}{20}\) s, so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{1/20} = 40\pi\); starting at the maximum height at \(t = 0\) gives \(y(t) = 3\cos(40\pi t) + 15\).

qs.q: The water depth in a harbor is modeled by a cosine function. A low tide of 4.2 meters occurs at \(t = 0\) hours, and the consecutive high tide of 11.8 meters occurs 6.5 hours later. Which cosine equation models the water depth \(h(t)\) (in meters) at time \(t\) (in hours)?
qs.s: The time from low to high tide is half a period, so \(P = 2 \times 6.5 = 13\) h and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{13}\). The amplitude is \(A = \frac{11.8 - 4.2}{2} = 3.8\) m and midline is \(D = \frac{11.8 + 4.2}{2} = 8\) m; starting at low tide gives \(h(t) = -3.8\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{13}t\right) + 8\).

qs.q: In a high-altitude desert, the temperature fluctuates periodically over a 24-hour cycle. At 3:00 AM (\(t = 0\) hours), the temperature reaches its daily minimum of \(-8^\circ\text{C}\). The daily maximum of \(28^\circ\text{C}\) is reached 12 hours later at 3:00 PM. Which cosine equation models the temperature \(T(t)\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) as a function of the number of hours \(t\) elapsed since 3:00 AM?
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = \frac{28 - (-8)}{2} = 18^\circ\text{C}\) and the midline is \(D = \frac{28 + (-8)}{2} = 10^\circ\text{C}\). For a 24-hour period, \(b = \frac{2\pi}{24} = \frac{\pi}{12}\), and since \(t = 0\) is the minimum, \(T(t) = -18\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{12}t\right) + 10\).

exercises.name: Modeling periodic phenomena with sinusoidal equations

qs.q: A weight attached to a spring oscillates with an amplitude of 7 cm and a period of 2 seconds. If its displacement \(d\) is at its maximum of 7 cm when \(t = 0\), find an equation in terms of cosine that describes the displacement at time \(t\) seconds.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = 7\), and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{P} = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\). Since the displacement is at its maximum at \(t = 0\), the equation is \(d = 7 \cos(\pi t)\).

qs.q: An alternating voltage \(V\) in a circuit has an amplitude of 150 volts and a period of \(\frac{1}{120}\) seconds. If \(V = 150\) when \(t = 0\), find an equation in terms of cosine that describes this voltage.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = 150\), and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{P} = \frac{2\pi}{1/120} = 240\pi\). Since \(V = 150\) when \(t = 0\), the equation is \(V = 150 \cos(240\pi t)\).

qs.q: A sound wave produces an alternating pressure variation \(P\) (in pascals) with an amplitude of 6 pascals and a period of \(\frac{1}{200}\) seconds. If \(P = 6\) when \(t = 0\), find an equation in terms of cosine that models this pressure variation.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = 6\), and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{P} = \frac{2\pi}{1/200} = 400\pi\). Since \(P = 6\) when \(t = 0\), the equation is \(P = 6 \cos(400\pi t)\).

qs.q: The alternating current \(I\) (in amperes) in an electrical circuit has an amplitude of 12 amperes and a period of \(\frac{1}{50}\) seconds. If \(I = 12\) when \(t = 0\), find an equation in terms of cosine that describes this current.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = 12\), and the coefficient \(b = \frac{2\pi}{P} = \frac{2\pi}{1/50} = 100\pi\). Since \(I = 12\) when \(t = 0\), the equation is \(I = 12 \cos(100\pi t)\).

qs.q: An ocean buoy bobs vertically so that its height \(y\) (in meters) relative to sea level has an amplitude of 2 meters and a period of 8 seconds. If \(y = 2\) when \(t = 0\), find an equation in terms of cosine that models the height \(y\) at time \(t\) seconds.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(A = 2\), and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{P} = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\). Since the buoy starts at its maximum height at \(t = 0\), the equation is \(y = 2 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4} t\right)\).

qs.q: The voltage \(V\) in an electrical circuit oscillates between a minimum of \(-150\) volts and a maximum of 250 volts at a frequency of 60 cycles per second. If \(V = 250\) when \(t = 0\), find an equation in terms of cosine that models the voltage \(V\) after \(t\) seconds.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(\frac{250 - (-150)}{2} = 200\), the vertical shift is \(\frac{250 + (-150)}{2} = 50\), and \(b = 2\pi f = 2\pi(60) = 120\pi\), giving \(V = 200 \cos(120\pi t) + 50\).

qs.q: The average monthly temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) in a city reaches a maximum of \(26^\circ\text{C}\) in July (\(t = 0\)) and drops to a minimum of \(-6^\circ\text{C}\) six months later. If the temperature follows an annual 12-month sinusoidal cycle, find an equation in terms of cosine that models \(T\) as a function of time \(t\) (in months).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(\frac{26 - (-6)}{2} = 16\), the vertical shift is \(\frac{26 + (-6)}{2} = 10\), and \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Since the maximum occurs at \(t = 0\), the equation is \(T = 16 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6} t\right) + 10\).

qs.q: A Ferris wheel has a radius of 18 meters and completes one full revolution every 48 seconds. A passenger boards a seat at the lowest point, which is 4 meters above the ground. If \(t\) is measured in seconds from boarding, find an equation in terms of cosine that gives the passenger's height \(h\) (in meters) after \(t\) seconds.
qs.s: The amplitude is 18 and the vertical displacement of the center is \(18 + 4 = 22\). With \(P = 48\), \(b = \frac{2\pi}{48} = \frac{\pi}{24}\), and since boarding occurs at the minimum height, the cosine is inverted: \(h = -18 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{24} t\right) + 22\).

qs.q: A mass suspended from a spring is pulled down to a minimum height of 12 cm above the floor and released at \(t = 0\). The mass moves upward to reach a maximum height of 36 cm, completing 2 full oscillations per second. Write an equation in terms of cosine that models the height \(h\) (in cm) of the mass above the floor after \(t\) seconds.
qs.s: The amplitude is \(\frac{36 - 12}{2} = 12\) and the vertical shift is \(\frac{36 + 12}{2} = 24\). Since the frequency is 2 oscillations per second, the period is \(P = \frac{1}{2}\) second so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{1/2} = 4\pi\); starting at the minimum at \(t = 0\) requires an inverted cosine: \(h = -12 \cos(4\pi t) + 24\).

qs.q: At a coastal harbor, the water depth \(d\) (in meters) reaches a high tide of 16 meters at \(t = 0\) hours and a low tide of 4 meters 6 hours later. Assuming the water depth varies periodically according to a cosine model, write an equation that describes \(d\) as a function of time \(t\) (in hours).
qs.s: The amplitude is \(\frac{16 - 4}{2} = 6\), and the vertical shift is \(\frac{16 + 4}{2} = 10\). The period is \(2 \times 6 = 12\) hours, so \(b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}\), which gives \(d = 6 \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6} t\right) + 10\).

qs.q: A passenger on a Ferris wheel reaches a maximum height of 42 m above the ground and a minimum height of 6 m above the ground. The wheel turns at a constant rate of 3 revolutions per minute. What is the period in seconds for this periodic function?
qs.s: The period is the time for one complete revolution. With a rate of 3 revolutions per minute, the period is 60 / 3 = 20 seconds.

qs.q: The tip of a wind turbine blade reaches a maximum height of 90 m above the ground and a minimum height of 30 m above the ground. The turbine rotates at a constant rate of 12 revolutions per minute. What is the period in seconds for this periodic function?
qs.s: The period is the time it takes to complete one revolution. Since the turbine makes 12 revolutions in 60 seconds, the period is 60 / 12 = 5 seconds.

qs.q: A buoy bobs up and down with the ocean waves such that its beacon reaches a maximum height of 14 ft above the seabed and a minimum height of 6 ft above the seabed. The buoy completes 10 full bobbing cycles per minute. What is the period in seconds for this periodic function?
qs.s: The period is the duration of one complete cycle. With 10 cycles per minute, the period is 60 / 10 = 6 seconds.

qs.q: A paddle wheel on a boat has a maximum height of 16 ft above the water line and a minimum depth of 4 ft below the water line (a height of -4 ft). The wheel rotates at a constant rate of 15 cycles per minute. What is the period in seconds for this periodic function?
qs.s: The period is the time required for one complete cycle. At a rate of 15 cycles per minute, the period is 60 / 15 = 4 seconds.

qs.q: The needle of a sewing machine moves up and down between a maximum height of 50 mm and a minimum height of 10 mm above the needle plate. The machine operates at a constant rate of 30 cycles per minute. What is the period in seconds for this periodic function?
qs.s: The period is the time needed for one full cycle. At 30 cycles per minute, the period is 60 / 30 = 2 seconds.
