qs.s: The denominator is 0 when sin x = 0 (x = 0, pi) or cos x = 0 (x = pi/2, 3pi/2). All four values are restricted.

qs.q: For \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\), which set lists all the restrictions (non-permissible values) of \(\dfrac{\tan x}{1 + \cos x}\)?
qs.s: tan x is undefined at pi/2 and 3pi/2. The denominator is 0 when cos x = -1 (x = pi). So x = pi/2, pi, 3pi/2.

qs.q: For \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\), which set lists all the restrictions (non-permissible values) of \(\dfrac{\csc x \sec x}{2\sin x - \sqrt{3}}\)?
qs.s: csc x needs sin x not 0 (0, pi), sec x needs cos x not 0 (pi/2, 3pi/2), and the denominator is 0 when sin x = sqrt(3)/2 (pi/3, 2pi/3).

qs.q: For \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\), which set lists all the restrictions (non-permissible values) of \(\dfrac{\sec x}{2\sin^2 x - 1}\)?
qs.s: sec x is undefined when cos x = 0 (pi/2, 3pi/2). The denominator is 0 when sin^2 x = 1/2, i.e. sin x = +-sqrt(2)/2 (pi/4, 3pi/4, 5pi/4, 7pi/4).

qs.q: For \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\), which set lists all the restrictions (non-permissible values) of \(\dfrac{\csc x}{\tan x - 1}\)?
qs.s: csc x is undefined when sin x = 0 (0, pi); tan x is undefined at pi/2 and 3pi/2; and the denominator is 0 when tan x = 1 (pi/4, 5pi/4).

qs.q: For \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\), which set lists all the restrictions (non-permissible values) of \(\dfrac{\cot x}{2\cos x + \sqrt{2}}\)?
qs.s: cot x = cos x / sin x is undefined when sin x = 0 (0, pi). The denominator is 0 when cos x = -sqrt(2)/2 (3pi/4, 5pi/4).

qs.q: For \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\), which set lists all the restrictions (non-permissible values) of \(\dfrac{\tan x}{\sin x - \cos x}\)?
qs.s: tan x is undefined at pi/2 and 3pi/2. The denominator is 0 when sin x = cos x, i.e. tan x = 1 (pi/4, 5pi/4).

qs.q: Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\cos^2 x - 3\cos x + 1}\)
Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{\sin^2 x - \sin x}\)
Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{4\cos^2 x - 3}\)
Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\cos^2 x - 1}\)
Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\sin^2 x - \sin x - 1}\)
Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{\tan^2 x - 3}\)
qs.s: \(\tan^2x=3\) gives \(x=\pi/3,\ 2\pi/3,\ 4\pi/3,\ 5\pi/3\); also \(\tan x\) is undefined at \(x=\pi/2,\ 3\pi/2\), so these are restricted too.

qs.q: Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\sin x\cos x - \sin x}\)
qs.s: \(2\sin x\cos x-\sin x=\sin x(2\cos x-1)=0\), so \(\sin x=0\) (\(x=0,\ \pi\)) or \(\cos x=\frac12\) (\(x=\pi/3,\ 5\pi/3\)).

qs.q: Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\cos^2 x - 5\cos x + 2}\)
qs.s: \(2\cos^2x-5\cos x+2=(2\cos x-1)(\cos x-2)=0\). \(\cos x=2\) is impossible, so only \(\cos x=\frac12\) gives \(x=\pi/3,\ 5\pi/3\).

qs.q: Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\cos^2 x + 3\cos x + 1}\)
Determine all restrictions for \(0 \le x < 2\pi\): \(\dfrac{1}{2\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1}\)
How many restrictions (non-permissible values) does \(\sec x+\cot x\) have for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: \(\sec x\) is undefined when \(\cos x=0\) (\(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}\)) and \(\cot x\) is undefined when \(\sin x=0\) (\(0,\pi\)): 4 values.

qs.q: How many restrictions (non-permissible values) does \(\tan x\) have for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: \(\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) is undefined when \(\cos x=0\), i.e. at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(x=\frac{3\pi}{2}\): 2 values.

qs.q: Which of the following is a restriction (non-permissible value) of \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: The expression is undefined when \(\sin x=0\), which on \(0\le x<2\pi\) happens at \(x=0\) and \(x=\pi\). The other values give \(\sin x\ne0\).

qs.q: How many restrictions (non-permissible values) does \(\frac{1}{\cos x-1}\) have for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: The denominator is 0 when \(\cos x=1\), which on \(0\le x<2\pi\) happens only at \(x=0\): 1 value.

qs.q: Which of the following is a restriction (non-permissible value) of \(\frac{1}{2\sin x-1}\) for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: The denominator is 0 when \(\sin x=\frac12\), i.e. \(x=\frac{\pi}{6}\) or \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\). For the other values \(\sin x\ne\frac12\).

qs.q: Which of the following is a restriction (non-permissible value) of \(\frac{1}{\sin x-\cos x}\) for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: The denominator is 0 when \(\sin x=\cos x\), i.e. \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\) or \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\). At \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) and \(\frac{7\pi}{4}\) the two have opposite signs, and at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) they are 1 and 0.

qs.q: How many restrictions (non-permissible values) does \(\frac{\cot x}{\cos x-1}\) have for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: \(\cot x\) is undefined at \(x=0\) and \(\pi\); the denominator is 0 only when \(\cos x=1\), i.e. \(x=0\), which is already counted. Total: 2 values.

qs.q: How many restrictions (non-permissible values) does \(\frac{\cot x}{\sin x-1}\) have for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: \(\cot x\) is undefined at \(x=0\) and \(\pi\) (\(\sin x=0\)); the denominator is 0 when \(\sin x=1\), i.e. \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Total: 3 values.

qs.q: Which of the following is a restriction (non-permissible value) of \(\frac{1}{2\cos x+\sqrt{3}}\) for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: The denominator is 0 when \(\cos x=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\), i.e. \(x=\frac{5\pi}{6}\) or \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\). The other values give \(\cos x=\pm\frac12\).

qs.q: How many restrictions (non-permissible values) does \(\frac{\tan x+\cot x}{2\sin x-1}\) have for \(0 \leq x < 2\pi\)?
qs.s: \(\tan x\): \(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}\); \(\cot x\): \(0,\pi\); denominator (\(\sin x=\frac12\)): \(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6}\). All six values are different, so 6.

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x - \cos x)(1 + \cot^2 x)\)
qs.s: Rewrite the first factor as \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\) and use the identity \(1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x = \frac{1}{\sin^2 x}\). Multiplying gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x \csc x - \cot x)(\tan x + \cot x)\)
qs.s: Simplify the first factor to \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \tan x\), and the second factor to \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\cos x \sin x}\). Their product is \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x \sin x} = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\csc x - \cot x)(\sec x + 1)\)
qs.s: Express each factor in terms of sine and cosine: \(\left(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x}\right)\left(\frac{1 + \cos x}{\cos x}\right) = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x}\). Applying \(1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x - \tan x)(\csc x + 1)\)
qs.s: Rewrite using common denominators: \(\left(\frac{1 - \sin x}{\cos x}\right)\left(\frac{1 + \sin x}{\sin x}\right) = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\cos x \sin x}\). By the Pythagorean identity, \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \cot x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x \csc x - \tan x)(\sec x - \cos x)\)
qs.s: Express the terms using sine and cosine: \(\left(\frac{1}{\cos x \sin x} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x\right) = \left(\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\cos x \sin x}\right)\left(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x}\right) = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} \cdot \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Simplifying the product yields \(\sin x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x + \tan x - 1)(\sec x - \tan x + 1)\)
qs.s: Regroup the terms as \([\sec x + (\tan x - 1)][\sec x - (\tan x - 1)] = \sec^2 x - (\tan x - 1)^2\). Expanding and using \(\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\) gives \((\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x) + 2\tan x - 1 = 1 + 2\tan x - 1 = 2\tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sin x + \cos x)(\tan x + \cot x) - \sec x\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x + \cot x = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Multiplying gives \(\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x \cos x} = \sec x + \csc x\). Subtracting \(\sec x\) leaves \(\csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\left(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x} - \frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x}\right)\csc x\)
qs.s: Combine the fractions using a common denominator: \(\frac{\cos x(1 + \sin x) - \cos x(1 - \sin x)}{1 - \sin^2 x} = \frac{2\cos x \sin x}{\cos^2 x} = 2\tan x\). Multiplying by \(\csc x\) gives \(2\tan x \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x} = \frac{2}{\cos x} = 2\sec x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x}}{\frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x} + \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x}}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \(\frac{(1 + \sin x)^2 + \cos^2 x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{2(1 + \sin x)}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = 2\sec x\), and similarly the denominator simplifies to \(\frac{2(1 + \cos x)}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = 2\csc x\). The quotient is \(\frac{2\sec x}{2\csc x} = \frac{1/\cos x}{1/\sin x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sin x + \cos x - 1)(\sin x + \cos x + 1)(\sec x \csc x)\)
qs.s: Group the first two factors as a difference of squares: \([(\sin x + \cos x) - 1][(\sin x + \cos x) + 1] = (\sin x + \cos x)^2 - 1 = (1 + 2\sin x \cos x) - 1 = 2\sin x \cos x\). Multiplying by \(\sec x \csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\) yields \(2\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cot x - 1}{\frac{\cot x}{\cot x + 1}} + \tan x\)
qs.s: Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{(\cot x - 1)(\cot x + 1)}{\cot x} + \tan x = \frac{\cot^2 x - 1}{\cot x} + \frac{1}{\cot x} = \frac{\cot^2 x}{\cot x} = \cot x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\csc x - 1}{\frac{\csc x}{\csc x + 1}} + \sin x\)
qs.s: Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{(\csc x - 1)(\csc x + 1)}{\csc x} + \sin x = \frac{\csc^2 x - 1}{\csc x} + \frac{1}{\csc x} = \frac{\csc^2 x}{\csc x} = \csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec x - 1}{\frac{\sec x}{\sec x + 1}} + \cos x\)
qs.s: Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{(\sec x - 1)(\sec x + 1)}{\sec x} + \cos x = \frac{\sec^2 x - 1}{\sec x} + \frac{1}{\sec x} = \frac{\sec^2 x}{\sec x} = \sec x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan x + 1}{\frac{\tan x}{\tan x - 1}} - \tan x\)
qs.s: Multiplying the numerator by the reciprocal of the denominator gives \(\frac{(\tan x + 1)(\tan x - 1)}{\tan x} - \tan x = \frac{\tan^2 x - 1 - \tan^2 x}{\tan x} = -\frac{1}{\tan x} = -\cot x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan x - 1}{\frac{\tan x}{\tan x + 1}} + \cot x\)
qs.s: Multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\frac{(\tan x - 1)(\tan x + 1)}{\tan x} + \cot x = \frac{\tan^2 x - 1}{\tan x} + \frac{1}{\tan x} = \frac{\tan^2 x}{\tan x} = \tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan^2 x - 1}{\frac{\tan x - 1}{\tan x + 1}} - \sec^2 x\)
qs.s: Factoring \(\tan^2 x - 1 = (\tan x - 1)(\tan x + 1)\) and multiplying by the reciprocal yields \((\tan x + 1)^2 = \tan^2 x + 2\tan x + 1 = \sec^2 x + 2\tan x\). Subtracting \(\sec^2 x\) leaves \(2\tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\frac{1}{\sec x - 1} + \frac{1}{\sec x + 1}}{\frac{\cot x}{\sin x}}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \(\frac{2\sec x}{\sec^2 x - 1} = \frac{2\sec x}{\tan^2 x} = \frac{2\cos x}{\sin^2 x}\). Dividing by the denominator \(\frac{\cot x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x}\) results in \(2\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec x + 1}{\tan x} + \frac{\tan x}{\sec x + 1} - \csc x\)
qs.s: Finding a common denominator for the first two terms gives \(\frac{(\sec x + 1)^2 + \tan^2 x}{\tan x(\sec x + 1)} = \frac{2\sec x(\sec x + 1)}{\tan x(\sec x + 1)} = \frac{2\sec x}{\tan x} = 2\csc x\). Subtracting \(\csc x\) gives \(\csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\frac{1}{\cos x - \sin x} - \frac{1}{\cos x + \sin x}}{\frac{1}{\cos x - \sin x} + \frac{1}{\cos x + \sin x}}\)
qs.s: Combining terms over the common denominator \(\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x\) in both numerator and denominator produces \(\frac{2\sin x}{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}\) over \(\frac{2\cos x}{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{2\sin x}{2\cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x}}{\frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} + \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}}\)
qs.s: Combining the fractions in the numerator yields \(\frac{\sin^2 x + (1+\cos x)^2}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} = \frac{2(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} = 2\csc x\), while the denominator similarly simplifies to \(2\sec x\), so the ratio is \(\frac{2\csc x}{2\sec x} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cot x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \cot^2 x}{\cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: Replacing \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x\) with \(1\), the numerator becomes \(1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x\). Then, \(\frac{\csc^2 x}{\cot^2 x} = \frac{1/\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x/\sin^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \tan^2 x}{\tan^2 x}\)
qs.s: Replacing \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x\) with \(1\), the numerator becomes \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\). Dividing gives \(\frac{\sec^2 x}{\tan^2 x} = \frac{1/\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x/\cos^2 x} = \frac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \csc^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: Using \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\), the expression becomes \(\frac{1}{1 + \cot^2 x} = \frac{1}{\csc^2 x} = \sin^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \tan^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: Replacing \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x\) with \(1\) in both the numerator and denominator gives \(\frac{1 + \tan^2 x}{1 + \cot^2 x} = \frac{\sec^2 x}{\csc^2 x}\). Converting to sine and cosine yields \(\frac{1/\cos^2 x}{1/\sin^2 x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \tan^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cot^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: Using \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the denominator simplifies to \(1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x\). Then, \(\frac{\cot^2 x}{\csc^2 x} = \frac{\cos^2 x / \sin^2 x}{1 / \sin^2 x} = \cos^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{1 - \cos x} + \frac{1}{1 + \cos x} - 2\cot^2 x\)
qs.s: Combining the first two fractions gives \(\frac{2}{1 - \cos^2 x} = \frac{2}{\sin^2 x} = 2\csc^2 x\). Then, \(2\csc^2 x - 2\cot^2 x = 2(\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x) = 2(1) = 2\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x}\)
qs.s: Finding a common denominator yields \(\frac{\sin^2 x + (1 + \cos x)^2}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{2 + 2\cos x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)}\). Factoring the numerator gives \(\frac{2(1 + \cos x)}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x} - \tan x\)
qs.s: Writing \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) and finding a common denominator gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x - \sin x(1 - \sin x)}{\cos x(1 - \sin x)} = \frac{1 - \sin x}{\cos x(1 - \sin x)}\). Cancelling \((1 - \sin x)\) leaves \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \tan^2 x} + \frac{\cot^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + \cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: Using Pythagorean identities, the two terms simplify to \(\frac{\tan^2 x}{\sec^2 x} = \sin^2 x\) and \(\frac{\cot^2 x}{\csc^2 x} = \cos^2 x\), respectively. Their sum is \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the following trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec x + \csc x}{1 + \tan x}\)
qs.s: Rewriting in terms of sine and cosine gives \(\frac{\frac{1}{\cos x} + \frac{1}{\sin x}}{1 + \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}} = \frac{\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x \cos x}}{\frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x}}\). Cancelling the common factor \((\sin x + \cos x)\) and \(\cos x\) simplifies the expression to \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin x \cdot \cot x + \cos x}{2\cot x}\)
qs.s: Since \(\sin x \cdot \cot x = \sin x \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cos x\), the numerator simplifies to \(\cos x + \cos x = 2\cos x\). Dividing by the denominator gives \(\frac{2\cos x}{2\cot x} = \frac{\cos x}{\cos x / \sin x} = \sin x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cot x \cdot \sec x + \csc x}{2\sec x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\cot x \cdot \sec x\) as \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x} = \csc x\), making the numerator \(2\csc x\). Dividing by \(2\sec x\) yields \(\frac{\csc x}{\sec x} = \frac{1/\sin x}{1/\cos x} = \cot x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\cot x - \cos x \cdot \csc x}{2\cos x}\)
qs.s: Since \(\cos x \cdot \csc x = \cos x \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x} = \cot x\), the numerator becomes \(3\cot x - \cot x = 2\cot x\). Dividing by \(2\cos x\) gives \(\frac{\cot x}{\cos x} = \frac{\cos x / \sin x}{\cos x} = \csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3\tan x - \sin x \cdot \sec x}{2\sin x}\)
qs.s: Since \(\sin x \cdot \sec x = \sin x \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x} = \tan x\), the numerator becomes \(3\tan x - \tan x = 2\tan x\). Dividing by \(2\sin x\) gives \(\frac{\tan x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin x / \cos x}{\sin x} = \sec x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan x \cdot \csc x + \sec x}{2\csc x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x \cdot \csc x\) as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x} = \sec x\), making the numerator \(2\sec x\). Dividing by \(2\csc x\) yields \(\frac{\sec x}{\csc x} = \frac{1/\cos x}{1/\sin x} = \tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin x \cdot \tan x + \cos x}{\csc x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x\) as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) to get the numerator \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\). Then \(\frac{\sec x}{\csc x} = \frac{1/\cos x}{1/\sin x} = \tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan x + \cot x}{\csc x}\)
qs.s: Express the numerator in sine and cosine: \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing by \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\) results in \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cos x \cdot \cot x + \sin x}{\sec x}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) into the numerator to get \(\frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\). Dividing by \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\) yields \(\frac{1/\sin x}{1/\cos x} = \cot x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cos^2 x \cdot \tan x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x + \sin x \cdot \cot x}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) into the numerator to get \(\cos x(\sin x + \cos x)\), and substitute \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) into the denominator to get \(\sin x + \cos x\). Canceling the common binomial factor \((\sin x + \cos x)\) leaves \(\cos x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec x \cdot \csc x - \cot x}{\sec x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator in terms of sine and cosine: \(\frac{1}{\cos x \sin x} - \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \tan x\). Dividing by \(\sec x\) yields \(\frac{\tan x}{\sec x} = \sin x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin^2 x} - \csc^2 x\)
qs.s: Since \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), the fraction simplifies to \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x} = \cot^2 x\). Then, \(\cot^2 x - \csc^2 x = -1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan^2 x + 1}{\sec^2 x} - \sin^2 x\)
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identity \(\tan^2 x + 1 = \sec^2 x\), the expression becomes \(\frac{\sec^2 x}{\sec^2 x} - \sin^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin^2 x - 1}{\cos^2 x} - \tan^2 x\)
qs.s: Since \(\sin^2 x - 1 = -\cos^2 x\), the fraction simplifies to \(\frac{-\cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = -1\). Then, \(-1 - \tan^2 x = -(1 + \tan^2 x) = -\sec^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1 + \cot^2 x}{\cot^2 x} - \sec^2 x\)
qs.s: Separating the fraction gives \(\frac{1}{\cot^2 x} + 1 = \tan^2 x + 1 = \sec^2 x\). Then, \(\sec^2 x - \sec^2 x = 0\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec^2 x - 1}{\sec^2 x} + \cos^2 x\)
qs.s: Using \(\sec^2 x - 1 = \tan^2 x\), the fraction becomes \(\frac{\tan^2 x}{\sec^2 x} = \sin^2 x\). Then, \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \frac{\sin x}{1 - \cos x} - 2\csc x\)
qs.s: Finding a common denominator yields \(\frac{\sin x(1 - \cos x) + \sin x(1 + \cos x)}{1 - \cos^2 x} = \frac{2\sin x}{\sin^2 x} = \frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\). Subtracting \(2\csc x\) gives \(2\csc x - 2\csc x = 0\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \left(\frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \cot x\right)\sin x - \cos^2 x\)
qs.s: Rewriting \(\cot x\) as \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) and adding gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos x(1 + \cos x)}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \csc x\). Then, \(\csc x \cdot \sin x - \cos^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec x \csc x - \tan x}{\cot x} + \tan^2 x\)
qs.s: In terms of sine and cosine, the numerator is \(\frac{1}{\cos x \sin x} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \cot x\). Thus, \(\frac{\cot x}{\cot x} + \tan^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{1 - \sin x} + \frac{1}{1 + \sin x} - 2\tan^2 x\)
qs.s: Combining the fractions over the common denominator gives \(\frac{(1 + \sin x) + (1 - \sin x)}{1 - \sin^2 x} = \frac{2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x\). Then, \(2\sec^2 x - 2\tan^2 x = 2(\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x) = 2(1) = 2\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{1 - \cos x} - \frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} - \cot^2 x\)
qs.s: Multiplying \(\frac{1}{1 - \cos x}\) by the conjugate \(\frac{1 + \cos x}{1 + \cos x}\) gives \(\frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin^2 x}\). Subtracting \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x}\) leaves \(\frac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \csc^2 x\), and \(\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x = 1\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan x + \cot x}{\sec^2 x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing by \(\sec^2 x = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x}\) gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cot x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\sec^2 x - 1}\)
qs.s: Apply the Pythagorean identities \(1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\) and \(\sec^2 x - 1 = \tan^2 x\). Dividing yields \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\sin^2 x / \cos^2 x} = \sin^2 x \cdot \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x} = \cos^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x \sec x}{\tan x + \cot x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\sin x \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) and the denominator as \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing yields \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot (\sin x \cos x) = \sin^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cot x}{\csc x - \sin x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(\csc x - \sin x = \frac{1}{\sin x} - \sin x = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Dividing \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) by \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\) gives \(\frac{\cos x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1 + \tan^2 x}{1 + \cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identities, substitute \(1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x\) and \(1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x\). Rewriting in terms of sine and cosine yields \(\frac{1/\cos^2 x}{1/\sin^2 x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \tan^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\cot^2 x - \cos^2 x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{\sin^2 x(1 - \cos^2 x)}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin^4 x}{\cos^2 x}\) and the denominator as \(\frac{\cos^2 x(1 - \sin^2 x)}{\sin^2 x} = \frac{\cos^4 x}{\sin^2 x}\). Dividing these fractions gives \(\frac{\sin^4 x}{\cos^2 x} \cdot \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^4 x} = \frac{\sin^6 x}{\cos^6 x} = \tan^6 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x}{1 - \cos x} - \cot x\)
qs.s: Write \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) and combine over \(\sin x(1 - \cos x)\) to get \(\frac{\sin^2 x - \cos x(1 - \cos x)}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)} = \frac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)}\). Cancelling \((1 - \cos x)\) gives \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x - \cos x)^2 + (\csc x - \sin x)^2 - (\tan x - \cot x)^2\)
qs.s: Expand each square and use the reciprocal products \(\sec x\cos x = 1\), \(\csc x\sin x = 1\), and \(\tan x\cot x = 1\). Regrouping the terms gives \((\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x) + (\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x) + (\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) - 2 - 2 - (-2) = 1 + 1 + 1 - 2 = 1\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x} - \frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x}\)
qs.s: Find a common denominator of \((1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x) = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\). The numerator simplifies to \(\cos x(1 + \sin x) - \cos x(1 - \sin x) = 2\cos x \sin x\), yielding \(\frac{2\cos x \sin x}{\cos^2 x} = 2\tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x}\)
qs.s: Combine over the common denominator \(\sin x(1 + \cos x)\) to obtain \(\frac{\sin^2 x + (1 + 2\cos x + \cos^2 x)}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{2 + 2\cos x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)}\). Factoring out \(2\) and cancelling \((1 + \cos x)\) leaves \(\frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x(\tan x + \cot x)}{\sec x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x + \cot x\) as \(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\), which simplifies the numerator to \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\). Dividing by \(\sec x\) yields \(\frac{1/\sin x}{1/\cos x} = \cot x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cot x(\tan x - \sin x)}{\csc x - \cot x}\)
qs.s: Expand the numerator to get \(1 - \cos x\) and rewrite the denominator as \(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x}\). Dividing the two expressions simplifies to \(\sin x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x(\tan x + \cot x)}{\csc x}\)
qs.s: Write \(\tan x + \cot x\) as \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\), making the numerator \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\). Dividing by \(\csc x\) gives \(\frac{1/\cos x}{1/\sin x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan x(\cos x + \cot x)}{\sec x + \tan x}\)
qs.s: Expand the numerator to get \(\sin x + 1\) and rewrite the denominator as \(\frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}\). Dividing the numerator by the denominator gives \(\cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x + \tan x}{\tan x(\cos x + \cot x)}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}\) and expand the denominator to \(\sin x + 1\). Dividing the numerator by the denominator gives \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{(\sin x + \cos x)^2 - 1}{2\cos^2 x}\)
qs.s: Expand the numerator to get \(\sin^2 x + 2\sin x \cos x + \cos^2 x - 1 = 2\sin x \cos x\). Dividing by \(2\cos^2 x\) leaves \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x} - \tan x\)
qs.s: Write \(\tan x\) as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) and combine using the common denominator \(\cos x(1 - \sin x)\) to get \(\frac{\cos^2 x - \sin x(1 - \sin x)}{\cos x(1 - \sin x)} = \frac{1 - \sin x}{\cos x(1 - \sin x)} = \sec x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x \tan x}{\sec x - 1} - 1\)
qs.s: Express the fraction in terms of sine and cosine to obtain \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{1 - \cos x} = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{1 - \cos x} = 1 + \cos x\). Subtracting 1 yields \(\cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan x + \cot x}{\sec x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x + \cot x\) as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing by \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\) gives \(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos x} \cdot \cos x = \frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\sin x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Dividing by \(\sin x\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\csc x - \sin x}{\cos x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{1}{\sin x} - \sin x = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Dividing by \(\cos x\) gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cot x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x + \cos x \cot x}{\cot x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\sin x + \cos x \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{1}{\sin x}\). Dividing by \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) yields \(\frac{1}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\csc x - \sin x}{\cot x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\csc x\) as \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) to get \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\) in the numerator. Dividing by \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x} + \frac{\sin x}{1 - \cos x}\)
qs.s: Combine over a common denominator: \(\frac{(1 - \cos x)^2 + \sin^2 x}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)} = \frac{1 - 2\cos x + \cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)}\). Using \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the numerator becomes \(2(1 - \cos x)\), giving \(\frac{2(1 - \cos x)}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)} = \frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1}{1 - \sin x} + \frac{1}{1 + \sin x}\)
qs.s: Find a common denominator: \(\frac{(1 + \sin x) + (1 - \sin x)}{(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{2}{1 - \sin^2 x}\). Using the Pythagorean identity \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), this simplifies to \(\frac{2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x - \sin^3 x}{\cos x - \cos^3 x}\)
qs.s: Factor both the numerator and denominator: \(\frac{\sin x(1 - \sin^2 x)}{\cos x(1 - \cos^2 x)} = \frac{\sin x \cos^2 x}{\cos x \sin^2 x}\). Canceling common factors gives \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cot x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x + \csc x}{1 + \tan x}\)
qs.s: Express all terms in sine and cosine: \(\frac{\frac{1}{\cos x} + \frac{1}{\sin x}}{1 + \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}} = \frac{\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x \cos x}}{\frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x}}\). Multiply by the reciprocal to obtain \(\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x \cos x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\cos x + \sin x} = \frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\csc x(\csc x + \cot x) - \cot^2 x(1 + \sec x)}{\tan x(\cos x + \cot x) - 1}\]
qs.s: Expanding the numerator yields \((\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x) + (\csc x \cot x - \cot^2 x \sec x) = 1 + 0 = 1\), and expanding the denominator gives \(\sin x + 1 - 1 = \sin x\). The expression simplifies to \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\csc^2 x(1 + \sec x) - \cot x(\csc x + \cot x)}{\sec x(1 + \cos x)}\]
qs.s: Expanding the numerator yields \((\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x) + \csc x(\csc x \sec x - \cot x) = 1 + \sec x\), while the denominator expands to \(\sec x + 1\). The ratio simplifies to \(\frac{1 + \sec x}{\sec x + 1} = 1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\sec x(\sec x - \tan x) + \tan^2 x(\csc x - 1)}{\cot x(\sin x + \tan x) - 1}\]
qs.s: Expanding the numerator yields \((\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x) + (\tan^2 x \csc x - \sec x \tan x) = 1 + 0 = 1\), and expanding the denominator gives \(\cos x + 1 - 1 = \cos x\). The quotient is \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\sec x(\sin x + \cot x) - \csc x}{\csc x(\cos x + \tan x) - \sec x}\]
qs.s: Distributing terms in the numerator gives \(\tan x + \csc x - \csc x = \tan x\), and distributing terms in the denominator gives \(\cot x + \sec x - \sec x = \cot x\). The ratio simplifies to \(\frac{\tan x}{\cot x} = \tan^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\sin x(1 + \cot^2 x) - \cot x \cos x}{\cos x(1 + \tan^2 x) - \tan x \sin x}\]
qs.s: Using \(1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x\), the numerator simplifies to \(\sin x \csc^2 x - \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\sin x} = \sin x\), and similarly the denominator simplifies to \(\cos x\). The quotient is \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\sec^4 x(1 - \sin^4 x) - 2\tan^2 x}{(\sec x - \tan x)^2 (1 + \sin x)^2}\]
qs.s: Factor \(1 - \sin^4 x = \cos^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x)\), simplifying the numerator to \(\sec^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x) - 2\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\). The denominator simplifies to \([(\sec x - \tan x)(1 + \sin x)]^2 = [\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\cos x}]^2 = \cos^2 x\), giving \(\frac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x - 1}{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x - 1}\]
qs.s: Using algebraic expansions with \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\), the denominator is \(\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x - 1 = -2\sin^2 x \cos^2 x\) and the numerator is \(\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x - 1 = -3\sin^2 x \cos^2 x\). The ratio simplifies to \(\frac{-3\sin^2 x \cos^2 x}{-2\sin^2 x \cos^2 x} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{1 + \sin x - \cos x}{1 + \sin x + \cos x} + \frac{1 + \sin x + \cos x}{1 + \sin x - \cos x}\]
qs.s: Grouping \((1+\sin x)\) gives a common denominator of \((1+\sin x)^2 - \cos^2 x = 2\sin x(1+\sin x)\) and combines the numerators into \(2[(1+\sin x)^2 + \cos^2 x] = 4(1+\sin x)\). The fraction reduces to \(\frac{4(1+\sin x)}{2\sin x(1+\sin x)} = \frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\[\frac{\tan x}{1 - \cot x} + \frac{\cot x}{1 - \tan x} - \sec x \csc x\]
qs.s: Rewriting in sine and cosine combines the fractions into \(\frac{\sin^3 x - \cos^3 x}{\sin x \cos x(\sin x - \cos x)} = \frac{1 + \sin x \cos x}{\sin x \cos x} = 1 + \sec x \csc x\). Subtracting \(\sec x \csc x\) leaves \(1\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\tan x}\)
qs.s: Write \(\sec x - \cos x\) over a common denominator as \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\), then divide by \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) to get \(\sin x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan^2 x + 1}{\tan x \sec x}\)
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identity \(\tan^2 x + 1 = \sec^2 x\), the expression reduces to \(\frac{\sec x}{\tan x} = \frac{1/\cos x}{\sin x/\cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \tan x} + \frac{\sin x}{1 - \cot x}\)
qs.s: Convert \(\tan x\) and \(\cot x\) to sines and cosines to write the expression as \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x} - \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x}\), then factor the difference of squares in the numerator to simplify to \(\sin x + \cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x}{\sec x - 1} + \frac{\sec x}{\sec x + 1}\)
qs.s: Combine the fractions to get \(\frac{2\sec^2 x}{\sec^2 x - 1} = \frac{2\sec^2 x}{\tan^2 x}\), then express in terms of sine and cosine: \(\frac{2/\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x/\cos^2 x} = \frac{2}{\sin^2 x} = 2\csc^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x - \cos x)(\csc x - \sin x)(\tan x + \cot x)\)
qs.s: Using common denominators and Pythagorean identities, rewrite the three factors as \(\left(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\right)\left(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\right)\), which multiplies out to \(1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\tan x + \sec x}{1 + \sin x}\)
qs.s: Express the numerator as \(\frac{\sin x + 1}{\cos x}\), then cancel \((1 + \sin x)\) with the denominator to arrive at \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin x + \tan x}{1 + \sec x}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator as \(\sin x(1 + \sec x)\) and cancel \((1 + \sec x)\) with the denominator to obtain \(\sin x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\cot x + \csc x}{1 + \cos x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator in terms of sine and cosine as \(\frac{\cos x + 1}{\sin x}\), then cancel \((1 + \cos x)\) to get \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1 + \tan x}{1 + \cot x}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(\cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x}\) into the denominator to get \(\frac{1 + \tan x}{(\tan x + 1)/\tan x}\), which simplifies directly to \(\tan x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1 + \cot x}{\csc x + \sec x}\)
qs.s: Convert all terms to sine and cosine to rewrite the fraction as \(\frac{(\sin x + \cos x)/\sin x}{(\sin x + \cos x)/(\sin x \cos x)}\), which simplifies to \(\cos x\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin x + \cos x} + \sin x \cos x\)
qs.s: Factor the sum of cubes to get \(\frac{(\sin x + \cos x)(\sin^2 x - \sin x\cos x + \cos^2 x)}{\sin x + \cos x} = 1 - \sin x\cos x\), and adding \(\sin x\cos x\) yields \(1\).

qs.q:
Simplify the trigonometric expression:
\(\displaystyle \frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\csc x - \sin x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\) and the denominator as \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\), then divide to obtain \(\frac{\sin^3 x}{\cos^3 x} = \tan^3 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x + \sin x \tan x}{\tan x}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator as \(\cos x + \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\). Then dividing by \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) gives \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan x}{\tan x + \cot x}\)
qs.s: Express the terms in sine and cosine: the denominator is \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) by \(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\) simplifies to \(\sin^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1}{\sec x - \tan x} - \frac{1}{\sec x + \tan x}\)
qs.s: Combine the fractions over the common denominator \((\sec x - \tan x)(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\) to get \(\frac{(\sec x + \tan x) - (\sec x - \tan x)}{1} = 2\tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x + 1}{\tan x} + \frac{\tan x}{\sec x + 1}\)
qs.s: Combine over a common denominator: \(\frac{(\sec x + 1)^2 + \tan^2 x}{\tan x(\sec x + 1)} = \frac{2\sec^2 x + 2\sec x}{\tan x(\sec x + 1)} = \frac{2\sec x}{\tan x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1}{1 - \cos x} + \frac{1}{1 + \cos x} - 2\cot^2 x\)
qs.s: Combining the first two terms gives \(\frac{2}{1 - \cos^2 x} = 2\csc^2 x\). Then \(2\csc^2 x - 2\cot^2 x = 2(\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x) = 2(1) = 2\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\sec^2 x + \tan^2 x\)?
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identity \(\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x\), substitute to obtain \((1 + \tan^2 x) + \tan^2 x = 2\tan^2 x + 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(2\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x\) into the expression to obtain \(2\sin^2 x + (1 - \sin^2 x) = \sin^2 x + 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x\)?
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x\), substitute to get \(\cos^2 x - (1 - \cos^2 x) = 2\cos^2 x - 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\csc^2 x + \cot^2 x\)?
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identity \(\cot^2 x = \csc^2 x - 1\), substitute to get \(\csc^2 x + (\csc^2 x - 1) = 2\csc^2 x - 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(1 - \sin^2 x + \cos^2 x\)?
qs.s: Using the Pythagorean identity \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), the expression simplifies to \(\cos^2 x + \cos^2 x = 2\cos^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\frac{\tan^2 x}{1 + \sec x}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan^2 x\) as \(\sec^2 x - 1 = (\sec x - 1)(\sec x + 1)\). Dividing out the common factor \((\sec x + 1)\) leaves \(\sec x - 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\frac{1}{1 - \sin x} + \frac{1}{1 + \sin x}\)?
qs.s: Combine using a common denominator to get \(\frac{(1 + \sin x) + (1 - \sin x)}{(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{2}{1 - \sin^2 x}\). Since \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), this simplifies to \(\frac{2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\csc x - \sin x}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite numerator and denominator with common denominators: \(\frac{1/\cos x - \cos x}{1/\sin x - \sin x} = \frac{(1 - \cos^2 x)/\cos x}{(1 - \sin^2 x)/\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x/\cos x}{\cos^2 x/\sin x} = \frac{\sin^3 x}{\cos^3 x} = \tan^3 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x\)?
qs.s: Factor as a difference of squares: \((\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = (\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(1)\). Then substitute \(\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x\) to get \(\sin^2 x - (1 - \sin^2 x) = 2\sin^2 x - 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is identically equal to \(\frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} + \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}\)?
qs.s: Combine over a common denominator: \(\frac{\cos^2 x + (1 + \sin x)^2}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{\cos^2 x + 1 + 2\sin x + \sin^2 x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}\). Using \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the numerator becomes \(2 + 2\sin x = 2(1 + \sin x)\), which reduces to \(\frac{2}{\cos x} = 2\sec x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\cos x + \sin x \tan x = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x\) as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) to get \(\cos x + \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Using the Pythagorean identity \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), this simplifies to \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\csc x - \cos x \cot x = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\csc x\) as \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) and \(\cot x\) as \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) to obtain \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Applying \(1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \sin x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \((\sec x - \cos x)\csc x = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Find a common denominator inside the parentheses: \(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Multiplying by \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \((\csc x - \sin x)\sec x = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Find a common denominator inside the parentheses: \(\frac{1}{\sin x} - \sin x = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Multiplying by \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\) gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cot x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\sec x - \sin x \tan x = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Express the terms using sine and cosine: \(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \sin x \left(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right) = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Since \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), simplifying yields \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \cos x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\sin x}{1 - \cos x} - \cot x = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) and find a common denominator: \(\frac{\sin^2 x - \cos x(1 - \cos x)}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)} = \frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x - \cos x}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)}\). Using \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\), this simplifies to \(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x(1 - \cos x)} = \frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} + \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x} = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Combine using the common denominator \(\cos x(1 + \sin x)\) to obtain \(\frac{\cos^2 x + (1 + \sin x)^2}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{\cos^2 x + 1 + 2\sin x + \sin^2 x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}\). Since \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\), the numerator simplifies to \(2 + 2\sin x = 2(1 + \sin x)\), leaving \(\frac{2}{\cos x} = 2\sec x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x} - \frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Combine the fractions over the common denominator \((1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x) = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\). The numerator becomes \(\cos x(1 + \sin x) - \cos x(1 - \sin x) = 2\sin x \cos x\), so \(\frac{2\sin x \cos x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{2\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\tan x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cot x(\sin x + \tan x)}{\csc x + \cot x} = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Distribute the numerator using \(\cot x \sin x = \cos x\) and \(\cot x \tan x = 1\) to get \(\cos x + 1\). The denominator is \(\frac{1}{\sin x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x}\), so dividing gives \((\cos x + 1) \cdot \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} = \sin x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x + \cot x}{1 + \csc x} = \underline{\quad}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\cot x\) as \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) and \(\csc x\) as \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) to get \(\frac{\frac{\cos x(\sin x + 1)}{\sin x}}{\frac{\sin x + 1}{\sin x}}\). Canceling the common factor \(\frac{\sin x + 1}{\sin x}\) yields \(\cos x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{1}{\cos^2 x} - 1 = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Combine over a common denominator to get \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x}\). Using the identity \(1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\), this becomes \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\sin x + \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Combine over the common denominator to obtain \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Applying the Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1\) gives \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{1}{\sin^2 x} - 1 = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Write with a common denominator as \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin^2 x}\). Substituting \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\) yields \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{1}{\sin x} - \sin x = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Write with a common denominator as \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x}\). Using the identity \(1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), this simplifies to \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\cos x + \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Write with a common denominator as \(\frac{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Since \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the expression simplifies to \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{1}{1 - \cos x} + \frac{1}{1 + \cos x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Combine over the common denominator \((1 - \cos x)(1 + \cos x)\) to get \(\frac{(1 + \cos x) + (1 - \cos x)}{1 - \cos^2 x} = \frac{2}{1 - \cos^2 x}\). Applying \(1 - \cos^2 x = \sin^2 x\) results in \(\frac{2}{\sin^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\left(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x\right)\left(\frac{1}{\sin x} - \sin x\right) = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the factors using common denominators as \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Multiplying and cancelling common factors simplifies the product to \(\sin x \cos x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{\sin x}{1 - \cos x} - \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Combine terms over \((1 - \cos x)(1 + \cos x)\) to get \(\frac{\sin x(1 + \cos x) - \sin x(1 - \cos x)}{1 - \cos^2 x} = \frac{2\sin x \cos x}{\sin^2 x}\). Cancelling \(\sin x\) gives \(\frac{2\cos x}{\sin x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} + \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Find a common denominator to write \(\frac{\cos^2 x + (1 + \sin x)^2}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{\cos^2 x + 1 + 2\sin x + \sin^2 x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}\). Since \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the numerator becomes \(2(1 + \sin x)\), which cancels with the denominator factor to leave \(\frac{2}{\cos x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity: \(\frac{\frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x}{\sin x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Simplify the numerator as \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Dividing this by \(\sin x\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x \sin x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{1}{\sec x - \cos x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Simplify the denominator as \(\sec x - \cos x = \frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Inverting gives \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} = \frac{1}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \csc x \cot x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\tan x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\sec x - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Dividing by \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \sin x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{1}{\csc x - \sin x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Simplify the denominator as \(\csc x - \sin x = \frac{1}{\sin x} - \sin x = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Inverting gives \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \sec x \tan x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{\csc x - \sin x}{\cot x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\csc x - \sin x = \frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Dividing by \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \cos x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{1}{\csc x \cot x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator in terms of sine and cosine to get \(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Using \(\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x\), separate the fraction into \(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \sec x - \cos x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\csc x - \sin x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\) and the denominator as \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Dividing the two yields \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin^3 x}{\cos^3 x} = \tan^3 x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{1}{1 - \sin x} + \frac{1}{1 + \sin x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Combine the fractions using the common denominator \((1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x) = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\). The numerator becomes \((1 + \sin x) + (1 - \sin x) = 2\), yielding \(\frac{2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{1}{\sec x - \tan x} - \frac{1}{\sec x + \tan x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Combine over the common denominator \((\sec x - \tan x)(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\). The numerator simplifies to \((\sec x + \tan x) - (\sec x - \tan x) = 2\tan x\), so the result is \(2\tan x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} + \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Write with the common denominator \(\cos x(1 + \sin x)\) to obtain \(\frac{\cos^2 x + (1 + 2\sin x + \sin^2 x)}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}\). Using \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the numerator simplifies to \(2(1 + \sin x)\), reducing the expression to \(\frac{2}{\cos x} = 2\sec x\).

qs.q: Which expression correctly completes the identity \(\sec x - \frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} = \dots\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\sec x\) as \(\frac{1}{\cos x}\) and combine over \(\cos x(1 + \sin x)\) to get \(\frac{1 + \sin x - \cos^2 x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}\). Replace \(1 - \cos^2 x\) with \(\sin^2 x\), factor the numerator as \(\sin x(\sin x + 1)\), and cancel to obtain \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x}{1 - \cot^4 x}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator as \((\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = \sin^2 x - \cos^2 x\), and rewrite the denominator as \(\frac{\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x}{\sin^4 x} = \frac{\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x}{\sin^4 x}\). Dividing the numerator by the denominator yields \(\sin^4 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cot^4 x - 1}{1 - \tan^4 x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator using \(\tan x = \frac{1}{\cot x}\) to get \(1 - \tan^4 x = 1 - \frac{1}{\cot^4 x} = \frac{\cot^4 x - 1}{\cot^4 x}\). Dividing \(\cot^4 x - 1\) by this expression gives \(\cot^4 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos^4 x - \sin^4 x}{\cos x + \sin x}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator as \((\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x)(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x) = (\cos x - \sin x)(\cos x + \sin x)(1)\). Dividing by \((\cos x + \sin x)\) leaves \(\cos x - \sin x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec^4 x - \tan^4 x - 1}{2\sec^2 x}\)
qs.s: Factor \(\sec^4 x - \tan^4 x = (\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x)(\sec^2 x + \tan^2 x) = 1(1 + 2\tan^2 x)\). The numerator is \(1 + 2\tan^2 x - 1 = 2\tan^2 x\), and dividing by \(2\sec^2 x\) simplifies to \(\frac{\tan^2 x}{\sec^2 x} = \sin^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x + 1}{2\cos^2 x}\)
qs.s: Factor \(\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x\) as \((\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = \sin^2 x - \cos^2 x\). The numerator becomes \(\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x + 1 = 2\sin^2 x\), so dividing by \(2\cos^2 x\) gives \(\frac{2\sin^2 x}{2\cos^2 x} = \tan^2 x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos^4 x - \sin^4 x}{1 - \tan^4 x} + \frac{\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x}{1 - \cot^4 x} + 2\sin^2 x \cos^2 x\)
qs.s: The first term simplifies to \(\cos^4 x\) and the second term simplifies to \(\sin^4 x\). The entire expression becomes \(\cos^4 x + 2\sin^2 x \cos^2 x + \sin^4 x = (\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x)^2 = 1\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\sec^4 x (1 - \sin^4 x) - 2\tan^2 x\)
qs.s: Factor \(1 - \sin^4 x = \cos^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x)\), so \(\sec^4 x(1 - \sin^4 x) = \sec^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x) = \sec^2 x + \tan^2 x\). Then, \(\sec^2 x + \tan^2 x - 2\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\sec^2 x \csc^2 x - \frac{\tan^4 x - \cot^4 x}{\tan^2 x - \cot^2 x}\)
qs.s: The fraction simplifies by difference of squares to \(\tan^2 x + \cot^2 x\). Since \(\sec^2 x \csc^2 x = \sec^2 x + \csc^2 x = (1 + \tan^2 x) + (1 + \cot^2 x) = 2 + \tan^2 x + \cot^2 x\), subtracting the fraction gives \(2\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{(\sin x + \cos x)^4 - (\sin x - \cos x)^4}{8\cos x}\)
qs.s: Using difference of squares, \([(\sin x + \cos x)^2 - (\sin x - \cos x)^2][(\sin x + \cos x)^2 + (\sin x - \cos x)^2] = (4\sin x \cos x)(2) = 8\sin x \cos x\). Dividing by \(8\cos x\) gives \(\sin x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos^4 x - \sin^4 x}{\cot^2 x - \tan^2 x}\)
qs.s: The numerator factors to \(\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x\), and the denominator is \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x} - \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{\cos^4 x - \sin^4 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x} = \frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x}\). Dividing the numerator by the denominator leaves \(\sin^2 x \cos^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\csc^4 x - 1}{\cot^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \(\csc^4 x - 1 = (\csc^2 x - 1)(\csc^2 x + 1) = \cot^2 x(\csc^2 x + 1)\). Dividing by \(\cot^2 x\) and substituting \(\csc^2 x = 1 + \cot^2 x\) yields \((1 + \cot^2 x) + 1 = 2 + \cot^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{1 - \cos^4 x}{\sin^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \(1 - \cos^4 x = (1 - \cos^2 x)(1 + \cos^2 x) = \sin^2 x(1 + \cos^2 x)\). Dividing by \(\sin^2 x\) and substituting \(\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x\) gives \(1 + (1 - \sin^2 x) = 2 - \sin^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\tan^4 x - 1}{\sec^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \(\tan^4 x - 1 = (\tan^2 x + 1)(\tan^2 x - 1) = \sec^2 x(\tan^2 x - 1)\). Dividing by \(\sec^2 x\) and replacing \(\tan^2 x\) with \(\sec^2 x - 1\) results in \((\sec^2 x - 1) - 1 = \sec^2 x - 2\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{1 - \sin^4 x}{\cos^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \(1 - \sin^4 x = (1 - \sin^2 x)(1 + \sin^2 x) = \cos^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x)\). Dividing by \(\cos^2 x\) and substituting \(\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x\) gives \(1 + (1 - \cos^2 x) = 2 - \cos^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\cot^4 x - 1}{\csc^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the numerator as a difference of squares: \(\cot^4 x - 1 = (\cot^2 x + 1)(\cot^2 x - 1) = \csc^2 x(\cot^2 x - 1)\). Dividing by \(\csc^2 x\) and replacing \(\cot^2 x\) with \(\csc^2 x - 1\) gives \((\csc^2 x - 1) - 1 = \csc^2 x - 2\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\sec^4 x (1 - \sin^4 x) - 2\tan^2 x\)?
qs.s: Factor \(1 - \sin^4 x = (1 - \sin^2 x)(1 + \sin^2 x) = \cos^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x)\), so \(\sec^4 x(1 - \sin^4 x) = \sec^2 x(1 + \sin^2 x) = \sec^2 x + \tan^2 x\). Subtracting \(2\tan^2 x\) leaves \(\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\sec^4 x - 1}{\tan^2 x} - \frac{\tan^4 x - 1}{\sec^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Simplify each term by factoring differences of squares: \(\frac{\sec^4 x - 1}{\tan^2 x} = \sec^2 x + 1\) and \(\frac{\tan^4 x - 1}{\sec^2 x} = \tan^2 x - 1\). Subtracting the two expressions gives \((\sec^2 x + 1) - (\tan^2 x - 1) = (\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x) + 2 = 1 + 2 = 3\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\cot^4 x + 2\cot^2 x + 1 - \csc^2 x}{\cot^2 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the first three terms as a perfect square: \((\cot^2 x + 1)^2 - \csc^2 x = (\csc^2 x)^2 - \csc^2 x = \csc^2 x(\csc^2 x - 1)\). Since \(\csc^2 x - 1 = \cot^2 x\), dividing by \(\cot^2 x\) leaves \(\csc^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\sec^3 x - \sec^2 x - \sec x + 1}{\tan^4 x}\)?
qs.s: Factor the numerator by grouping: \(\sec^2 x(\sec x - 1) - (\sec x - 1) = (\sec^2 x - 1)(\sec x - 1) = \tan^2 x(\sec x - 1)\). Dividing by \(\tan^4 x\) gives \(\frac{\sec x - 1}{\tan^2 x} = \frac{\sec x - 1}{\sec^2 x - 1} = \frac{1}{\sec x + 1}\).

qs.q: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \(\frac{\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x + 1}{1 - \cos x}\)?
qs.s: Factor \(\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x = (\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x) = \sin^2 x - \cos^2 x\), making the numerator \(\sin^2 x + (1 - \cos^2 x) = 2\sin^2 x\). Then dividing by \(1 - \cos x\) gives \(\frac{2(1 - \cos^2 x)}{1 - \cos x} = 2(1 + \cos x) = 2 + 2\cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1 + \cot x}{\csc x + \sec x}\)
qs.s: Rewriting in terms of sine and cosine gives \(\frac{1 + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}}{\frac{1}{\sin x} + \frac{1}{\cos x}} = \frac{\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x}}{\frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\sin x \cos x}}\). Multiplying by the reciprocal cancels \((\sin x + \cos x)\) and \(\sin x\), leaving \(\cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x + \tan x}{1 + \sec x}\)
qs.s: Factor \(\sin x\) out of the numerator to get \(\sin x\left(1 + \frac{1}{\cos x}\right) = \sin x(1 + \sec x)\). Dividing by the denominator \((1 + \sec x)\) leaves \(\sin x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan x}{\sec x - \cos x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the denominator as \(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \cos x = \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\). Dividing \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) by \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\) results in \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sec x - \csc x}\)
qs.s: The denominator is \(\frac{1}{\cos x} - \frac{1}{\sin x} = \frac{\sin x - \cos x}{\sin x \cos x} = -\frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing \((\cos x - \sin x)\) by this fraction cancels the binomial and gives \(-\sin x \cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec x + \csc x}{\tan x + \cot x}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x \cos x}\) and the denominator as \(\frac{\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Dividing the two fractions yields \(\sin x + \cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \tan x} + \frac{\sin x}{1 - \cot x}\)
qs.s: Writing \(\tan x\) and \(\cot x\) in terms of sine and cosine gives \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x} - \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x}\). Factoring the difference of squares in the numerator and canceling \((\cos x - \sin x)\) leaves \(\sin x + \cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{1}{\sec x - \tan x} - \frac{1}{\sec x + \tan x}\)
qs.s: Find the common denominator \((\sec x - \tan x)(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\). The numerator simplifies to \((\sec x + \tan x) - (\sec x - \tan x) = 2\tan x\), giving \(2\tan x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((\sec x \csc x - \cot x)(\sin x - \csc x)\)
qs.s: The first factor simplifies to \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), and the second factor simplifies to \(\frac{\sin^2 x - 1}{\sin x} = -\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Multiplying them yields \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \left(-\frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\right) = -\cos x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \((1 + \cot x - \csc x)(1 + \tan x + \sec x)\)
qs.s: Expressing both factors with common denominators gives \(\left(\frac{\sin x + \cos x - 1}{\sin x}\right)\left(\frac{\sin x + \cos x + 1}{\cos x}\right) = \frac{(\sin x + \cos x)^2 - 1}{\sin x \cos x}\). Expanding the numerator yields \(\frac{1 + 2\sin x \cos x - 1}{\sin x \cos x} = 2\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x}\)
qs.s: Combine with the common denominator \(\sin x(1 + \cos x)\) to get \(\frac{\sin^2 x + 1 + 2\cos x + \cos^2 x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{2 + 2\cos x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)}\). Factoring the numerator gives \(\frac{2(1 + \cos x)}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\sec x + 1}{\sec x - 1} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\) to get \(\frac{\frac{1}{\cos x} + 1}{\frac{1}{\cos x} - 1}\), then multiply numerator and denominator by \(\cos x\) to obtain \(\frac{1 + \cos x}{1 - \cos x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\tan x - 1}{\tan x + 1} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan x\) as \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) to obtain \(\frac{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} - 1}{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} + 1}\), then multiply numerator and denominator by \(\cos x\) to get \(\frac{\sin x - \cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x - \cos x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Dividing both the numerator and the denominator by \(\sin x\) gives \(\frac{1 + \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}}{1 - \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}} = \frac{1 + \cot x}{1 - \cot x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Dividing both the numerator and the denominator by \(\cos x\) yields \(\frac{\frac{\cos x}{\cos x} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}}{\frac{\cos x}{\cos x} + \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}} = \frac{1 - \tan x}{1 + \tan x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\csc x - 1}{\csc x + 1} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\) into the fraction and multiply both numerator and denominator by \(\sin x\) to simplify to \(\frac{1 - \sin x}{1 + \sin x}\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\sec x - \cos x}{\csc x - \sin x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Express with common denominators: the numerator is \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x} = \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}\) and the denominator is \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\sin x} = \frac{\cos^2 x}{\sin x}\). Dividing the two fractions results in \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin^3 x}{\cos^3 x} = \tan^3 x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \sin x} - \frac{\cos x}{1 + \sin x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Using the common denominator \((1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x) = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\), the numerator becomes \(\cos x(1 + \sin x) - \cos x(1 - \sin x) = 2\sin x\cos x\). Simplifying \(\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos^2 x}\) gives \(\frac{2\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\tan x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cot x - \tan x}{\cot x + \tan x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Rewrite in terms of sine and cosine to get \(\frac{\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}}{\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} + \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}} = \frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}\). Since \(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1\), the expression simplifies directly to \(\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\cos x}{1 - \tan x} + \frac{\sin x}{1 - \cot x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) and \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) to simplify the terms to \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x} - \frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x - \sin x}\). Factoring the numerator as the difference of squares \((\cos x - \sin x)(\cos x + \sin x)\) and canceling yields \(\cos x + \sin x\).

qs.q: Which expression completes the identity \(\frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x} = \text{?}\)
qs.s: Combining with the common denominator \(\sin x(1 + \cos x)\) gives \(\frac{\sin^2 x + (1 + \cos x)^2}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{2 + 2\cos x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)}\). Factoring the numerator to \(2(1 + \cos x)\) and canceling leaves \(\frac{2}{\sin x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\cos x}{\sec x - 1}\)?
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\sec x + 1\) to get \(\frac{\cos x(\sec x + 1)}{\sec^2 x - 1} = \frac{\cos x \sec x + \cos x}{\tan^2 x} = \frac{1 + \cos x}{\tan^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\sin x}{\csc x - 1}\)?
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(\csc x + 1\) to get \(\frac{\sin x(\csc x + 1)}{\csc^2 x - 1} = \frac{\sin x \csc x + \sin x}{\cot^2 x} = \frac{1 + \sin x}{\cot^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\csc x}{1 - \sin x}\)?
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by \(1 + \sin x\) to get \(\frac{\csc x(1 + \sin x)}{(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)} = \frac{\csc x + \csc x \sin x}{1 - \sin^2 x} = \frac{\csc x + 1}{\cos^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\sec x}{1 + \cos x}\)?
qs.s: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(1 - \cos x\) to obtain \(\frac{\sec x(1 - \cos x)}{(1 + \cos x)(1 - \cos x)} = \frac{\sec x - \sec x \cos x}{1 - \cos^2 x} = \frac{\sec x - 1}{\sin^2 x}\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\csc x + \cot x}{\tan x + \sin x}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite using sine and cosine: \(\frac{\frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x}}{\frac{\sin x(1 + \cos x)}{\cos x}} = \frac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x} \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} = \cot x \csc x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\sec x}{1 - \cos x} - \frac{\sec x}{1 + \cos x}\)?
qs.s: Write with the common denominator \((1 - \cos x)(1 + \cos x) = \sin^2 x\) to get \(\frac{\sec x(1 + \cos x) - \sec x(1 - \cos x)}{\sin^2 x} = \frac{(\sec x + 1) - (\sec x - 1)}{\sin^2 x} = \frac{2}{\sin^2 x} = 2\csc^2 x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{\sec x + \csc x}{1 + \tan x}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\cos x \sin x}\) and denominator as \(\frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x}\); dividing them and canceling \((\sin x + \cos x)\) and \(\cos x\) leaves \(\frac{1}{\sin x} = \csc x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{1}{\sec x - \tan x} - \frac{1}{\sec x + \tan x}\)?
qs.s: Combine over the common denominator \((\sec x - \tan x)(\sec x + \tan x) = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1\) to obtain \((\sec x + \tan x) - (\sec x - \tan x) = 2\tan x\).

qs.q: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to \(\frac{1 + \sec x}{\tan x} + \frac{\tan x}{1 + \sec x}\)?
qs.s: Combine over a common denominator: \(\frac{(1 + \sec x)^2 + \tan^2 x}{\tan x(1 + \sec x)} = \frac{1 + 2\sec x + \sec^2 x + (\sec^2 x - 1)}{\tan x(1 + \sec x)} = \frac{2\sec x(1 + \sec x)}{\tan x(1 + \sec x)} = \frac{2\sec x}{\tan x} = 2\csc x\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sec \theta - \sin \theta \tan \theta}{\cos \theta \csc \theta}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \(\frac{1}{\cos \theta} - \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \cos \theta\). The denominator is \(\cos \theta \csc \theta = \cot \theta\), so \(\frac{\cos \theta}{\cot \theta} = \cos \theta \cdot \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} = \sin \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin \theta + \cos \theta \cot \theta}{\tan \theta \csc \theta}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \(\sin \theta + \frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta} = \frac{\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta} = \csc \theta\). The denominator simplifies to \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin \theta} = \sec \theta\), giving \(\frac{\csc \theta}{\sec \theta} = \cot \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos \theta + \sin \theta \tan \theta}{\sin \theta \sec \theta}\)
qs.s: Rewriting the numerator with a common denominator gives \(\frac{\cos^2 \theta + \sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \sec \theta\). The denominator is \(\sin \theta \cdot \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \tan \theta\), so the quotient is \(\frac{\sec \theta}{\tan \theta} = \frac{1/\cos \theta}{\sin \theta / \cos \theta} = \csc \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\csc \theta - \cos \theta \cot \theta}{\sin \theta \sec \theta}\)
qs.s: The numerator simplifies to \(\frac{1}{\sin \theta} - \frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta} = \frac{1 - \cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta} = \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\sin \theta} = \sin \theta\). Dividing by the denominator \(\sin \theta \sec \theta = \tan \theta\) gives \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\tan \theta} = \cos \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos \theta + \sin \theta \tan \theta}{\cot \theta \sec \theta}\)
qs.s: The numerator equals \(\cos \theta + \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \sec \theta\). The denominator is \(\frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} \cdot \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \csc \theta\), so \(\frac{\sec \theta}{\csc \theta} = \frac{1/\cos \theta}{1/\sin \theta} = \tan \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\tan \theta (\cos \theta + \cot \theta)}{\sec \theta + \tan \theta} + \sin \theta \tan \theta\)
qs.s: The fraction's numerator is \(\tan \theta \cos \theta + \tan \theta \cot \theta = \sin \theta + 1\), and its denominator is \(\frac{1 + \sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\), so the fraction simplifies to \(\cos \theta\). Then \(\cos \theta + \sin \theta \tan \theta = \cos \theta + \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \sec \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\sin \theta}{1 + \cos \theta} + \frac{1 + \cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\)
qs.s: Writing with a common denominator produces \(\frac{\sin^2 \theta + (1 + \cos \theta)^2}{\sin \theta(1 + \cos \theta)} = \frac{\sin^2 \theta + 1 + 2\cos \theta + \cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta(1 + \cos \theta)}\). Using \(\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1\), the numerator becomes \(2(1 + \cos \theta)\), which cancels with the denominator to leave \(\frac{2}{\sin \theta} = 2\csc \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cos \theta}{\sec \theta - \tan \theta} - \frac{\cos \theta}{\sec \theta + \tan \theta}\)
qs.s: The common denominator is \((\sec \theta - \tan \theta)(\sec \theta + \tan \theta) = \sec^2 \theta - \tan^2 \theta = 1\). The numerator simplifies to \(\cos \theta(\sec \theta + \tan \theta - \sec \theta + \tan \theta) = 2\cos \theta \tan \theta = 2\sin \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{\cot \theta}{\csc \theta - 1} + \frac{\cot \theta}{\csc \theta + 1}\)
qs.s: Finding a common denominator yields \(\frac{\cot \theta(\csc \theta + 1 + \csc \theta - 1)}{\csc^2 \theta - 1} = \frac{2\cot \theta \csc \theta}{\cot^2 \theta}\). Simplifying gives \(\frac{2\csc \theta}{\cot \theta} = \frac{2/\sin \theta}{\cos \theta / \sin \theta} = 2\sec \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\frac{(\csc \theta \sec \theta - \tan \theta)(\sec \theta - \cos \theta)}{\sin \theta \cot \theta}\)
qs.s: The first factor simplifies to \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 \theta}{\sin \theta \cos \theta} = \cot \theta\), and the second factor simplifies to \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta}\), so their product is \(\sin \theta\). Since the denominator is \(\sin \theta \cot \theta = \cos \theta\), the quotient is \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} = \tan \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\sec \theta - \cos \theta}{\tan \theta}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{1}{\cos \theta} - \cos \theta = \frac{1 - \cos^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta}\). Dividing by \(\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\) cancels common factors, leaving \(\sin \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\cos \theta + \cot \theta}{1 + \sin \theta}\)
qs.s: Factor the numerator as \(\cos \theta\left(1 + \frac{1}{\sin \theta}\right) = \frac{\cos \theta(\sin \theta + 1)}{\sin \theta}\). Dividing by \(1 + \sin \theta\) leaves \(\frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \cot \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\sin \theta + \tan \theta}{1 + \cos \theta}\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(\tan \theta\) as \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\) to express the numerator as \(\frac{\sin \theta(\cos \theta + 1)}{\cos \theta}\). Dividing by \(1 + \cos \theta\) leaves \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} = \tan \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\cos \theta + \cot \theta}{1 + \csc \theta}\)
qs.s: Write \(\cot \theta = \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\) and \(\csc \theta = \frac{1}{\sin \theta}\) to express the fraction as \(\frac{\frac{\cos \theta(\sin \theta + 1)}{\sin \theta}}{\frac{\sin \theta + 1}{\sin \theta}}\). Canceling \(\frac{\sin \theta + 1}{\sin \theta}\) leaves \(\cos \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{1 + \csc \theta}{\cos \theta + \cot \theta}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the terms as fractions with \(\sin \theta\), giving \(\frac{\frac{\sin \theta + 1}{\sin \theta}}{\frac{\cos \theta(\sin \theta + 1)}{\sin \theta}}\). Canceling the common factor \(\frac{\sin \theta + 1}{\sin \theta}\) leaves \(\frac{1}{\cos \theta} = \sec \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\cos \theta}{1 + \sin \theta} + \frac{1 + \sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\)
qs.s: Combine the fractions over the common denominator \(\cos \theta(1 + \sin \theta)\) to get \(\frac{\cos^2 \theta + (1 + \sin \theta)^2}{\cos \theta(1 + \sin \theta)} = \frac{2 + 2\sin \theta}{\cos \theta(1 + \sin \theta)}\). Factoring \(2(1 + \sin \theta)\) and canceling leaves \(\frac{2}{\cos \theta} = 2\sec \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\sin \theta}{1 - \cos \theta} - \cot \theta\)
qs.s: Write \(\cot \theta = \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\) and combine over the common denominator \(\sin \theta(1 - \cos \theta)\) to get \(\frac{\sin^2 \theta - \cos \theta(1 - \cos \theta)}{\sin \theta(1 - \cos \theta)} = \frac{1 - \cos \theta}{\sin \theta(1 - \cos \theta)}\). Canceling \(1 - \cos \theta\) leaves \(\frac{1}{\sin \theta} = \csc \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\sec \theta - \cos \theta}{\csc \theta - \sin \theta}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the numerator as \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta}\) and the denominator as \(\frac{1 - \sin^2 \theta}{\sin \theta} = \frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta}\). Dividing these fractions gives \(\frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\cos \theta} \cdot \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos^2 \theta} = \tan^3 \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \(\frac{\cot \theta(\sin \theta + \tan \theta)}{\csc \theta + \cot \theta}\)
qs.s: Expand the numerator to get \(\cot \theta \sin \theta + \cot \theta \tan \theta = \cos \theta + 1\), and rewrite the denominator as \(\frac{1 + \cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\). Dividing the numerator by the denominator cancels \(1 + \cos \theta\), resulting in \(\sin \theta\).

qs.q: Simplify the expression: \((\sec \theta \csc \theta - \cot \theta)(\sin \theta - \csc \theta)\)
qs.s: Simplify the first factor to \(\frac{1 - \cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta \cos \theta} = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\) and the second factor to \(\frac{\sin^2 \theta - 1}{\sin \theta} = -\frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta}\). Multiplying them yields \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} \left(-\frac{\cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta}\right) = -\cos \theta\).

qs.q: Which expression is identically equal to \(\frac{\cos x}{\sec x - \tan x}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\sec x - \tan x\) as \(\frac{1 - \sin x}{\cos x}\), turning the fraction into \(\frac{\cos^2 x}{1 - \sin x}\). Replacing \(\cos^2 x\) with \(1 - \sin^2 x = (1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)\) allows \((1 - \sin x)\) to cancel, leaving \(1 + \sin x\).

qs.q: Which expression is identically equal to \(\frac{1}{1 - \sin x} + \frac{1}{1 + \sin x}\)?
qs.s: Combine the fractions using the common denominator \((1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x) = 1 - \sin^2 x = \cos^2 x\). The numerator becomes \((1 + \sin x) + (1 - \sin x) = 2\), so the expression simplifies to \(\frac{2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\sec^2 x\).

qs.q: Which expression is identically equal to \(\frac{\csc x}{1 + \cos x}\)?
qs.s: Rewrite \(\csc x\) as \(\frac{1}{\sin x}\) and multiply the numerator and denominator by \((1 - \cos x)\). Since \((1 + \cos x)(1 - \cos x) = \sin^2 x\), the expression becomes \(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\sin^3 x}\).

qs.q: Which expression is identically equal to \(\frac{\sec x}{1 + \sin x}\)?
